candidates.title: [Bug] Gemma-4 mm: single non-RGB image crashes vision tower and kills scheduler (mat1 256 vs 768)
candidates.body:
## Summary

Two stacked bugs make a single non-RGB image (e.g. a grayscale or RGBA JPEG served by an upstream CDN) crash the entire Gemma-4 SGLang scheduler and restart the pod, dropping every unrelated in-flight request in the batch.

- **Bug A (Gemma-4 mm channel guard):** non-RGB images survive the loader path and reach the vision tower with the wrong channel count.
- **Bug B (scheduler blast-radius):** that per-request encoder error escapes the embedding layer, propagates through `run_batch`, and SIGQUITs the scheduler subprocess. **Bug B is the higher-impact half.** A single bad image takes ~24 unrelated users with it.

I have a draft fix PR up (will link after submission) that ships Bug A fully and ships a partial Bug B (pod survives, but the batch is still aborted as a whole). True per-request isolation is sketched at the bottom of this issue.

## Crash signature

```
RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (2520x256 and 768x1152)
  File "python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_vision.py", line 435, in _patch_projection
    return self.input_proj(patches.to(self.input_proj.weight.dtype))
  File "python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_vision.py", line 579, in forward
    inputs_embeds = self.patch_embedder(...)
  File "python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_mm.py", line 434, in get_image_feature
    pooled, pooler_mask = vt(pv, pp)
  File "python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_utils.py", line 703, in _get_chunked_prefill_embedding
    all_miss_embedding = data_embedding_func(all_miss_items)
  <- embed_mm_inputs <- general_mm_embed_routine <- Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration.forward
  <- scheduler.py run_batch -> forward_batch_generation
-> TP0+TP1 both die -> SIGQUIT -> pod restart, drops ~20-24 unrelated in-flight requests
```

## Decisive root-cause math

- `768 = 16 * 16 * 3` = `Gemma4VisionPatchEmbedder.input_proj.in_features` (3-channel RGB patch flattened, `patch_size=16`).
- `256 = 16 * 16 * 1` = grayscale (single-channel) patch flattened.

A 1-channel image survives `PIL.Image.open` (mode `L`) and `torchvision.io.decode_jpeg` on GPU (which returns a `(1, H, W)` tensor preserving the source channel count), patchifies as `(N, 256)`, and crashes the `Linear(768, 1152)` projection.

## Why it slips through today

`base_processor.BaseMultimodalProcessor._load_single_item` already has an RGB-normalization step that is gated on `discard_alpha_channel=True`:

```python
if (
    discard_alpha_channel
    and not isinstance(img, torch.Tensor)
    and img.mode != "RGB"
):
    img = img.convert("RGB")
```

But the `not isinstance(img, torch.Tensor)` guard means the GPU-decode path (`gpu_image_decode=True`, which Gemma-4 inherits as the default) skips normalization entirely. nvJPEG returns a `(C, H, W)` tensor preserving the source channel count, so a grayscale JPEG keeps `C=1` all the way to the patch embedder.

## Production impact

- 14+ pod restarts in 3 hours across 8 pods on 2 clusters.
- Each restart drops ~20-24 unrelated in-flight requests (the running batch).
- Single customer-traffic trigger (ads-media CDN serving occasional grayscale JPEGs that survive PIL load).
- Reproduced on `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1-cu126` with `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-Dynamic` on 2xH200, TP=2 (Triton attention backend, auto-selected).


## Minimal repro

Untested against a live server (I do not have a free GPU to spin one up on this exact rev), but the trigger is straightforward:

```python
import base64
import io
import requests
from PIL import Image

# 1-channel grayscale JPEG that survives PIL load but patchifies wrong.
buf = io.BytesIO()
Image.new("L", (224, 224), color=128).save(buf, format="JPEG")
b64 = base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode()

# POST to a Gemma-4 SGLang server with OpenAI-style chat completions:
resp = requests.post(
    "http://localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions",
    json={
        "model": "gemma-4-31b",
        "messages": [{
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {"type": "text", "text": "Describe."},
                {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {
                    "url": f"data:image/jpeg;base64,{b64}",
                }},
            ],
        }],
        "max_tokens": 1,
    },
    timeout=30,
)
# Expected today: scheduler pod restarts, this request fails along with every
# other request in the same forward batch.
# Expected after Fix A+B: this request fails cleanly with a 400-class error,
# the pod stays up, other requests in the batch complete normally
# (Fix B v2 sketch below) or are aborted with an attributable error
# (Fix B v1 in the draft PR).
```

You can also force the path by handing the server a `.png` saved with `Image.new("RGBA", ...)` or `Image.new("L", ...)` directly; the JPEG path above is what we see in production.

## Search for existing fixes

I searched the repo and the open PR list and did not find anything that already addresses either half:

- The crash site (`gemma4_vision.py::_patch_projection`) is unchanged since the original Gemma-4 PR #21952.
- The Gemma-4 roadmap #26596 does not list either fix.
- Adjacent open Gemma-4 mm PRs that **do not** fix this:
  - #26606 (perf batching for ViT calls across images in one batch) — touches the same neighborhood but is a perf change, not a robustness fix.
  - #26320 (HF prompt token regex) — unrelated to image preprocessing.

Apologies if I missed an in-flight fix; happy to rebase / close the PR.

## Proposed fix (draft PR linked above)

**Fix A (ships in the draft PR):** in `base_processor._load_single_item`, when `discard_alpha_channel=True` and the loaded image is a `torch.Tensor`, normalize the channel dim by expanding `C=1` and `C=2` to 3 channels and dropping the alpha for `C=4`. Mirrors the existing PIL `.convert(\"RGB\")` path. Also adds a defensive `ValueError` in `Gemma4VisionPatchEmbedder._patch_projection` that surfaces a clear typed error instead of a cryptic mat-mul shape mismatch.

**Fix B v1 (ships in the draft PR):** wrap the per-modality encoder call in `embed_mm_inputs` and re-raise `RuntimeError` as a new typed `MultimodalEmbeddingError`. The scheduler event loops catch this typed error around `run_batch`, mark every request in the failing batch as `FINISH_ABORT` with `err_type=\"MultimodalEmbeddingError\"`, and continue the loop. The pod stays up.

This is a half-fix for the blast-radius issue: it limits the damage from \"pod-wide\" to \"batch-wide\". Unrelated requests in the same batch are still aborted, but with a clean per-request error response instead of a connection drop, and subsequent batches are served normally.

**Fix B v2 (sketch, not in this PR — wants maintainer review):** true per-request isolation. When the batched encoder call raises, retry items one at a time to identify the failing item index, map that back to its request via `items_size` (the per-request cumulative bounds already maintained in `embed_mm_inputs`), abort only that request, and re-run the encoder on the surviving items for the rest of the batch. Sketch:

```python
# inside embed_mm_inputs, replacing the simple try/except above

try:
    embedding, mask, input_ids = get_embedding_and_mask(...)
except RuntimeError as batch_err:
    # Identify the failing item by retrying one at a time.
    bad_item_indices = []
    surviving = []
    surviving_size = [0]
    for i, item in enumerate(items):
        try:
            _ = get_embedding_and_mask(
                data_embedding_func=embedder,
                embedding_items=[item],
                placeholder_tensor=placeholder_tensor[i : i + 1],
                input_ids=input_ids,
                items_size=[0, 1],
                # NOTE: per-request prefix/extend slices need plumbing here
                prefix_length=[prefix_for(item)],
                extend_length=[extend_for(item)],
                items_offset_list=[items_offsets_for(item)],
            )
            surviving.append(item)
            surviving_size.append(surviving_size[-1] + 1)
        except RuntimeError as item_err:
            req_idx = _item_index_to_request_index(i, items_size)
            bad_item_indices.append((i, req_idx, item_err))

    # Abort exactly the failing requests
    raise MultimodalEmbeddingError(
        modality=modality,
        failing_item_indices=bad_item_indices,
        original_batch_error=batch_err,
    )
    # Caller (scheduler) sets FINISH_ABORT only on the failing rids,
    # then re-runs embed_mm_inputs on the surviving items.
```

The hard parts I would want maintainer input on before implementing:
1. The `_item_index_to_request_index` mapping is straightforward (`items_size` is already cumulative).
2. Re-running the encoder on the surviving items inside the same forward is the part that needs care: the caller (`run_batch`) builds a `ForwardBatch` once before `general_mm_embed_routine` is called, so swapping out the request set mid-forward is non-trivial. The cleaner path may be to abort the failing requests, mark the whole batch as needing a re-schedule, and let the next iteration of the event loop pick up the surviving requests.

## Sign-off

Reported by Parasail (parasail.io). Reproduced in production on `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1-cu126` running `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-Dynamic`, 2xH200, TP=2 (Triton attention backend, auto-selected).

candidates.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4 DSpark TP=8 can permanently stall under HiCache long-prefix load
candidates.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Full environment information and a minimal reproducer are included.
- [x] This is a bug report, not a general question.
- [x] This report is in English.

The positive recurrence was observed on July 24 using source revision `50d1edaa7f` (July 14). Here “latest” means a recent affected build, not the repository’s rapidly moving instantaneous HEAD. The tested hardware, software versions, launch command, and concrete reproducer are included below.

## Describe the bug

DeepSeek-V4 DSpark with TP=8 can enter a permanent scheduler stall under HiCache long-prefix load. The process remains alive, but prefill/decode progress stops, fresh tiny requests also stop completing, and service returns only after the worker is restarted.

Relevant configuration:

- `flashinfer_mxfp4`
- decode CUDA graphs
- HiCache `write_through` with the kernel I/O backend
- 32K chunked prefill
- mixed cold, overlapping, cached-prefix, and fixed-decode traffic

One natural run stopped after about 68 minutes. A bounded workload reproduced the same persistent behavior within its third block.

This is not yet a root-cause claim. In an earlier sample, seven TP ranks were inside `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe_op` while one rank had advanced, followed by an NCCL timeout. The wedge later recurred despite both TP verification-outcome synchronization and a guard disabling PDL in eager MXFP4 MoE while retaining graph PDL. Those mitigations therefore do not establish a sufficient fix.

**Expected behavior:** all TP ranks continue making progress, or the server fails fast with a useful rank/collective diagnostic instead of remaining alive in a permanent stall.

## Concrete reproducer (verified on 8xB200)

This is a concrete reproducer, not a speculative stress pattern. The `test_function()` below uses the same profile order and byte-identical corpus generator as the bounded workload that produced this measured transition:

1. The server was initially healthy.
2. Two complete workload blocks returned 54/54 semantic responses; their two 254,953-token HiCache seeds also completed.
3. In block 2, after the cold-128K and 8-way overlapping-32K profiles completed, the next 254,953-token HiCache seed stopped after exactly two 32,768-token prefill chunks, with 189,417 tokens pending.
4. That request timed out after 62.057 seconds.
5. Two independent rounds of four fresh tiny probes all timed out after 62.115–62.136 seconds.
6. The process stayed alive with zero restarts and accepted new ingress, but produced no later scheduler batch before watchdog recovery.

A failed long request alone is not accepted as a wedge. The function returns `True` only after two all-failing rounds of fresh tiny probes.

Important interpretation: exit 1 means only that this timing-sensitive wedge was not observed in that bounded run. It does **not** demonstrate that the bug is fixed.

### Server

The exact positive configuration used a very large host HiCache allocation. `--mem-fraction-static 0.82 --hicache-ratio 14` requires roughly a 4 TiB host; it can OOM during startup on a 2 TiB host.

```bash
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7

sglang serve \
  --model-path /models/DeepSeek-V4-DSpark \
  --served-model-name dspark-model \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000 \
  --tp 8 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --context-length 262144 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.82 \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \
  --max-running-requests 32 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \
  --stream-interval 10 \
  --grammar-backend xgrammar \
  --disable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --watchdog-timeout 3600 \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \
  --enable-hierarchical-cache \
  --hicache-ratio 14 \
  --hicache-write-policy write_through \
  --hicache-io-backend kernel \
  --hicache-mem-layout page_first \
  --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \
  --enable-cache-report \
  --enable-metrics
```

### Client

<details>
<summary>repro_dspark_hicache_wedge.py</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Concrete bounded reproducer for a persistent SGLang DSpark/HiCache wedge.

This uses the exact profile order and byte-identical corpus generator from the
verified transition on an 8xB200 server: two complete 27-request blocks
remained healthy; during block 2 a 254,953-token HiCache-reuse seed stalled;
then two rounds of four fresh tiny probes all failed.

Exit 0 means that persistent signature was reproduced. Exit 1 means only that
this timing-sensitive bug was not observed during this bounded run; it does
not demonstrate that the bug is fixed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import concurrent.futures
import os
import time
from collections import Counter

import requests


BASE_URL = os.environ.get("BASE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1")
MODEL = os.environ.get("MODEL", "dspark-model")
REQUEST_TIMEOUT = int(os.environ.get("REQUEST_TIMEOUT", "75"))
BLOCKS = int(os.environ.get("BLOCKS", "12"))
PROFILES = (
    "cold_8k_c1",
    "cold_32k_c1",
    "cold_128k_c1",
    "overlap_32k_c8",
    "hicache_reuse_128k_c8",
    "decode_256_c8",
)


def make_document(namespace: str, nominal_tokens: int, suffix: str = "") -> str:
    """Build the calibrated corpus; response usage is the token authority."""

    repeats = nominal_tokens // 12 + 1
    body = " ".join(
        (
            f"perf{namespace} part{index} the quick brown fox jumps over "
            "the lazy dog beside the wide river"
        )
        for index in range(repeats)
    )
    return body + suffix


def request(prompt: str, *, max_tokens: int, ignore_eos: bool = False) -> dict:
    started = time.monotonic()
    try:
        payload = {
            "model": MODEL,
            "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
            "max_tokens": max_tokens,
            "temperature": 0,
        }
        if ignore_eos:
            payload["ignore_eos"] = True
        response = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/chat/completions",
            json=payload,
            timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT,
        )
        data = response.json()
        choices = data.get("choices") or []
        message = choices[0].get("message", {}) if choices else {}
        semantic_success = bool(
            response.status_code == 200
            and choices
            and (
                str(message.get("content") or "").strip()
                or str(message.get("reasoning_content") or "").strip()
            )
        )
        return {
            "status": response.status_code,
            "semantic_success": semantic_success,
            "seconds": round(time.monotonic() - started, 3),
            "usage": data.get("usage") or {},
        }
    except Exception as exc:
        return {
            "status": "EXCEPTION",
            "semantic_success": False,
            "seconds": round(time.monotonic() - started, 3),
            "error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
        }


def run_parallel(
    prompts: list[str],
    *,
    concurrency: int,
    max_tokens: int,
    ignore_eos: bool = False,
) -> list[dict]:
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=concurrency) as pool:
        return list(
            pool.map(
                lambda prompt: request(
                    prompt,
                    max_tokens=max_tokens,
                    ignore_eos=ignore_eos,
                ),
                prompts,
            )
        )


def summary(results: list[dict]) -> dict:
    return {
        "semantic_successes": sum(
            result["semantic_success"] for result in results
        ),
        "statuses": dict(Counter(str(result["status"]) for result in results)),
        "prompt_tokens": sum(
            int((result.get("usage") or {}).get("prompt_tokens") or 0)
            for result in results
        ),
        "seconds_max": max(result["seconds"] for result in results),
    }


def persistent_after_failure(run_id: str, candidate: str) -> bool:
    """Require two independent all-failing rounds of fresh tiny probes."""

    for probe_round in range(2):
        prompts = [
            (
                f"fresh wedge probe {run_id}-{candidate}-{probe_round}-"
                f"{time.time_ns()}-{probe}"
            )
            for probe in range(4)
        ]
        results = run_parallel(prompts, concurrency=4, max_tokens=8)
        print(
            {
                "event": "tiny_probe_round",
                "candidate": candidate,
                "round": probe_round,
                **summary(results),
            },
            flush=True,
        )
        if any(result["semantic_success"] for result in results):
            return False
        if probe_round == 0:
            time.sleep(5)
    return True


def run_profile(run_id: str, profile: str, block: int) -> list[dict]:
    namespace = f"{run_id}-b{block}-{profile}"
    if profile == "cold_8k_c1":
        prompts = [make_document(namespace, 5_300, "\nAnswer OK.")]
        concurrency, max_tokens = 1, 16
    elif profile == "cold_32k_c1":
        prompts = [make_document(namespace, 21_300, "\nAnswer OK.")]
        concurrency, max_tokens = 1, 16
    elif profile == "cold_128k_c1":
        prompts = [make_document(namespace, 85_300, "\nAnswer OK.")]
        concurrency, max_tokens = 1, 16
    elif profile == "overlap_32k_c8":
        prompts = [
            make_document(
                f"{namespace}-request-{index}",
                21_300,
                "\nAnswer OK.",
            )
            for index in range(8)
        ]
        concurrency, max_tokens = 8, 16
    elif profile == "hicache_reuse_128k_c8":
        shared = make_document(namespace, 85_300)
        seed = request(
            shared + "\nSeed this prefix and answer OK.",
            max_tokens=16,
            ignore_eos=True,
        )
        print(
            {
                "event": "hicache_seed",
                "block": block,
                **summary([seed]),
            },
            flush=True,
        )
        if not seed["semantic_success"]:
            return [seed]
        prompts = [
            shared + f"\nReuse query {index}: answer with the number {index}."
            for index in range(8)
        ]
        concurrency, max_tokens = 8, 16
    elif profile == "decode_256_c8":
        prompts = [
            f"Fixed decode benchmark block {block}, lane {index}. Count upward forever."
            for index in range(8)
        ]
        concurrency, max_tokens = 8, 256
    else:
        raise ValueError(profile)

    return run_parallel(
        prompts,
        concurrency=concurrency,
        max_tokens=max_tokens,
        ignore_eos=True,
    )


def test_function() -> bool:
    """Return True only for healthy -> persistent-wedge behavior."""

    run_id = str(time.time_ns())
    smoke = request(f"fresh smoke {run_id}", max_tokens=8)
    if not smoke["semantic_success"]:
        raise RuntimeError("server was not healthy before the test")

    warmup = request(
        "Warm the fixed decode graph. Count upward forever.",
        max_tokens=256,
        ignore_eos=True,
    )
    if not warmup["semantic_success"]:
        raise RuntimeError("decode warmup failed before the test")

    completed_semantic = 2
    for block in range(BLOCKS):
        offset = block % len(PROFILES)
        order = PROFILES[offset:] + PROFILES[:offset]
        for profile in order:
            candidate = f"block={block},profile={profile}"
            results = run_profile(run_id, profile, block)
            profile_summary = summary(results)
            completed_semantic += profile_summary["semantic_successes"]
            print(
                {
                    "event": "profile_complete",
                    "block": block,
                    "profile": profile,
                    "completed_semantic": completed_semantic,
                    **profile_summary,
                },
                flush=True,
            )
            if all(result["semantic_success"] for result in results):
                continue
            if persistent_after_failure(run_id, candidate):
                print(
                    {
                        "event": "persistent_wedge_reproduced",
                        "candidate": candidate,
                        "completed_semantic": completed_semantic,
                    },
                    flush=True,
                )
                return True
            print(
                {
                    "event": "rejected_failure",
                    "candidate": candidate,
                    "reason": "fresh tiny traffic remained live",
                },
                flush=True,
            )

    print(
        (
            "no persistent wedge observed in this bounded run; "
            "this does not demonstrate that the bug is fixed"
        ),
        flush=True,
    )
    return False


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(0 if test_function() else 1)
```

</details>

Run against a fresh server:

```bash
python repro_dspark_hicache_wedge.py

# exit 0: concrete persistent-wedge signature reproduced
# exit 1: not observed in this bounded run; this does not prove a fix
```

The calibrated HiCache seed measured 254,953 prompt tokens with the affected DeepSeek-V4 tokenizer. Check `usage.prompt_tokens` if using a different tokenizer; the request plus output must remain below the 262,144-token context limit.

## Environment

```text
Hardware: single node, 8 x NVIDIA B200, TP=8, approximately 4 TiB host RAM
SGLang upstream source base: 50d1edaa7fcff16b49d2d9797599a4015a1926c3
Python: 3.12.3
CUDA: 12.9
PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu129
sglang-kernel: 0.4.4+cu129
flashinfer-python: 0.6.14
Triton: 3.6.0
Transformers: 5.12.1
```

The positive predicate is timing-sensitive. A bounded no-wedge result on a newer revision would not, by itself, prove the issue fixed.

candidates.title: [Bug] Kimi-K3 DSPARK: Xid 13 (CTA Not Present) crash at ~218k token context on B300
candidates.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Serving Kimi-K3 on a B300 1×8 (single node, 8 GPUs) with DSPARK speculative decoding + overlap scheduler + HiCache, the scheduler crashes with `cudaErrorLaunchFailure` (Xid 13: "Graphics SM Cga Exception — CTA Not Present") when a single request's decode context reaches ~219k tokens. The crash is reproducible across restarts and hits different GPU ranks (TP6 first, then another GPU after restart), confirming a kernel-level bug rather than a hardware fault.

**Trigger condition**: Single request, decode phase, context grows to ~218k–219k tokens. No OOM — KV usage 36%, mamba usage 3% at crash time.

**Crash signature**: `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure` surfaced at `result.copy_done.synchronize()` inside `advance_grammar_fsm` (grammar barrier on the overlap-scheduler path). CUDA notes the error is asynchronous, so the stacktrace points to the sync site, not the faulting kernel.

**dmesg Xid 13** (two separate crashes on two different GPUs):

```
[Thu Jul 30 09:31:13 2026] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:1a:00): 13, Graphics SM Cga Exception on (GPC 1, TPC 3, SM 1): CTA Not Present
[Thu Jul 30 09:31:13 2026] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:1a:00): 13, pid=1118758, name=python3, Graphics Exception: channel 0x0000000f, Class 0000cdc0, Offset 00000000, Data 00000000

[Thu Jul 30 09:58:55 2026] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:df:00): 13, Graphics SM Cga Exception on (GPC 1, TPC 4, SM 1): CTA Not Present
[Thu Jul 30 09:58:55 2026] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:df:00): 13, pid=1339292, name=python3, Graphics Exception: channel 0x00000002, Class 0000cdc0, Offset 00000000, Data 00000000
```

**No ECC errors**: `nvidia-smi -q` shows no retired pages, no ECC error counts, no channel/TPC repair pending — hardware excluded.

**Analysis**: The crash occurs on the DSPARK overlap-scheduler path at the grammar barrier sync point:

```
scheduler.event_loop_overlap
  → run_batch
    → dspark_worker_v2._forward_decode
      → grammar_barrier()
        → _advance_pending_grammar
          → advance_grammar_fsm
            → result.copy_done.synchronize()   ← CUDA error surfaces here (async)
```

Since CUDA reports the error asynchronously, `copy_done.synchronize()` is the sync point where the error is caught, not the actual faulting kernel. The Xid 13 "CTA Not Present" exception indicates a kernel launched with an invalid CTA-to-SM mapping — most likely a grid dimension calculation that overflows at ~219k token context length.

**Candidate kernels** (any of the three running in the decode forward at this context length):
1. `trtllm_mla` decode/verify kernel (24 MLA layers, reads ~219k × 576B × 24 ≈ 3 GB KV per step)
2. Triton KDA decode kernel (69 KDA layers)
3. `nv_cutedsl` spec-verify kernel (DSPARK target verify, 8 positions per step)

**Scheduler decode log immediately before crash**:

```
[2026-07-30 01:58:52 TP0] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 218880, full token usage: 0.36, mamba num: 4, mamba usage: 0.03, accept len: 1.23, accept rate: 0.03, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 59.73, #queue-req: 0, est. decode TFLOPS/s (per GPU): 11.78, est. read BW (GB/s per GPU): 11777.03, est. write BW (GB/s per GPU): 1.34
[2026-07-30 01:58:52 TP0] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 218944, full token usage: 0.36, mamba num: 4, mamba usage: 0.03, accept len: 1.02, accept rate: 0.00, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 49.86, #queue-req: 0, est. decode TFLOPS/s (per GPU): 10.39, est. read BW (GB/s per GPU): 10391.14, est. write BW (GB/s per GPU): 1.12
[2026-07-30 01:58:53 TP0] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 219008, full token usage: 0.36, mamba num: 4, mamba usage: 0.03, accept len: 1.38, accept rate: 0.05, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 66.87, #queue-req: 0, est. decode TFLOPS/s (per GPU): 12.77, est. read BW (GB/s per GPU): 12768.20, est. write BW (GB/s per GPU): 1.50
```

**Crash stacktrace**:

```
[2026-07-30 01:58:54 TP6] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 4735, in run_scheduler_process
    scheduler.run_event_loop()
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 1540, in run_event_loop
    dispatch_event_loop(self)
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 4586, in dispatch_event_loop
    scheduler.event_loop_overlap()
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/torch/utils/_contextlib.py", line 124, in decorate_context
    return func(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 1641, in event_loop_overlap
    batch_result = self.run_batch(batch)
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/utils/nvtx_utils.py", line 109, in wrapper
    return func(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 3416, in run_batch
    batch_result = self.model_worker.forward_batch_generation(
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py", line 396, in forward_batch_generation
    return self._forward_decode(batch, on_publish, grammar_barrier)
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py", line 645, in _forward_decode
    grammar_barrier()
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 1713, in _advance_pending_grammar
    self.batch_result_processor.advance_grammar_fsm(prev_result, prev_batch)
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py", line 674, in advance_grammar_fsm
    result.copy_done.synchronize()
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/torch/cuda/streams.py", line 254, in synchronize
    super().synchronize()
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure
CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call, so the stacktrace below might be incorrect.
For debugging consider passing CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1

terminate called after throwing an instance of 'c10::AcceleratorError'
[2026-07-30 01:58:54] SIGQUIT received. signum=None, frame=None. It usually means one child failed.
  what():  CUDA error: unspecified launch failure

Exception raised from currentStreamCaptureStatusMayInitCtx at /pytorch/c10/cuda/CUDAGraphsC10Utils.h:71 (most recent call first):
  frame #0: c10::Error::Error(...) + 0x9d
  frame #4: c10::TensorImpl::~TensorImpl() + 0x9
  frame #7: sglang::scheduler_TP6() [0x59edb3]
  ...
Fatal Python error: Aborted
```

**Note on recovery**: The crash does not produce a clean exit code — it is not restarted by Docker Compose's restart policy. Instead, SGLang's internal crash handler (`SIGQUIT` → `kill_process_tree` → process teardown) brings down the scheduler process and SGLang re-initializes the model from within the container, causing a full model reload (~minutes of downtime) rather than a fast container-level restart.

### Reproduction

1. Launch Kimi-K3 with the command below (no `--context-length` limit):

```bash
docker run --gpus all --shm-size 4tb \
  -e SGLANG_DG_CACHE_DIR=/root/.cache/deep_gemm \
  -e SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_FAST_WARMUP=true \
  -e TRITON_CACHE_DIR=/root/.triton/cache \
  -e TVM_FFI_CACHE_DIR=/root/.cache/tvm-ffi \
  -e TILELANG_CACHE_DIR=/root/.tilelang/cache \
  lmsysorg/sglang:kimi-k3 \
  --model-path moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 \
  --tp 8 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
  --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 \
  --mamba-full-memory-ratio 0.45 \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \
  --speculative-draft-model-path RadixArk/Kimi-K3-DSpark \
  --speculative-dspark-block-size 7 \
  --enable-linear-replayssm-spec \
  --enable-hierarchical-cache \
  --enable-metrics \
  --enable-mfu-metrics
```

2. Send a single chat request with a long prompt (~150k+ tokens) and let it decode until the total context exceeds ~218k tokens.
3. Observe the crash in the scheduler log and Xid 13 in `dmesg`.

### Environment

```text
Model: moonshotai/Kimi-K3 (2.8T, hybrid KDA + MLA, 93 layers)
Docker image: lmsysorg/sglang:kimi-k3 (CUDA 13)
sglang version: 0.5.16
Hardware: B300 1×8 (SM103, Blackwell), 288 GB/GPU, 4 TiB host RAM
GPU driver: 580.159.04 (NVIDIA UNIX Open Kernel Module)
Topology: Single node, TP=8, NVLink intra-node (no MNNVL)

Environment variables:
  SGLANG_DG_CACHE_DIR=/root/.cache/deep_gemm
  SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_FAST_WARMUP=true
  TRITON_CACHE_DIR=/root/.triton/cache
  TVM_FFI_CACHE_DIR=/root/.cache/tvm-ffi
  TILELANG_CACHE_DIR=/root/.tilelang/cache

dmesg (Xid 13, two crashes on two different GPUs):
  [Thu Jul 30 09:31:13 2026] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:1a:00): 13, Graphics SM Cga Exception on (GPC 1, TPC 3, SM 1): CTA Not Present
  [Thu Jul 30 09:58:55 2026] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:df:00): 13, Graphics SM Cga Exception on (GPC 1, TPC 4, SM 1): CTA Not Present

nvidia-smi ECC: No retired pages, no ECC error counts, no channel/TPC repair pending — hardware excluded.
```

candidates.title: DeepEP CUDA illegal memory access in NIXL transfer_worker during disaggregated prefill
candidates.body:
## Summary
Prefill worker 1 (node inkwell-copper-cn03) crashes with `CUDA error /build/DeepEP/csrc/deep_ep.cpp:278 'an illegal memory access was encountered'` during disaggregated prefill warmup phase, causing job failure.

## Error
```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'EPException'
  what():  Failed: CUDA error /build/DeepEP/csrc/deep_ep.cpp:278 'an illegal memory access was encountered'
```

Stack trace shows the error originates from:
- `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/nixl/conn.py:697` in `transfer_worker`
- Multiple threads affected: `transfer_worker`, `bootstrap_thread`, watchdog threads

## Repro Context
- **Model**: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1 (DeepSeek-V3)
- **Precision**: FP8 (e4m3)
- **Topology**: 2 prefill nodes (TP=8, EP=8, DP=8) + 8 decode nodes (TP=32, EP=32, DP=32)
- **Disaggregation mode**: prefill with `--disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl --moe-a2a-backend deepep`
- **Job ID**: 5114 (dsr1-fp8-1k1k-max-tpt-26861695033)
- **Container**: lmsysorg_sglang_dev-cu13_20260603.sqsh

## Timeline
1. Workers start at 04:26:12
2. Model weights loaded by 04:38:27
3. NIXL initialized at 04:38:30, DeepGEMM warmup begins
4. Watchdog timeout at 04:38:24 (300s)
5. DeepEP crash at 04:39:46, scheduler subprocess exited with code -3

## Suspect Commits
Recent changes to NIXL code may have introduced instability:
- [c3aaafc5](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/c3aaafc5f26e0fc0b11a89339ee78bf0676f992c): "[Bugfix] Clean up failed NIXL sender state" — directly modifies `nixl/conn.py`
- [6c69756f](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/6c69756f): "NIXL: use prep+make API to improve performance" — significant refactor of transfer_worker

## Log Location
Full log: `inkwell-copper-cn03_prefill_w1.out`

## Suggested Fix
1. Add memory validation before DeepEP operations to catch illegal memory accesses earlier
2. Review recent changes to `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/nixl/conn.py` for race conditions
3. Consider adding debug logging to identify which specific tensor shape triggers the illegal memory access

candidates.title: [Question] Does SGLang GLM-5 support NVIDIA SM120 GPUs?
candidates.body:
Hi SGLang team,

  I am trying to run `nvidia/GLM-5.1-NVFP4` with SGLang on an 8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 node. These GPUs compute capability are SM120.

  Environment:

  - GPU: 8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, SM120
  - Driver: 595.58.03
  - Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12-cu130`
  - Model: `nvidia/GLM-5.1-NVFP4`
  - Model architecture: `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`
  - Quantization: `modelopt_fp4`
  - Attention backend: DSA (NSA alias)
  - KV cache tested: `bf16` and `fp8_e4m3`

  I tested several DSA (NSA) backend combinations:

  - `flashmla_sparse`
  - `flashmla_kv`
  - `flashmla_auto`
  - `fa3`
  - `tilelang`
  - `aiter`
  - `trtllm`

  All of them fail during server startup before `/health` becomes ready. The common error is:

  ```text
  RuntimeError: Assertion error (/deepgemm/csrc/apis/attention.hpp:219): Unsupported architecture
  ```
  From the stack trace, the failure happens in DSA metadata initialization:
  ```
  sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa_backend.py
    init_forward_metadata
      deep_gemm.get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata(...)
  ```
  I also checked the code and it looks like `deep_gemm.get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata`, `fp8_mqa_logits`, and
  `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` only dispatch for `arch_major == 9` or `arch_major == 10`, while SM120 reports
  `arch_major == 12`.

  So my questions are:

  1. Is GLM-5.1 NVFP4 with DSA currently expected to work on SM120 GPUs?
  2. If not, is SM120 support for the DeepGEMM DSA/indexer path planned?
  3. Is there any recommended workaround, image, branch, or backend setting for running GLM-5.1 on
     RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell / SM120?

  Thanks!

candidates.title: [Bug] GLM-5-FP8 two-host PD with mooncake wedges decode/detokenizer; NIXL contrast passes
candidates.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version/image available to us.
- [x] I included environment info and a minimal reproducible setup.
- [x] This is a bug report, not a general question.
- [x] This issue is written in English.

### Describe the bug

We are seeing a reproducible decode/detokenizer wedge when serving GLM-5-FP8 with two-host formal PD and the `mooncake` transfer backend.

The services start normally. The decode worker also passes its internal disaggregation warmup request. However, the first real request sent through the SGLang router times out. After that, decode `/health` starts timing out and the router reports that no decode worker is available.

The main contrast is that switching only the PD transfer backend from `mooncake` to `nixl` avoids the issue in the same tiny readiness test.

I am not claiming that the root cause is proven to be inside mooncake. The current evidence points to the mooncake backend path, or its interaction with GLM-5-FP8 + two-host formal PD + EAGLE runtime.

### Environment

- SGLang image: `lmsysorg/sglang:latest`
- SGLang version from image metadata: `v0.5.12`
- Model: `GLM-5-FP8`
- Hardware: 2 hosts, each with 8x H200
- Topology:
  - prefill host: SGLang server, TP=8, port 30000, bootstrap port 8998
  - decode host: SGLang server, TP=8, port 30001
  - router host: SGLang router, port 8000
- PD transfer backend tested: `mooncake` and `nixl`
- Speculative decoding: EAGLE enabled on decode
- `--skip-server-warmup`: not used
- `--disable-cuda-graph`: not used

### Minimal reproduction setup

Prefill server:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /model \
  --served-model-name /local/GLM-5-FP8 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000 \
  --tp-size 8 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --enable-metrics \
  --export-metrics-to-file \
  --export-metrics-to-file-dir /metrics/request \
  --disaggregation-mode prefill \
  --disaggregation-transfer-backend <mooncake|nixl> \
  --disaggregation-bootstrap-port 8998 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85
```

Decode server:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /model \
  --served-model-name /local/GLM-5-FP8 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30001 \
  --tp-size 8 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --enable-metrics \
  --export-metrics-to-file \
  --export-metrics-to-file-dir /metrics/request \
  --disaggregation-mode decode \
  --disaggregation-transfer-backend <mooncake|nixl> \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4
```

For the attention-mode variant, add this to the decode command:

```bash
--speculative-attention-mode decode
```

Router:

```bash
python -m sglang_router.launch_router \
  --pd-disaggregation \
  --prefill http://<prefill-host>:30000 8998 \
  --decode http://<decode-host>:30001 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000
```

Test request:

```bash
curl --max-time 180 http://127.0.0.1:8000/generate \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"text":"hello","sampling_params":{"max_new_tokens":8,"temperature":0},"stream":false}'
```

### Observed behavior with mooncake

Startup looks healthy before the first real router request:

- prefill / decode / router containers start successfully
- decode internal disaggregation warmup `/generate` returns 200 OK
- `/v1/models`, `/metrics`, and initial `/health` look normal
- router loads the tokenizer

After the first router-native `/generate` request:

- client request times out
- decode `/health` starts timing out
- decode log repeatedly shows:

```text
Health check failed. Server couldn't get a response from detokenizer for last 20 seconds
```

- router later reports:

```text
No available decode workers (all circuits open or unhealthy)
```

In an earlier no-spec diagnostic run, the request had already entered `scheduler.cur_batch` and had `output_ids`, so this does not look like the request never reached decode.

### NIXL contrast

With the same model, image, topology, TP size, EAGLE parameters, and request payload, changing only the transfer backend to `nixl` passes the tiny readiness test.

Results:

| backend | `--speculative-attention-mode decode` | actual attention mode | `/generate` result | chat completion result | decode `/health` | result |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| mooncake | no | `prefill` | first real router request hangs; later requests unusable | unusable | timeout | FAIL |
| mooncake | yes | `decode` | first real router request hangs; later requests unusable | unusable | timeout | FAIL |
| nixl | no | `prefill` | 3/3 succeeded | 2/2 succeeded | OK after each request | PASS |
| nixl | yes | `decode` | 3/3 succeeded | 2/2 succeeded | OK after each request | PASS |

The NIXL runs show:

```text
NIXL KVManager initialized with backend: UCX
```

and do not show the detokenizer health failure or router `No available decode workers` error.

### Control variables

The result does not appear to depend on `--speculative-attention-mode decode`:

- mooncake fails with and without it
- NIXL passes with and without it

The NIXL passing runs also did not use:

- `--skip-server-warmup`
- `--disable-cuda-graph`

The logs show:

```text
skip_server_warmup=False
disable_cuda_graph=False
```

### Expected behavior

The mooncake PD backend should either serve the first router request successfully, like the NIXL backend does in the same tiny test, or fail with a clear error instead of wedging decode/detokenizer and making the decode worker unhealthy.

### Related issues / PRs

This looks related, but not identical, to:

- #22511: GLM-5 multi-node deployment reports detokenizer health failure
- #21837: PD separation + mooncake transfer can make D node unhealthy after abort request
- #20756: disagg health / idle false-positive fix

The additional signal in this report is the controlled mooncake-vs-NIXL contrast under the same GLM-5-FP8 two-host formal PD setup.

### Notes

This is a tiny readiness reproduction, not a long-running load test. It is enough to show that the failure follows the mooncake backend path in this setup, but it does not prove the exact root cause.

candidates.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4-Pro，PD Disaggregation Input Length Hard-Capped at 18,432 Tokens Due to Incorrect SWA Limit Enforcement on Prefill Node
candidates.body:
### Checklist

### Describe the bug

In the PD-disaggregated deployment using the `ds-v4-hopper` image with the `deepseek-v4-pro` model and SGLang's official FP8 configuration, the following code path is triggered:

```python
if self.scheduler.tp_worker.is_hybrid_swa:
    # FIXME: current SWA allocation allocate full kv cache size in prefill
    self.max_total_num_tokens = min(
        self.max_total_num_tokens,
        self.scheduler.tp_worker.model_runner.swa_max_total_num_tokens,
    )

[2026-05-06 09:15:41 DP7 TP7 EP7] DSv4 memory calculation: bytes_per_full_token=23749.84, available_bytes=4.13 GB, full_token=186368
[2026-05-06 09:15:41 DP7 TP7 EP7] DSv4 pool sizes: full=186368, swa=18432, c4=46592, c128=1456, c4_state=1152, c128_state=18432
[2026-05-06 09:15:41 DP6 TP6 EP6] Memory profiling: available_gpu_memory=17.94 GB, total_gpu_memory=138.17 GB, mem_fraction_static=0.90, rest_memory=4.13 GB
[2026-05-06 09:15:41 DP6 TP6 EP6] DSv4 memory calculation: bytes_per_full_token=23749.84, available_bytes=4.13 GB, full_token=186368
[2026-05-06 09:15:41 DP5 TP5 EP5] Memory profiling: available_gpu_memory=17.94 GB, total_gpu_memory=138.17 GB, mem_fraction_static=0.90, rest_memory=4.13 GB
[2026-05-06 09:15:41 DP6 TP6 EP6] DSv4 pool sizes: full=186368, swa=18432, c4=46592, c128=1456, c4_state=1152, c128_state=18432
[2026-05-06 09:15:41 DP5 TP5 EP5] DSv4 memory calculation: bytes_per_full_token=23749.84, available_bytes=4.13 GB, full_token=186368


 python3 -c "
import json
text = ('hell word。' + '\n') * 4800
payload = {
    'model': '/data/models/DeepSeek-V4-Pro',
    'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': text}],
    'max_tokens': 400,
    'temperature': 0.7
}
with open('/tmp/80k_req.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(payload, f)
print('chars:', len(text), 'estimated tokens:', int(len(text) * 84006 / 136000))
" && curl -s http://172.16.0.8:8889/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @/tmp/80k_req.json
chars: 163200 estimated tokens: 100807
{"error":{"type":"Bad Request","code":"decode_bad_request","message":"Request 212ff413b9d844ed9d944c70e9ab6c1e exceeds the maximum number of tokens: 100804 > 18432"}}
```

Because the prefill node operates under `is_hybrid_swa = true`, its effective token capacity is clamped to `swa_max_total_num_tokens` (18,432) instead of the full KV-cache budget (186,368). The FIXME comment explicitly notes that the current SWA allocator reserves the **full KV cache size** during prefill, yet the runtime still enforces the SWA upper bound on `max_total_num_tokens`. This is why the prefill node rejects any request exceeding 18,432 tokens, even though the hardware has sufficient HBM for the full 186k context window. @fzyzcjy @boxiaowave 

### Reproduction

The deployment runs on H200 GPUs, using the deepseek-v4-hopper container image and the deepseek-v4-fp8 model, following the PD disaggregation commands from the official documentation.

### Environment

GPU：H200
models：DeepSeek-V4-Pro

candidates.title: [Bug] [AMD] Qwen3.5 GatedDeltaNet + dp-attention on ROCm/MoRI: HIP "invalid configuration argument" (linear-attn/Mamba state path); process hangs in chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd under kernel serialization
candidates.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Enabling **`--enable-dp-attention`** for **Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8** (a GatedDeltaNet hybrid MoE model) in PD-disaggregation with `--moe-a2a-backend mori` on **MI355X/ROCm** fails: the model loads, but the scheduler aborts during warmup / first batch with a HIP `invalid configuration argument`, in the GatedDeltaNet / Mamba (linear-attention) state path.

This is the **root blocker** for Qwen3.5 dp-attention on ROCm. It is reached only after working around two earlier, separate bugs so the model can load and start capturing:

- the fused-MoE shared-expert slot assertion on MoRI (companion report / bug #1), and
- the `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_with_gate` zero-grid HIP abort (companion report / bug #2).

With `dp-attention` **off**, the same model + MoRI disagg runs correctly (GSM8K passes), so this is specific to `dp-attention`. DeepSeek-R1 (MLA, **no** GatedDeltaNet) runs fine with `dp-attention` + MoRI disagg — the differentiator is Qwen3.5's GatedDeltaNet linear-attention / Mamba-state path.

### The HIP error has two async manifestations (red herrings)

Because HIP reports kernel errors asynchronously, the Python traceback surfaces at whatever Mamba-pool op runs next. We observed two, depending on which rank/stage hit it first:

**(A) Prefill — Mamba allocator:**

```
File ".../srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 2883, in _get_new_batch_prefill_raw
    mamba_allocator.alloc_group_end()
File ".../srt/mem_cache/allocator/mamba.py", line 64, in alloc_group_end
    self.free(torch.cat(remaining))
torch.AcceleratorError: HIP error: invalid configuration argument
```

**(B) Decode — hybrid req-to-token pool:**

```
File ".../srt/disaggregation/decode.py", line 1963, in process_decode_queue
    req_conns, _ = self.disagg_decode_prealloc_queue.pop_preallocated()
File ".../srt/disaggregation/decode.py", line 1293, in _pre_alloc
    req_pool_indices = self.req_to_token_pool.alloc([req])
File ".../srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py", line 780, in alloc
    mamba_index_tensor = torch.stack(mamba_indices).to(dtype=torch.int32)
torch.AcceleratorError: HIP error: invalid configuration argument
```

### Localization: the fault is the GatedDeltaNet chunk kernel

Re-running with kernel serialization (`AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3` and `HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`) changes the failure from an async crash to a **synchronous hang**, which pinpoints the offending kernel. In that run the servers came up and the last scheduler activity before the detokenizer heartbeat froze (permanently) during warmup was autotuning the GatedDeltaNet linear-attention chunk kernel:

```
Autotuning kernel chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kkt_solve_kernel with config BK: 32, num_warps: 1, ...
Autotuning kernel chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kkt_solve_kernel with config BK: 64, num_warps: 4, ...
# ... heartbeat then freezes; no further progress; all requests fail ...
```

So the `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_*` Triton kernel(s) (the GatedDeltaNet linear-attention chunk-scan) are launched with a configuration HIP rejects (zero/invalid grid or block dims) under `dp-attention`'s data-parallel token sharding (`--dp-size 8`, idle/uneven per-rank batches). The Mamba-pool `torch.cat`/`torch.stack(...).to(int32)` aborts in (A)/(B) are the asynchronous surfacing of the same fault.

### Why we can't just switch kernels

sglang's alternate linear-attention backends (`--linear-attn-backend {triton,cutedsl,flashinfer}`) are CUDA/SM100-only (`cutedsl`, `flashinfer` are gated behind `is_cuda()`/`is_sm100_supported()`), so **`triton` is the only linear-attn backend available on ROCm/MI355X** — there is no config-level workaround.

### Reproduction

Prerequisites: apply the bug #1 and bug #2 workarounds so the model loads and reaches warmup. Then launch Qwen3.5 with dp-attention + MoRI on 2 MI355X nodes (1 prefill + 1 decode):

```
# prefill (node 0) and decode (node 1), TP=8 each, dp-attention on
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 --trust-remote-code \
  --disaggregation-mode {prefill|decode} \
  --tp-size 8 --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head \
  --moe-a2a-backend mori --disaggregation-transfer-backend mori \
  --attention-backend aiter --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --chunked-prefill-size 65536
```

Send one request through the PD router; the scheduler aborts (or, with `AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3 HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, hangs in `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_*`).

### Environment

- Container: `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.14-rocm720-mi35x`
- sglang: 0.5.14
- GPU: AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) x8, 1 prefill + 1 decode node
- ROCm: 7.2 (roctracer / hip runtime 7.2)
- Model: Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 (GatedDeltaNet hybrid MoE)
- Attention backend: aiter; linear-attn backend: triton (only option on ROCm);
  MoE a2a backend + disaggregation transfer backend: mori

### Notes

- Works: `dp-attention` **off** (Qwen3.5 MoRI disagg), and `dp-attention` **on**
  for DeepSeek-R1 (MLA, no GatedDeltaNet) — isolating the GatedDeltaNet + dp-attn
  combination on ROCm as the cause.
- Likely part of the broader ROCm-MoRI hybrid-model enablement tracked in #21886.
- Ask: does the GatedDeltaNet linear-attn (`chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd`) path and
  the hybrid Mamba req-to-token pool support `dp-attention` token sharding on
  ROCm/HIP, or is a guard needed for empty/uneven per-DP-rank batches?

candidates.title: [Bug] [AMD] Qwen3.5 + dp-attention: fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_with_gate Triton kernel aborts with HIP "invalid configuration argument" (zero-sized grid on empty/idle-rank batch)
candidates.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Running **Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8** with **`--enable-dp-attention`** on MI355X/ROCm, the Qwen3.5 fused QK-RMSNorm+gate Triton kernel (`fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_with_gate` in `python/sglang/srt/models/utils.py`) aborts with a HIP `invalid configuration argument` and a GPU coredump. It fires during CUDA-graph capture and/or the first decode/prefill forward passes.

(This is reached after working around the separate MoRI shared-expert assertion so the model can load — see companion report. In the same run, other Qwen3.5 kernels on the GatedDeltaNet path also abort with the same HIP error; that is tracked separately.)

```
[DPx TPx EPx] Scheduler hit an exception / GPU coredump / Fatal Python error: Aborted

Thread (most recent call first):
  File ".../triton/backends/amd/compiler.py", line 468 in make_amdgcn
  File ".../triton/compiler/compiler.py", line 327 in compile
  File ".../triton/runtime/jit.py", line 739 in run
  File ".../srt/models/utils.py", line 696 in fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_with_gate
  File ".../srt/models/qwen3_5.py", line 914 in forward_prepare_hip
  File ".../srt/models/qwen3_5.py", line 962 in self_attention
  File ".../srt/models/qwen3_5.py", line 1013 in forward
  ...
torch.AcceleratorError: HIP error: invalid configuration argument
Search for `hipErrorInvalidConfiguration' ...
```

### Root cause

Under data-parallel attention, CUDA-graph capture (and runtime) can hand **idle DP ranks a zero-token batch** (`seq_len == 0`). In `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_with_gate`:

```python
seq_len = q_gate.shape[0]
...
q_rows = seq_len * num_heads          # == 0 for an empty batch
...
_fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_gate_kernel[(q_rows,)](...)   # launched with grid = (0,)
```

Launching a Triton kernel with a **zero-sized grid `(0,)`** raises `hipErrorInvalidConfiguration` on ROCm/HIP (CUDA tolerates a 0-grid launch as a no-op; HIP aborts). The sibling `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm` (non-gate, same file) launches the same `[(q_rows,)]` grid and has the identical hazard.

### Proposed fix

Guard the launch: when `q_rows == 0`, skip the kernel and return the already-correctly-shaped empty output tensors. Apply to **both** `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_with_gate` and `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm`:

```python
q_out = torch.empty(q_rows, head_dim, dtype=..., device=...)
k_out = torch.empty(k_rows, head_dim, dtype=..., device=...)
gate_out = torch.empty(q_rows, head_dim, dtype=..., device=...)  # gate variant only
if q_rows == 0:
    return q_out, k_out, gate_out      # (q_out, k_out) for the non-gate variant
# ... launch kernel ...
```

More generally, any Triton launch of the form `kernel[(n,)](...)` in the model forward should be guarded against `n == 0` for HIP robustness.

2. Launch Qwen3.5 with dp-attention on ROCm:

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tp-size 8 --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head \
  --moe-a2a-backend mori --attention-backend aiter \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3
```

### Checklist

- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.

### Describe the bug

Running **Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8** in **PD-disaggregation (1 prefill + 1 decode node)** with **MoRI EP all-to-all** and **`--enable-dp-attention`** (TP8/EP8/DP8) on MI355X/ROCm, both prefill and decode servers now start cleanly and reach `Application startup complete`, but the benchmark completes **0 successful requests**. On first traffic, every decode DP rank fails to reach the prefill **disaggregation bootstrap server** (`--disaggregation-bootstrap-port`, default `8998`):

```
Error querying dp_ranks from bootstrap: HTTPConnectionPool(host='172.18.170.23', port=8998):
Max retries exceeded with url: /query_dp_ranks
(Caused by NewConnectionError("HTTPConnection(host='172.18.170.23', port=8998):
Failed to establish a new connection: [Errno 99] Cannot assign requested address"))
```

The message repeats **~1.36 million times in a single run** — a `/query_dp_ranks` connect/retry storm that exhausts client ephemeral ports (`[Errno 99]`), so the prefill↔decode KV-transfer handshake never establishes and no request completes. `benchmark_serving` reports `Successful requests: 0` with all throughput/latency metrics `0.00`.

(This is reached after applying the model-init/kernel fixes so the servers can load and serve — see "Applied fixes" below. It is a separate layer — the disaggregation bootstrap/handshake — from the shared-expert-fusion assertion (#31793), the idle-rank zero-grid HIP abort (#31794/#31350), and the decode CUDA-graph/MoRI routing (#32039), all of which are resolved here.)

### Root cause (suspected)

Under dp-attention with per-rank EP (MoRI), each of the 8 decode DP ranks issues `GET http://<prefill>:8998/query_dp_ranks` to resolve DP-rank info for the KV-transfer handshake. The query appears to be issued **per-DP-rank without connection pooling / backoff / caching**, so on a topology where the connection cannot be immediately established, the ranks spin in a tight connect-retry loop and exhaust local ephemeral ports (`[Errno 99] Cannot assign requested address`) rather than backing off or querying once per node. The result is a request-serving deadlock: servers are up and healthy, but the disaggregation handshake never completes.

### Proposed fix

- Add connection pooling + bounded retry/backoff to the decode-side `/query_dp_ranks` bootstrap query (reuse a session; cap retries; exponential backoff) so a transiently-unreachable bootstrap does not turn into a millions-of-connections ephemeral-port storm.
- Consider querying the bootstrap **once per node** (or caching the DP-rank map) instead of once per DP rank per request under dp-attention + MoRI.
- Surface a single clear error (bootstrap unreachable at `host:8998`) instead of an unbounded retry loop.

### Applied fixes (source overlays; required just to reach this point)

The tested image predates the fixes, so these merged/open PRs were applied by bind-mounting patched source files (read-only) over the image's originals under `/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/...`:

- **#31793** — disable Qwen global-slot shared-expert fusion under per-rank EP backends. File: `srt/models/qwen2_moe.py`.
- **#31794** (fixes #31350) — idle-DP-rank zero-grid guards + MoRI EP routing. Files: `srt/models/qwen2_moe.py`, `srt/models/utils.py`, `srt/layers/sampler.py`, `srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py`, `jit_kernel/triton/gdn_fused_proj.py`.
- **#32039** — MoRI expert routing, decode CUDA-graph disable under MoRI normal mode, AITER buffer capacity. Files: `srt/models/qwen2_moe.py`, `srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py`, `srt/server_args.py`.

With all three applied, init is clean (shared-expert fusion auto-disabled at `moe_ep_size=8`; no `invalid configuration argument`; decode CUDA graph auto-disabled for MoRI normal mode; both servers load 94/94 shards and reach `Application startup complete`). The bug in this report is what remains after that.

### Reproduction

1. Apply #31793 + #31794 + #32039 to `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.14-rocm720-mi35x-20260706` (source overlays as above).
2. Launch PD-disaggregation on two MI355X nodes (1 prefill + 1 decode), TP8/EP8/DP8, dp-attention on, MoRI transfer/EP backend:

**Prefill:**
```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
  --disaggregation-mode prefill --disaggregation-ib-device ionic_0,...,ionic_7 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --trust-remote-code \
  --tp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --dp-size 8 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --attention-backend aiter \
  --disaggregation-transfer-backend mori --moe-dense-tp-size 1 --moe-a2a-backend mori \
  --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --max-running-requests 256 --chunked-prefill-size 65536 \
  --cuda-graph-bs 1 2 3 --disable-radix-cache
```

**Decode:**
```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
  --disaggregation-mode decode --disaggregation-ib-device ionic_0,...,ionic_7 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --trust-remote-code \
```

candidates.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

DeepSeek V4 models can fail to start or fail on the first decode when loaded with `--load-format runai_streamer`.

The DeepSeek V4 loader currently materializes the `weights` iterable with `list(weights)` before checking for `.wo_a.scale` tensors and calling `_dequant_fp8_wo_a`. That is fine for normal local safetensors loading, but it is unsafe for streaming loaders because the iterator is the loading boundary. The non-streaming path also assumes all `.wo_a.weight` and `.wo_a.scale` tensors are available together before model loading continues.

With RunAI Model Streamer, the model can load all tensors but later fail during the first decode/warmup with CUTLASS grouped GEMM initialization errors. Switching to local loading does not reproduce the issue.

The loader should keep the weight-loading path streaming-safe and pair `.wo_a.weight` / `.wo_a.scale` tensors as they arrive, without converting the whole weight iterator to a list. If a streamed tensor must be retained until its matching pair arrives, it should be cloned only when it is marked as a RunAI Model Streamer tensor.

### Reproduction

Serve a DeepSeek V4 model with RunAI Model Streamer:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path <DeepSeek-V4-model> \
  --load-format runai_streamer \
  --tp-size 4
```

Then issue a minimal completion request:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"DeepSeek-V4-Flash","prompt":"Hello","max_tokens":1,"temperature":0}'
```

```text
tvm.error.InternalError: [Mixed dtype WS grouped GEMM] Failed to initialize cutlass mixed dtype WS grouped gemm. Error: Error Internal
Error: Failed to initialize the TMA descriptor 700
```

A local/non-streaming load of the same model does not reproduce the failure.

candidates.title: [PP + HiCache] HiCache Consistency Fix Plan
candidates.body: # PP HiCache Consistency for Disaggregated Prefill — PR Plan ## Background ### Motivation In agentic and long-context reasoning scenarios, requests frequently share long prefixes (system prompts, tool definitions, multi-turn history) that can span tens of thousands of tokens. Recomputing these shared prefixes for every request is prohibitively expensive. SGLang's **HiCache** addresses this with a 3-level KV cache hierarchy — **L1** (GPU device memory) → **L2** (CPU host memory) → **L3** (external distributed storage, e.g. Mooncake) — enabling prefix reuse across requests and even across restarts via persistent storage. Meanwhile, large models (e.g. DeepSeek-V3 with 60 layers) require **Pipeline Parallelism (PP)** to split layers across multiple GPU groups, combined with **disaggregated prefill** where prefill and decode run on separate server pools. This PP + HiCache + disaggregated prefill stack is critical for production agentic workloads: it maximizes both throughput (via disaggregation) and cache hit rates (via L3 persistence) on large models. However, combining PP with L3 storage introduces a class of consistency bugs that do not exist in simpler configurations. Understanding why requires examining the cache hierarchy level by level. ### Why L3 Storage Breaks PP Consistency In PP mode, each rank runs an independent scheduler with its own radix tree. The key question is: why does adding L3 cause divergence when L1 and L2 alone do not? **L1-only + PP (no HiCache)**: Both ranks receive the same requests in the same order via P2P. `match_prefix` operates on the device radix tree, which is fully deterministic — insert and evict are driven by the same batch picks, and all operations are synchronous within each scheduler cycle. **No divergence possible.** **L1 + L2 + PP (HiCache without storage)**: Adding the host cache introduces `write-through` (GPU→CPU backup) and `load-back` (CPU→GPU restore). These are still **synchronous** operations within each cycle — `writing_check()` and `loading_check()` are called at deterministic points in the event loop, and the host tree mutations they produce are driven by the same batch sequence. ~~**No divergence possible.**~~ There is a small probability of matched_host mismatch!!! **L1 + L2 + L3 + PP (HiCache with storage)**: Adding L3 storage introduces the **prefetch thread** — an asynchronous background thread that queries external storage independently on each rank. This is where consistency breaks: 1. **Async completion timing**: PP0 and PP1's prefetch threads may complete at different wall-clock times. When PP0's prefetch finishes first, it inserts nodes into its host tree immediately, while PP1's tree has not yet been updated. The next `match_prefix` on each rank sees different host tree states → different `host_hit_length` → different `prefix_indices`. 2. **Anchor divergence**: The L3 query uses a hash chain starting from an anchor node in the host tree. If PP0 has already inserted nodes from a previous prefetch (giving it `host_hit=896`), its anchor and token range differ from PP1's (which has `host_hit=0`). The two ranks compute **completely different hash chains** for the same request → fetch different (or wrong) data from storage. 3. **Eviction divergence from wall-clock LRU**: Even after fixing async finalization (making PP1 event-driven), the eviction layer itself can diverge. LRU eviction uses `last_access_time = time.monotonic()`, which differs by microseconds between ranks → different victim node selection → different GPU→CPU demotion → different host memory pressure → different `evictable_host_leaves` candidate sets. In production (PP2 + NSA + disagg prefill), this caused: PP0 finalized a prefetch → inserted host node → immediately triggered `evict_host` (memory pressure) → evicted the node. PP1 replayed the same finalize event one cycle later → inserted the node → no eviction pressure → node remained. Result: PP0 `matched_host=0`, PP1 `matched_host=17664` → shape mismatch crash. 4. **Amplification cascade**: Once the host tree diverges (even by one node), all subsequent operations compound the difference — different eviction decisions, different write-through timing, different prefetch anchors for the next request — until a shape mismatch crash occurs. In essence: **L1 and L2 operations are synchronous and deterministic within each cycle, but L3 prefetch is asynchronous and state-dependent. The async completion timing, state-dependent query parameters, and wall-clock-dependent eviction ordering create a feedback loop where small divergences amplify into crashes.** ## Solution Architecture thanks @stepinto ### Three Communication Channels (Three Edge Types) ① PG1 — green bidirectional (between prefetch_thread) - Uses prefetch_sync_groups, gloo (CPU) backend, members = TP+CP+PP - Handles `#1` : global MIN over storage_hit_count - Bidirectional arrow = a truly symmetric all_reduce; all ranks participate equally and obtain the same hit count ② PG2 — purple bidirectional (between prefetch_sync_thread) - Uses prefetch_sync_groups2, also gloo, members = TP+CP+PP - Handles `#2`: global MIN over completed_tokens - Likewise a symmetric all_reduce ③ Scheduler-thread _all_reduce — directional (between Scheduler loops, PP0→PP1→PP2) - Handles `#3`/ `#4`/ `#5`/ `#6` (terminate MAX, qsize MIN, finish MIN) - Different mechanism: first reduces within the local stage's TP/CP group via GLOO, then uses _pp_sync point-to-point to overwrite downstream ranks with PP0's result - Directional arrow = not a symmetric reduce, but PP0 single-point decision + downstream broadcast ### Why Split It This Finely (Key Design Intent) 1. PG1 and PG2 have identical members, yet two sets are created — because `#1` and `#2` run on two different background threads. The same gloo communicator cannot be used for concurrent all_reduce from two threads (it would corrupt/deadlock), so each gets its own set. 2. Background uses gloo, while the scheduler-thread set mixes NCCL+P2P — gloo is CPU communication, isolated from the scheduler thread's CUDA collectives, preventing background all_reduce from blocking GPU computation. 3. The two categories have different semantics: - ①② are symmetric global MIN — pulling each rank's progress into alignment (whoever is slowest wins) - ③ is PP0 directional broadcast — termination timing / drain counts decided uniformly by the leader ## Work In Progress - [X] need cp sync https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20460 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27285 FIx L2 - [ ] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27010 Fix L3 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29106 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25887 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29258 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/30476 - [ ] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28379 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31869 Special thanks to @ShangmingCai @hzh0425 for their guidance on the HiCache architecture, PP synchronization design, and code review throughout this effort. candidates.title: [Bug] [PD][NIXL] Qwen3.5 TP1-attention prefill -> TP4 decode fails in prepXferDlist with NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND
candidates.body:
[by Codex]

### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution for this bootstrap-time failure.
- [x] The bug persists in a 2026-07-13 SGLang nightly (`g22c08a9be`).
- [x] Environment information and a minimal topology/config reproduction are included below.
- [x] This is a bug report rather than a general question.
- [x] This report is in English.

### Describe the bug

Qwen3.5-397B FP8 PD disaggregation with NIXL fails on the first request when
the prefill side has effective attention TP=1 and the decode side has
attention TP=4.

The observed configuration was:

| Side | SGLang parallelism | Effective attention ownership |
|---|---|---|
| Prefill | TP4, DP4, `--enable-dp-attention` | attention TP1 |
| Decode | TP4, DP1, DP attention disabled | attention TP4 |

There were two prefill workers and two decode workers, with four GPUs per
worker. All workers became healthy and each rank successfully initialized the
NIXL UCX backend. The first endpoint-verification request then failed in the
prefill bootstrap thread before any benchmark request completed:

```text
E0713 23:29:03.494601 nixl_agent.cpp:631] prepXferDlist: failed to prepare
the descriptors for any of the specified or potential backends for agent ''

Exception in thread Thread-7 (bootstrap_thread):
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../sglang/srt/disaggregation/nixl/conn.py", line 2356, in bootstrap_thread
    self._add_remote_peer(...)
  File ".../sglang/srt/disaggregation/nixl/conn.py", line 1294, in _add_remote_peer
    self._prepare_payload_xfer(decode_kv_args)
  File ".../sglang/srt/disaggregation/nixl/conn.py", line 990, in _prepare_payload_xfer
    self._init_hetero_tp_prep_handle(...)
  File ".../sglang/srt/disaggregation/nixl/conn.py", line 810, in _init_hetero_tp_prep_handle
    src_handle = self.agent.prep_xfer_dlist("", src_array, src_mem_kind)
  File ".../nixl_cu13/_api.py", line 513, in prep_xfer_dlist
    handle = self.agent.prepXferDlist(descs, handle_list)
nixl_cu13._bindings.nixlNotFoundError: NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND
```

The empty agent name in `prep_xfer_dlist("", ...)` is the local source dlist,
so this is not a missing remote worker or UCX initialization failure. NIXL
cannot prepare the sliced local VRAM descriptors generated for the
heterogeneous attention-TP layout.

The same model/container/transport works when prefill and decode have matching
effective attention ownership (for example, DP-attention prefill to
DP-attention decode). Pure TP decode is nevertheless an important low-TPOT
configuration, so mixed DEP/TP prefill/decode combinations should work rather
than forcing the same effective attention TP on both sides.

This is related to, but observably distinct from:

- #23746 / #23744: TP1 -> TP4 Qwen3.5 GQA/Mamba correctness bugs. In this
  reproduction, NIXL fails while preparing descriptors before any KV or Mamba
  state transfer occurs.
- #22145 and #22240: earlier heterogeneous NIXL KV/Mamba transfer support.
- #22536: NIXL heterogeneous-TP staging support. This reproduction uses the
  default direct path (`SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_BUFFER` is not enabled).

One possible connection to #23744 is that Qwen3.5 has two KV heads while the
decode attention TP is four. The direct NIXL path may be constructing source
dlist groups for replicated decode ranks that do not map to valid registered
source regions. This is only a hypothesis; the confirmed failure is the local
source `prep_xfer_dlist` call above.

Expected behavior: the request completes correctly for prefill attention TP1
to decode attention TP4. The same should extend to TP8 decode on an eight-GPU
node.

Actual behavior: the prefill bootstrap thread exits with
`NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND`, the request hangs, and zero requests complete.

### Reproduction

Use two B200 nodes (or otherwise place prefill and decode on separate hosts)
with NIXL/UCX connectivity. Launch one or more workers with the following
relevant arguments. The failure occurs during the first request, so a
high-concurrency benchmark is not required.

Prefill (effective attention TP1):

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
  --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 \
  --disaggregation-mode prefill \
  --disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl \
  --disaggregation-bootstrap-port 7200 \
  --tp-size 4 --dp-size 4 \
  --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head \
  --attention-backend trtllm_mha \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \
  --moe-dense-tp-size 1 \
  --quantization fp8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --mamba-scheduler-strategy no_buffer \
  --mamba-track-interval 2048 \
  --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --disable-cuda-graph \
  --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \
  --max-prefill-tokens 8192 \
  --max-running-requests 16 \
  --context-length 9280 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.7 \
  --trust-remote-code
```

Decode (attention TP4):

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
  --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30001 \
  --disaggregation-mode decode \
  --disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl \
  --tp-size 4 --dp-size 1 \
  --attention-backend trtllm_mha \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \
  --moe-dense-tp-size 1 \
  --quantization fp8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --mamba-scheduler-strategy no_buffer \
  --mamba-track-interval 2048 \
  --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --chunked-prefill-size 64 \
  --max-prefill-tokens 16384 \
  --max-running-requests 512 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs 512 \
  --context-length 9280 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.915 \
  --trust-remote-code
```

Start the PD router with the prefill bootstrap port explicitly supplied:

```bash
python3 -m sglang_router.launch_router \
  --pd-disaggregation \
  --prefill http://<prefill-host>:30000 7200 \
  --decode http://<decode-host>:30001 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```

Then send any request, for example:

```bash
curl http://<router-host>:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}],"max_tokens":16}'
```

If multiple prefill workers are used, pass each worker's bootstrap port
explicitly to the router. The observed failure is not the missing-bootstrap-
port problem discussed in #18414.
