candidates.title: [RFC] Porting ReplaySSM to SGLang: faster decode and speculative decoding for hybrid (GDN/KDA) models
candidates.body:
## Summary

[ReplaySSM](https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/) (Dao AI Lab, 2026) is a technique that makes the **recurrent decode step of linear-attention / SSM layers faster** by turning a *read + write* of the full recurrent state every step into a *read-only* step plus a periodic *flush*. The recurrent update is linear, so the state can be reconstructed on demand from a checkpoint plus a tiny ring buffer of the last `L` steps' `(d, k, g)` records — and the output can be read out **without ever materializing the full state matrix** on non-flush steps.

This is a **bandwidth** optimization for a **memory-bound** kernel: GDN decode at batch ≥ 64 runs at 70–79% of peak HBM bandwidth, so halving per-step state traffic translates almost directly into speedup.

This RFC tracks porting ReplaySSM to SGLang in two independently-shippable parts:

| Part | Scope | Resource won | Status |
|------|-------|--------------|--------|
| **A** | Buffered output-only GDN **decode** kernel + integration | HBM **bandwidth** → decode speedup | **Implemented** — [#28451](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28451) |
| **B** | ReplaySSM **spec-decode** verify (chunked, ring across verify steps) | bandwidth at high batch | **Implemented** — [#28695](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28695) |
| (rel.) |  Compact linear spec cache | spec-decode **memory footprint** | **In review** — [#27658](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27658) |

Upstream reference: vLLM ReplaySSM (commit `3c85112`), files `fused_recurrent_replayssm.py` (decode) and `gdn_replayssm_spec_decode.py` (spec).

> **Figure credit.** All figures below are reproduced from the [Dao AI Lab ReplaySSM blog](https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/) for illustration. Credit to the original authors; see the blog for full context, methodology, and additional results.

---

## Background & motivation

### The problem

GDN (Gated DeltaNet, the Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next lineage) and KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) decode maintain a fixed-size recurrent state `S` of shape `[HV, V, K]` per slot per layer (~1 MB in bf16 for `HV=32, K=V=128`). The standard packed decode kernel reads `S` from HBM, applies a rank-1 update, and writes `S` back **every** decode step — roughly `2 * |S|` of state traffic per step (read + write).

This kernel is **memory-bound** at serving batch sizes. Measured on H20-3e (peak copy bandwidth ~3.8 TB/s):

| batch | achieved HBM bandwidth |
|-------|------------------------|
| 1     | 2% (launch/latency bound) |
| 16    | 29% |
| 64    | **70%** |
| 256   | **79%** |

When a kernel is this bandwidth-bound, **reducing bytes moved per step ≈ reducing runtime**.

![Latency breakdown showing the SSM decode step is dominated by state memory traffic](https://dao-lab.ai/assets/img/2026-06-15-replayssm/motivation-latencybreakdown.png)

*Latency breakdown (Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4, batch 256, single B300) — the recurrent state traffic dominates the step. From the [Dao AI Lab ReplaySSM blog](https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/).*

### The idea

Keep the last flushed state `S0` (the **checkpoint**) frozen, and a small per-slot **ring buffer** of the last `L` steps' `(d, k, g)`. On a non-flush step, append the new `(d, k, g)` and reconstruct the readout from `S0` + the ring. Only every `L` steps **flush**: fold the ring into `S0` and write the full state back.

`S0` is still **read** every step, but the full-state **write** is amortized from every step to every `L` steps. Per-step state traffic drops from read+write (`~2|S|`) to read-only (`~|S|`) plus tiny ring appends — roughly halved. The ring records are negligible compared to the `[V, K]` state.

![ReplaySSM caches recent SSM inputs in a ring buffer and reconstructs state on the fly, writing back only on flush](https://dao-lab.ai/assets/img/2026-06-15-replayssm/headline_approach.png)

*ReplaySSM caches recent SSM inputs instead of storing the recurrent state every step, reconstructing states on the fly and writing back only when the buffer is full. From the [Dao AI Lab ReplaySSM blog](https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/).*

---

## Core algorithm

Single head, single decode step (matches `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode` exactly):

$$\alpha = \exp(g)$$
$$d = \beta (v - \alpha (S k))$$
$$o = \alpha (S q) + d (k^\top q)$$
$$S' = \alpha S + d k^\top$$

Because the state update is **linear** in `S`, after `m` buffered steps the state before the current token unrolls to:

$$S = A \cdot S_0 + \sum_{j} w_j \cdot d_j k_j^\top$$

$$A = \prod_i \alpha_i \qquad\text{(total decay)} \qquad w_j = \prod_{i > j} \alpha_i \qquad\text{(replay decay of entry } j)$$

The bookkeeping is one rule: the checkpoint `S0` is decayed by **all** buffered `\alpha`; each older entry `j` is decayed by every `\alpha` that came **after** it.

**Output-only readout.** The output needs only `S q` and `S k`, both matrix-vector products. Substituting the unrolled `S`:

$$S q = A (S_0 q) + \sum_j w_j (k_j^\top q) d_j$$

`(k_j^\top q)` is a **scalar**, computed first; the `[V, K]` outer product `d_j k_j^\top` is **never built in HBM** on a non-flush step. The reconstruction sum is a small GEMM, run on **tensor cores** (see Precision below).

![Two routes to the same output: build the full state then read it, versus form the key-query scalar first](https://dao-lab.ai/assets/img/2026-06-15-replayssm/output_only.png)

*Two routes to the same output. The state-and-output route builds the full state then reads it; the output-only route forms the scalar key-query product first, so the state matrix is never materialized. From the [Dao AI Lab ReplaySSM blog](https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/).*

**Degenerate L=1.** The ring is always empty and every step is a flush, so the reconstruction term vanishes, `A = 1`, and the kernel reduces *algebraically and numerically* to the baseline packed decode — a bit-exact anchor for testing.

---

## Scope & work breakdown

### Part A — buffered output-only GDN decode (implemented)

A standalone decode kernel plus full runtime integration. **Implemented in [#28451](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28451).**

- New kernel + wrapper: `fused_recurrent_gdn_replayssm_decode(...)`, ported from vLLM `3c85112` with SGLang's packed GDN decode layout.
- Memory pool: per-slot ring buffers `replayssm_{d,k,g}` and a persistent `replayssm_write_pos`; reset at slot alloc and on COW.
- Backend dispatch: `TritonGDNKernel.packed_decode` routes to the ReplaySSM kernel when ring kwargs are present.
- CUDA-graph safety: static per-bs `write_pos` buffer, refreshed/advanced outside capture.
- Radix coordination: device-side `force_flush` aligned byte-for-byte to the mamba radix track snapshot condition (zero off-by-one), so the ring is folded into the checkpoint on exactly the step the radix cache reads `temporal[slot]`.
- Server args: `--enable-gdn-replayssm`, `--gdn-replayssm-cache-len` (default 16).

Files touched: the new kernel/test/bench, `mem_cache/memory_pool.py`, `attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py`, `attention/linear/gdn_backend.py`, `attention/linear/kernels/gdn_triton.py`, `attention/mamba/mamba2_metadata.py`, `configs/mamba_utils.py`, `server_args.py`.

### Part B — ReplaySSM spec-decode verify (proposed, gated)

The upstream `gdn_replayssm_spec_decode.py` is **not** a state-cache tweak — it is a full **chunked verify forward** kernel that:

- computes verify outputs for all draft tokens via the chunked delta-rule UT-transform `(I + A)^{-1}`,
- reconstructs the carried state output-only from a **circular ring carried across verify steps**,
- flushes the full state only **every `L` committed tokens** (not every verify step),
- runs the reconstruction on tensor cores.

This would convert spec-decode's full-state write from **every verify step** to **every `L` committed tokens** — a bandwidth win at high batch. It also makes rejected-draft rollback a pointer move on the ring rather than a state write-back:

![ReplaySSM caches each draft's raw inputs, so rolling back rejected drafts is a pointer move with no state write-back](https://dao-lab.ai/assets/img/2026-06-15-replayssm/rollback_solution.png)

*ReplaySSM caches each draft's raw inputs, so rolling back rejected drafts is just a pointer move with no state write-back. From the [Dao AI Lab ReplaySSM blog](https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/).*

**Relationship to #27658 (important).** #27658 ("compact linear spec cache replay") already captured the **memory** half of this idea for spec-decode: it stores compact `(k, Δv, decay)` per draft token instead of full intermediate states (2.32 GB → 0.06 GB), replays the accepted state once at the accept boundary in full fp32, and integrates the radix track snapshot + KDA. It explicitly reports **no throughput change** (verify was not bandwidth-bound at its 32–64-concurrency test point). Part B is **complementary, not a replacement**: it would add the bandwidth/speed half on top of #27658's memory/correctness infrastructure.

**Decision gate (do this before writing Part B code).** Measure the achieved HBM bandwidth of the spec-decode verify GDN forward at the *target* serving batch:
- ≥ ~70% → the full-state-write amortization is a real speedup; Part B is worth prototyping.
- < ~30% → same conclusion as #27658; the rewrite buys no time. Do not build it.

The upstream blog's own breakdown shows where the spec-decode gain comes from (kernel vs verify forward vs full decode step) and the orthogonal concurrency benefit — useful priors for what to expect:

![Speedup over the spec-decode baseline at kernel, verify-forward, and full-decode-step levels](https://dao-lab.ai/assets/img/2026-06-15-replayssm/spec-speedupbreakdown.png)

*Speedup over vLLM's speculative-decoding baseline at the kernel, verify forward pass, and full decode step levels. From the [Dao AI Lab ReplaySSM blog](https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/).*

![Maximum decode concurrency under a fixed HBM budget with speculative window 4](https://dao-lab.ai/assets/img/2026-06-15-replayssm/spec-maxconcurrency.png)

*Maximum decode concurrency under a fixed HBM budget (speculative window 4) — the memory axis that #27658 already addresses. From the [Dao AI Lab ReplaySSM blog](https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/).*

If built, Part B should: base on #27658's branch / its successor in `main` (**not** the Part A decode branch — Part A shares no spec logic with #27658, only the abstract idea; the real spec infra lives in #27658); reuse #27658's compact cache / radix track / KDA wiring; port the **early-flush invariant** exactly (`max_cache_len >= 2 * max_spec_len`, flush one window early so the circular cache never overflows the spec window — an overflow feeds the rejection sampler an uninitialized logit and desyncs the committed state); be gated behind a flag and default off.

### Out of scope (possible follow-ups)

- KDA decode (shares the backend; different gating — not wired in Part A).
- Lower-precision (bf16/fp8) ring/checkpoint to stack additional traffic savings.
- Batch-adaptive `L` (fall back to `L=1` at small batch where ReplaySSM cannot help and its extra reconstruction compute would otherwise be a small net loss).

---

## Design & integration concerns

The kernel is the easy half; the hard part is wiring a stateful, ring-buffered kernel into continuous batching + CUDA graphs + the radix prefix cache.

1. **`write_pos` is a per-slot decode cursor, not derivable from `seq_len`.** It must track the physical mamba slot (reset to 0 at slot alloc, when the post-prefill checkpoint is correct and the ring is logically empty), and advance **once per forward** (shared by all GDN layers of a step), not per layer.
2. **CUDA-graph safety.** `write_pos` is a static per-bs buffer captured by the graph and advanced in-place outside capture; the advance is guarded by `not in_capture` so warmup/capture do not corrupt the persistent counter.
3. **Radix `force_flush` alignment.** The radix cache snapshots `temporal[slot]` at fixed track boundaries; between flushes the checkpoint is stale. `force_flush` forces a flush on exactly those steps, computed from the identical condition the scheduler uses (zero off-by-one). `cache_valid` still uses the true `write_pos` — never fake `write_pos = L-1` to force a flush, or the kernel reads uninitialized ring entries.
4. **COW reset.** On a prefix-cache hit, `MambaPool.copy_from` copies the (always-flushed) snapshot into the private slot and resets that slot's `write_pos` to 0 so the destination ring starts empty.

---

## Precision & correctness

- **Mathematically lossless** — the reconstruction is an exact algebraic identity.
- **Not bit-exact in floating point** — the reconstruction GEMM runs on tensor cores (TF32 for fp32, bf16 tensor cores for bf16) and reassociates the recurrence, so it differs from the sequential baseline at the `~1e-4` (TF32) / `~1e-3` (bf16) level. This matches the upstream vLLM kernel, which uses the same tensor-core path and validates at the same tolerances (fp32 `atol 1e-4`, bf16 `atol 2e-2`).
- **Accuracy-neutral end-to-end** — per-step decay `\alpha < 1` attenuates old reconstruction error (bounded, re-anchored at each flush). Note that baseline GDN inference is already non-bit-exact across batch/chunk sizes; this introduces no new error class.
- Forcing IEEE precision on the reconstruction dot would make it bit-exact but disables tensor cores and makes the kernel **10–20× slower** — bit-exactness and the speedup are mutually exclusive by construction.

---

## Validation methodology (Part A)

Layered, weakest-to-strongest:

| Layer | Method | Result |
|-------|--------|--------|
| Kernel math | unit test vs `..._packed_decode` | fp32 `L=1` bit-exact (`atol 2e-6`); `L>1` within tensor-core tolerances; `force_flush` mid-buffer passes |
| Integration plumbing | short greedy decode, flag-on vs baseline | byte-identical (eager / CUDA-graph / radix all on) |
| **End-to-end correctness** | **GSM8K, radix + CUDA-graph on** | **flag-on 0.900 vs baseline 0.850 — within noise, no regression** |
| Performance | microbench + bench_serving | see below |

The standalone kernel test caught the tensor-core trap (an `input_precision="ieee"` dot that silently disabled tensor cores → 15× slowdown) **before** any integration work.

---

## Performance (honest, model-dependent)

- **Kernel microbench:** 1.2–1.5× at batch ≥ 16 with `L=8`; slightly slower at batch 1 (overhead-bound, not an operating point — the reconstruction compute is not hidden when there is no bandwidth pressure).
- **End-to-end (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, 128 concurrent):** ~2.3% TPOT improvement.

The e2e gain is much smaller than the kernel gain because Qwen3.5-35B-A3B is **MoE-heavy**: the GDN linear layers (where the kernel wins) are a small fraction of decode cost, diluted by MoE and full-attention layers. **GDN-dense models would gain substantially more.** This is a model-dependent optimization, not a universal speedup.

The theoretical ceiling is `~0.57×` traffic (`L=8`) → `~1.75×`; the realized 1.2–1.5× reflects <100% bandwidth utilization, the still-every-step `S0` read, the added reconstruction compute, and ring traffic.

For reference, the upstream blog reports the same shape — strong kernel-level speedup that dilutes to a smaller end-to-end gain on MoE models, and a clear dependence on buffer size `L` and batch:

![Kernel-level and end-to-end per-step speedup over the vLLM baseline across Nemotron-3 and Qwen3.5 families](https://dao-lab.ai/assets/img/2026-06-15-replayssm/ar-e2espeedup.png)

*Kernel-level and end-to-end per-step speedup over vLLM's baseline (Nemotron-3 and Qwen3.5 families). From the [Dao AI Lab ReplaySSM blog](https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/).*

![Kernel speedup for buffer sizes 4, 8, 16, 32 at batch sizes 64 and 256](https://dao-lab.ai/assets/img/2026-06-15-replayssm/ar-buffersize.png)

*Kernel speedup vs buffer size (`L` = 4, 8, 16, 32) at batch 64 and 256 — informs our `--gdn-replayssm-cache-len` default. From the [Dao AI Lab ReplaySSM blog](https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/).*

---

## Task tracking

- [x] Part A: buffered output-only GDN decode kernel + wrapper
- [x] Part A: memory pool ring buffers + `write_pos` lifecycle (alloc/COW reset)
- [x] Part A: CUDA-graph-safe `write_pos`
- [x] Part A: radix `force_flush` alignment
- [x] Part A: server args + validation (unit / byte-identical / GSM8K) — **PR: [#28451](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28451)**
- [x] Decision gate: measure spec-decode verify GDN forward HBM bandwidth at target batch
- [x] Part B: ReplaySSM spec-decode verify kernel (chunked, ring-across-steps, early-flush) — **PR:  [#28695](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28695)**
- [ ] Follow-up: KDA decode coverage

---

## Open questions / risks

1. **Is spec-decode verify bandwidth-bound at realistic serving batch?** This single number decides whether Part B is worth building (see Decision gate). Spec-decode is often latency-focused (low batch), where the win may be marginal.
2. **Part B integration risk is high** — it is a forward-kernel rewrite (~650 lines, chunked UT-transform) with a subtle early-flush correctness invariant, not a surgical cache swap like #27658.
3. **Tensor-core precision** — accepted as accuracy-neutral (GSM8K parity), but worth a config escape hatch for anyone who needs the slow bit-exact path.
4. **Scope of models** — Part A is GDN-only; KDA shares the backend but has different gating.

---

## References

- ReplaySSM blog (Dao AI Lab) — https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/ (source of all figures in this RFC)
- ReplaySSM reference implementation — https://github.com/Johnny-Liou/ReplaySSM
- Upstream vLLM ReplaySSM kernels (commit `3c85112`): `fused_recurrent_replayssm.py`, `gdn_replayssm_spec_decode.py`
- Marconi: Prefix Caching for Hybrid LLMs (arXiv 2411.19379) — background on hybrid-model state caching

_No response_

candidates.title: [Bug] Qwen3.6-27B (hybrid GDN) + AWQ degenerates on few-shot / multi-turn prompts at temperature 0; same checkpoint is clean on vLLM
candidates.body:
## Describe the bug

QuantTrio/Qwen3.6-27B-AWQ served on sglang 0.5.14 (awq_marlin selected at load) produces degenerate output on multi-turn few-shot prompts at temperature 0: repetition loops, mixed scripts, percent-encoded fragments, spurious `</think>` tags. A 6-shot multiple-choice prompt that should answer with one letter instead runs to the 512-token cap on 8 of 9 probes (mean 435 completion tokens).

Sample (6-shot MC, "What is 2+2? A. 3 B. 4 C. 5 D. 6", temperature 0):

```
- **A. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 6, 9, 10, 1, 2, 3, 3, 1, 1, 1, 1, ...
```

The same checkpoint on vLLM 0.21 answers these prompts with 1-2 tokens, correctly.

## Isolation performed

| variable | result |
|---|---|
| chat template | exonerated: offline `apply_chat_template` output byte-identical to a known-good checkpoint's; the correctly rendered string degenerates identically via `/v1/completions` |
| dtype | not the cause: bfloat16 and all-float16 (with `SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE=float16`, see #31719) both degenerate |
| radix cache | not the cause: `--disable-radix-cache` unchanged |
| awq_marlin alone | works elsewhere: a non-GDN AWQ model (Seed-OSS-arch 36B) on the same install serves multi-turn cleanly |
| engine | vLLM 0.21, same artifact, same prompts: clean |

Remaining suspects are the `qwen3_5` GDN implementation (for example the fused GDN projection path under `sglang/jit_kernel/triton/gdn_fused_proj`) or its interaction with awq_marlin activations. I can run further ablations on request; single-GPU consumer hardware, so tensor-parallel variants are out of reach.

## Reproduction

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path QuantTrio/Qwen3.6-27B-AWQ --dtype bfloat16
# then send a 6-shot multiple-choice chat completion, temperature 0, max_tokens 512.
# Plain single-turn prompts answer fine; few-shot/multi-turn degenerates, as does
# single-turn under an instruction-style system prompt.
```

Probe script with verdict output available; happy to attach.

## Environment

sglang 0.5.14, torch 2.11.0+cu130, flashinfer 0.6.12, driver 595.71.05, CUDA 13.3, RTX 5090 32 GB (sm_120), single GPU.

candidates.title: [Bug] GlmMoeDsa (GLM-5.2) FP4 + EAGLE: illegal memory access in flashinfer_trtllm bf16 batched-GEMM (nextn draft MoE); triton nextn default is HIP-gated after #30137
candidates.body:
## Summary
Serving `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, TP4/TP8, B200 & B300, `modelopt_fp4`, kv `fp8_e4m3`) with EAGLE (`--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6`) crashes with `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access` under real production traffic (~10 min to crash per replica at ~1 req/s; ~226k req/day fleet). Disabling speculation (no other change) → zero crashes.

## Root cause evidence
Exception-state CUDA coredump (CUDA_ENABLE_COREDUMP_ON_EXCEPTION) captured the faulting kernel:
```
CUDA Exception: Device Unknown Exception (30)
Bmm_Bfloat16_Bfloat16Bfloat16_Fp32_t128x8x128u2_..._dynB_sm100f  grid (48,8,1)
```
This is a flashinfer TRTLLM batched-GEMM cubin (flashinfer_cubin `batched_gemm-*/Bmm_Bfloat16...dynB`), used by the **flashinfer_trtllm MoE runner for the bf16 nextn/EAGLE draft layer** of the FP4 checkpoint. The kernel family is the sibling of the padding/TMA-OOB issue reported in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3722 (E2m1 swiGlu dynB variant).

## Fix validated in production
`--speculative-moe-runner-backend triton --speculative-moe-a2a-backend none`. Controlled A/B on synchronized-mirrored production traffic (identical requests to both arms, 8xB200 each): **control (flashinfer_trtllm spec-MoE) crashed 5× in 5h; triton arm: 0 restarts in 5h.** Since deployed to production: 24h+ crash-free with healthy speculation (accept len 3.19, accept rate 0.44) and 2.5-2.8× TPOT improvement on real data vs no-spec.

## The config gap
Legacy `server_args.py` applied exactly this default for DeepseekV3-arch FP4 checkpoints ("Use triton fused moe by default for bf16 nextn layer") with **no platform gate**, but `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` was not covered — so GLM-5.2 landed on the broken path by default.
After yesterday's config-pipeline refactor (#30137), `_DEEPSEEK_FAMILY_ARCHS` now includes GlmMoeDsa (good), **but the whole default is now gated `if not is_hip(): return {}`** (arg_groups/overrides.py ~L1199) — i.e. CUDA users of DeepseekV3/V32/Kimi/GLM FP4 + EAGLE no longer get the protective default at all, and fall through to speculative_moe_runner_backend = moe_runner_backend = flashinfer_trtllm → the crashing bf16 dynB bmm path.

PR removing the gate: incoming. Happy to provide coredumps/repro details.

candidates.title: DSv4 topk_v2 fused-cluster kernel crashes on B300/SM100 with DP-attn + DeepEP
candidates.body:
## Summary

`topk_transform_512_v2` (the v2 indexer top-k kernel introduced in #23882 and made default in #25406) crashes on **B300 / SM100** when **DP-attention + DeepEP** are enabled, surfacing as `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`. Reproduces deterministically across `lmsysorg/sglang:deepseek-v4-b300-dev`, `:nightly-dev-cu13-20260509-9ee83034`, and `:nightly-dev-cu13-20260517-229cadec`.

## Root cause

`topk_fused_transform` is annotated `__cluster_dims__(1, kClusterSize=8, 1)` via `FUSED_COMBINE_KERNEL`, but its SMALL (`seq_len <= Small::kMax1PassLength`) and TRIVIAL (`seq_len <= K`) branches let 7 of every 8 cluster blocks `return` immediately **without ever calling `cluster.sync()`**:

```cpp
if (seq_len <= K) {
    if (cluster_rank != 0) return;   // 7 blocks exit with no cluster op
    impl::trivial_transform(transform, seq_len, K);
} else if (seq_len <= Small::kMax1PassLength) {
    if (cluster_rank != 0) return;   // 7 blocks exit with no cluster op
    Small::run(...);
    Small::transform(transform);
} else {
    /* large path -- uses cluster ops correctly */
}
```

On SM90 (Hopper) and on SM100 at TP=4/DP=4 this is tolerated. On SM100 at TP=8/DP=8 (where the fused 1-stage path is taken because `batch_size_per_rank=4 <= kNumClusters=15`), the cluster scheduler / PDL state machine trips and CUDA reports `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` at the next sync point — typically CUDA graph replay or a downstream `deep_gemm.fp8_gemm_nt` call, which makes the failure look like an unrelated GEMM/attention crash.

## Reproducer

- Hardware: 8× B300 SXM6 (single host, NVLink only — no IB)
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`
- Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260517-229cadec`
- Server flags:
  ```
  --tp 8 --dp-size 8 --enable-dp-attention --moe-a2a-backend deepep \
  --max-running-requests 768 --mem-fraction-static 0.90 \
  --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 --cuda-graph-max-bs 512 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --disable-flashinfer-autotune
  ```
- Env: `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=1` (the default since #25406), `SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE=1`, `SGLANG_OPT_FIX_MEGA_MOE_MEMORY=1`, `SGLANG_OPT_FIX_NEXTN_MEGA_MOE=1`, `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=4096`, `SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=0`, plus W4A4 (`SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_FP4_ACTS=1 SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_MXF4_KIND=1`)
- Workload: `random ISL=8192 OSL=1024 conc=32 num_prompts=320 warmup_requests=64`

Crash fires ~10 s into decode. With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` + `--disable-cuda-graph` the sync stack pinpoints the kernel:
```
File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py", line 429, in forward_c4_indexer
    topk_transform_512_v2(...)
File ".../sglang/jit_kernel/deepseek_v4.py", line 381, in topk_transform_512_v2
    module.topk_transform(...)
tvm.error.InternalError: Runtime check failed at
.../sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/deepseek_v4/topk_v2.cuh:473:
CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

## Why CI didn't catch it

`test/registered/dsv4/test_deepseek_v4_flash_fp4_megamoe_b200.py` (added in #25052) covers TP=4/DP=4 on B200 with DSv4-Flash. The TP=8/DP=8 + DSv4-Pro + B300 configuration is uncovered.

## Workaround

`export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=0` — falls back to the v1 kernel (`topk_transform_512`) at `indexer.py:438`. No measurable performance impact at conc=32 (within 0.5% in our measurements).

## Proposed fix

Restructure the SMALL and TRIVIAL branches so all 8 cluster blocks reach `cooperative_groups::this_cluster().sync()` before exit. PR: <PR_URL_PLACEHOLDER>.

The fix preserves the v2 fast path on all architectures. The added cluster barrier is a hardware-fast operation (tens of ns) and is essentially free — the 7 dummy ranks were already pinned to the cluster's SM allotment whether they early-returned or sat at the barrier (CUDA can't reclaim cluster SM slots block-by-block; the cluster releases only after all blocks exit).

Validated on the same reproducer: with `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=1` + the patch applied, the same conc=32 workload completes cleanly at 958.5 tok/s/gpu (vs 963.7 with the `TOPK_V2=0` workaround — well within run-to-run noise).

## Affected revisions

- Bug present since #23882 (DSv4 introduction, kernel was opt-in via `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=False`).
- Surfaces by default since #25406 (merged 2026-05-16) which flipped `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2` default from `False` to `True`.

This is **not** the FP8 KV cache issue. The repro uses `--kv-cache-dtype bfloat16`. The issue appears **only** under a larger GSM8K evaluation load. A small 32-question GSM8K sanity run is healthy, but the full 1319-question GSM8K run collapses in accuracy and produces many invalid responses under the same server configuration. ## Setup - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B` - Hardware: GB200 - Disagg setup: - Prefill: 1 node, 4 GPUs, TP=1 - Decode: 1 node, 4 GPUs, TP=1 - KV connector: `NixlConnector` - KV cache dtype: `bfloat16` - Prefix caching: disabled - Async scheduling: enabled ## Testing Done ### Qwen3.5 Disagg with async scheduling enabled ```bash # [prefill node]: Start server VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS \ VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST=$(hostname) \ VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=6550 \ vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B \ --served-model-name Qwen3.5-27B \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8100 \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \ --generation-config vllm \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \ --async-scheduling \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}' # [decode node]: Start server VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS \ VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST=$(hostname) \ VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=6551 \ vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B \ --served-model-name Qwen3.5-27B \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8200 \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \ --generation-config vllm \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \ --async-scheduling \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}' # [localhost]: Start proxy python tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/toy_proxy_server.py \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8000 \ --prefiller-hosts "$PREFILL_HOST" \ --prefiller-ports 8100 \ --decoder-hosts "$DECODE_HOST" \ --decoder-ports 8200 # [localhost]: GSM8K run python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py \ --host http://localhost \ --port 8000 \ --model Qwen3.5-27B \ --max-tokens 1024 \ --no-stop \ --save-results /tmp/qwen35_disagg_async_bf16_gsm8k_32.json \ --save-details ``` #### Output (incorrect): ```text Running GSM8K evaluation: 1319 questions, 5-shot Results: Accuracy: 0.122 Invalid responses: 0.350 Total latency: 61.530 s Questions per second: 21.437 Total output tokens: 321834 Output tokens per second: 5230.486 Results saved to /tmp/qwen35_27b_disagg_async_bf16_gsm8k_4.json ``` #### GSM8K evaluation script note [gsm8k_eval.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27558481/gsm8k_eval.py) The repro uses vLLM's `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` with small local CLI additions needed for this disaggregated OpenAI-compatible endpoint: - Added `--model` so the request body includes `"model": "Qwen3.5-27B"`. This is required by the proxy/server path; the upstream script does not send the `model` field. - Added `--no-stop` to avoid the default GSM8K stop strings (`"Question"`, `"Assistant:"`, `"<|separator|>"`). This is useful for Qwen3.5-style thinking output, where those strings can appear inside reasoning and prematurely truncate generations. - Added `--save-details` to store per-question raw responses for debugging. - Adjusted answer extraction to prefer the canonical GSM8K marker `#### ` when present, instead of always using the last number in the full response. These changes do not alter the server configuration or the request concurrency pattern. They only make the vLLM GSM8K script compatible with this served-model-name/proxy setup and make the reported accuracy easier to debug. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

HIP used to load rightful `/opt/rocm/lib/libamdhip64.so.7` first with RTLD_GLOBAL in https://github.com/ROCm/mori/blob/0cc74439d82e231ad12674c4db2240a612b57cb1/python/mori/cpp/__init__.py#L39. Removing this `mori.cpp` initialization, instead: 1. We run into the call stack: ``` vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/__init__.py:116 from vllm.models.deepseek_v4 import DeepseekV4FP8Config └─ vllm/models/deepseek_v4/__init__.py:18 from .amd.dspark import ... └─ vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/dspark.py:40 from vllm.model_executor.layers.mhc import HCHeadOp └─ vllm/model_executor/layers/mhc.py:28 HAS_TILELANG_MHC = _has_tilelang_mhc() └─ vllm/model_executor/layers/mhc.py:15 if not has_tilelang(): └─ vllm/utils/import_utils.py:406 importlib.import_module("tilelang") # <-- trial import ``` that is https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/beca88e59ea75a7aa1af72a5ae50188fa91d4e3d/vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/tilelang_kernels.py#L16 and `importlib.import_module(module_name)` call https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/beca88e59ea75a7aa1af72a5ae50188fa91d4e3d/vllm/utils/import_utils.py#L406 `tilelang/__init__.py:173` does `import tvm`, which reaches https://github.com/tile-ai/tvm/blob/8df8ebd61659505dd7005f4820b030e983e2c005/python/tvm/base.py#L51-L53: ```python _LIB_RUNTIME = libinfo.load_lib_ctypes( "tvm", "tvm_runtime", "RTLD_GLOBAL", extra_lib_paths=_extra_lib_paths ) ``` libhip_stub.so` is a `DT_NEEDED` dependency of `libtvm_runtime.so` (and of `libtilelang.so` / `libtvm_compiler.so`). `RTLD_GLOBAL` propagates to dependencies, so the stub's 35 exported HIP symbols — including `hipMalloc`, `hipFree`, `hipGetDevice`, `hipGetDevicePropertiesR0600`, `hipModuleLaunchKernel` — land in the process-wide global symbol scope and win `dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "hipMalloc")`. AITER's JIT modules are `dlopen`ed later, and use wrong symbols then. ## CI reproduction See failures: - https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/11701/list?sid=019fd126-db3f-4316-8fb3-04b9b28e096c&tab=output - https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/11696/canvas?sid=019fcffa-7ecb-4330-bdaa-cf90089914fd&tab=output Also e.g. ```bash VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_quantization[True-fp8_per_tensor-None-Fp8PerTensorOnlineLinearMethod-Fp8PerTensorOnlineMoEMethod] -s -vvvvv ``` started failing locally after https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50879: ``` (EngineCore pid=43826) ERROR 08-05 09:30:24 [core.py:1345] File "/felmarty/repos/vllm/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py", line 1167, in _allocate_buffers (EngineCore pid=43826) ERROR 08-05 09:30:24 [core.py:1345] common_workspace, workspace2 = current_workspace_manager().get_simultaneous( (EngineCore pid=43826) ERROR 08-05 09:30:24 [core.py:1345] ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ (EngineCore pid=43826) ERROR 08-05 09:30:24 [core.py:1345] File "/felmarty/repos/vllm/vllm/v1/worker/workspace.py", line 110, in get_simultaneous (EngineCore pid=43826) ERROR 08-05 09:30:24 [core.py:1345] current_workspace = self._ensure_workspace_size(total_bytes) (EngineCore pid=43826) ERROR 08-05 09:30:24 [core.py:1345] ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ (EngineCore pid=43826) ERROR 08-05 09:30:24 [core.py:1345] File "/felmarty/repos/vllm/vllm/v1/worker/workspace.py", line 176, in _ensure_workspace_size (EngineCore pid=43826) ERROR 08-05 09:30:24 [core.py:1345] self._current_workspaces[ubatch_id] = torch.empty( (EngineCore pid=43826) ERROR 08-05 09:30:24 [core.py:1345] ^^^^^^^^^^^^ (EngineCore pid=43826) ERROR 08-05 09:30:24 [core.py:1345] torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid configuration argument ``` ## Minimal reproduction ```python import ctypes import sys mode = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "broken" import torch # noqa: E402 if mode == "fixed": # What the eager Mori import used to do by accident: get the real HIP # runtime into the global scope before tilelang can put the stub there. ctypes.CDLL("/opt/rocm/lib/libamdhip64.so", mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL) import tilelang # noqa: E402,F401 -> libtvm_runtime.so RTLD_GLOBAL -> libhip_stub.so import aiter # noqa: E402 -> JIT .so files bind to whatever is global from aiter import topk_softmax # noqa: E402 torch.cuda.init() dev = "cuda" num_tokens, num_experts, topk = 16384, 32, 8 gate = torch.randn(num_tokens, num_experts, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev) # Primes AITER's cached device properties (multiProcessorCount == 1 via stub). topk_softmax( torch.empty(num_tokens, topk, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev), torch.empty(num_tokens, topk, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev), torch.empty(num_tokens, topk, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev), gate, False, ) torch.cuda.synchronize() # Sizes its grid from those properties -> invalid launch configuration. from aiter.fused_moe import moe_sorting # noqa: E402 topk_weights = torch.softmax(gate, -1)[:, :topk].contiguous() topk_ids = torch.topk(gate, topk, dim=-1)[1].to(torch.int32) try: moe_sorting(topk_ids, topk_weights, num_experts, 1024, torch.bfloat16) torch.cuda.synchronize() except Exception as exc: print(f"[{mode}] RESULT: FAIL -- {type(exc).__name__}: {str(exc).splitlines()[0]}") raise SystemExit(1) print(f"[{mode}] RESULT: PASS") ``` giving: ``` [aiter] WARNING: NUMA balancing is enabled, which may cause errors. It is recommended to disable NUMA balancing by running "sudo sh -c 'echo 0 > /proc/sys/kernel/numa_balancing'" for more details: https://rocm.docs.amd.com/en/latest/how-to/system-optimization/mi300x.html#disable-numa-auto-balancing [aiter] import [module_aiter_core] under /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/aiter/jit/module_aiter_core.so [aiter] import [module_moe_asm] under /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/aiter/jit/module_moe_asm.so Traceback (most recent call last): File "/felmarty/repos/vllm/_debug_mori/minimal_repro.py", line 90, in topk_weights = torch.softmax(gate, -1)[:, :topk].contiguous() ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid configuration argument Search for `hipErrorInvalidConfiguration' in https://rocm.docs.amd.com/projects/HIP/en/latest/index.html for more information. CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call, so the stacktrace below might be incorrect. For debugging consider passing AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3 Device-side assertion tracking was not enabled by user. ``` `python _debug_mori/minimal_repro.py fixed` gives: ``` [aiter] WARNING: NUMA balancing is enabled, which may cause errors. It is recommended to disable NUMA balancing by running "sudo sh -c 'echo 0 > /proc/sys/kernel/numa_balancing'" for more details: https://rocm.docs.amd.com/en/latest/how-to/system-optimization/mi300x.html#disable-numa-auto-balancing [aiter] import [module_aiter_core] under /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/aiter/jit/module_aiter_core.so [aiter] import [module_moe_asm] under /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/aiter/jit/module_moe_asm.so [aiter] import [module_moe_sorting_opus] under /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/aiter/jit/module_moe_sorting_opus.so [fixed] RESULT: PASS ``` ## Root cause - `has_tilelang()` should not load tilelang symbols. - tilelang loads broken symbols, with `hipDeviceProp_t` filled with the wrong ABI layout. The stub *exports* `hipGetDevicePropertiesR0600` (ROCm 6 ABI) but internally resolves the old `hipGetDeviceProperties` (ROCm 5 / R0000 ABI), so every field of the returned struct is read at the wrong offset. ## Hotfix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51110 works, but does not fix the root cause. Root cause is `has_tilelang()` and `tilelang` imports loading wrongful shared objects ## Root cause and suggested fixes In decreasing order of correctness: 1. **tilelang (upstream)** — fix `hip.cc:121` to resolve the same ABI it exports, e.g. look up `"hipGetDevicePropertiesR0600"` (with a fallback to `"hipGetDeviceProperties"` for ROCm 5). This is the actual defect: the stub silently mis-reports every device property to ROCm 6 callers. Arguably `libtvm_runtime.so` should also not be `dlopen`ed with `RTLD_GLOBAL` when it exports HIP symbols, since that makes it interpose on unrelated libraries in the same process. 2. **vLLM** — stop `_has_module()` from doing a trial import for tilelang, or skip the probe entirely on arches where the feature is disabled. Importing a large native package as a side effect of an availability check is surprising and, as here, can have process-wide consequences. `_has_tilelang_mhc()` already returns `False` on gfx942 — the probe should never have loaded anything. 3. **AITER** — explicitly load/`dlopen` the HIP runtime it needs rather than relying on whatever happens to be in the global scope. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

candidates.title: [Bug]: Gemma4 vision encoder crashes with ValueError: Expected hidden_size to be 5376, but found: 72

labels.name: unstale
labels.description: Recieved activity after being labelled stale

candidates.body:
## Your current environment

- **vLLM version**: main (commit approx. 2025-04-05)
- **Model**: `google/gemma-4-27b-it` (or any Gemma4 multimodal model)
- **Python**: 3.12
- **CUDA**: 13.x
- **Transformers**: installed via pip in `.vllm` venv

## 🐛 Describe the bug

Starting vLLM with a Gemma4 multimodal model (e.g. `google/gemma-4-27b-it`) fails during engine core initialization with:

```
ValueError: Expected hidden_size to be 5376, but found: 72
```

Full traceback (abbreviated):

```
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 5761, in profile_run
    dummy_encoder_outputs = self.model.embed_multimodal(...)
File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/multimodal.py", line 350, in embed_multimodal
    vision_embeddings = self.model.get_image_features(...)
File ".../transformers/models/gemma4/modeling_gemma4.py", line 905, in forward
    value_states = self.v_norm(value_states)
File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/layernorm.py", line 241, in forward_static
    raise ValueError(
ValueError: Expected hidden_size to be 5376, but found: 72
```

## Root Cause

When vLLM's `TransformersModelBase._recursive_replace` walks the model graph and replaces norm modules, it calls:

```python
# base.py:442
elif child_module.__class__.__name__.endswith("RMSNorm"):
    new_module = replace_rms_norm_class(
        child_module, self.text_config.hidden_size  # ← always 5376 (LM hidden size)
    )
```

Inside `replace_rms_norm_class` (`transformers/utils.py`), the `hidden_size` argument is only overridden when the norm module has a `weight` parameter:

```python
weight_meta = getattr(rms_norm, "weight", None)
if weight_meta is not None:
    kwargs["hidden_size"] = weight_meta.size(0)
```

Gemma4's vision encoder `v_norm` is `Gemma4RMSNorm(head_dim=72, with_scale=False)`. With `with_scale=False`, no `weight` is registered, so `hidden_size` stays at 5376. The resulting `RMSNorm(hidden_size=5376, has_weight=False)` then validates `x.shape[-1] == 5376` for every forward call, but the vision value states have shape `[..., 72]`.

## Fix

**Fix 1 (primary)** — `vllm/model_executor/layers/layernorm.py`: Only validate `hidden_size` when `weight is not None`. A weightless RMSNorm has no constraint on the input dimension.

```python
# Before
if x.shape[-1] != hidden_size:
    raise ValueError(...)

# After
if weight is not None and x.shape[-1] != hidden_size:
    raise ValueError(...)
```

**Fix 2 (defensive)** — `vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/utils.py`: In `replace_rms_norm_class`, for weightless norms, try to infer the correct dimension from module attributes (`dim`, `hidden_size`, `normalized_shape`) before falling back to the text model's hidden_size.

```python
else:
    # No weight: try to infer the norm's dimension from other attributes
    inferred = getattr_iter(
        rms_norm, ("dim", "hidden_size", "normalized_shape"), None
    )
    if inferred is not None:
        if isinstance(inferred, (list, tuple)):
            inferred = inferred[-1]
        kwargs["hidden_size"] = int(inferred)
```

Note: Fix 2 alone does **not** fix the Gemma4 case because `Gemma4RMSNorm` with `with_scale=False` does not store `dim` as an attribute. Fix 1 is necessary.

## How to Reproduce

```bash
vllm serve google/gemma-4-27b-it --trust-remote-code
```

Engine crashes before serving any requests.

## Expected behavior

Engine should start successfully and serve Gemma4 multimodal requests.

candidates.title: [Regression] Trailing <turn|> token appearing at the end of generated text in vLLM 0.26.0
candidates.body:
### Your current environment

Description: After upgrading from vLLM 0.25.1 to 0.26.0 with gemma-4-31b-it, the model outputs the literal special token <turn|> at the very end of the response instead of stopping generation.

Environment:

vLLM Version: 0.26.0
Previous Version: 0.25.1
Model: gemma-4-31b-it
Deployment: Docker
Steps to Reproduce:

Deploy vLLM 0.26.0 with the aforementioned model.
Send a standard chat prompt.
Observe the last character of the output.
Expected Behavior: The output should end cleanly at the logical end of the sentence/code block, as it did in 0.25.1.

Actual Behavior: The output ends with an extra ` character.

Example:

Expected: "The process is complete."
Actual: "The process is complete.<turn|>"
It appears vLLM 0.26.0 failed to register or respect <turn|> as a stop token ID for the chat template.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

none

candidates.title: [Bug]: Negative CUDA graph memory estimation (-35 GiB) with MTP speculative decoding leads to severe KV cache over-allocation and OOM
candidates.body:
### Your current environment

Bug Summary
When running Qwen3.6-35B with MTP speculative decoding (method: mtp) on a 128 GB Unified Memory system (NVIDIA GB10 Blackwell), vLLM incorrectly calculates the CUDA graph memory as a massive negative value (-35.69 GiB). This causes the memory profiler to artificially inflate the available KV cache pool. At a standard --gpu-memory-utilization of 0.8, this leads to an immediate OOM. Lowering the utilization to 0.55 acts as a workaround, but still allocates a suspicious 72 GiB KV cache.

Environment:

GPU: NVIDIA DGX Spark GB10 (128 GB Unified Memory)

CUDA Version: 13.2.0

vLLM Version: 0.22.1rc1.dev23+g6bdabbad5.d20260531

Model: RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 (KV-Cache dtype: fp8)

Command Line Arguments:

```
Bash
python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 \
  --max-model-len 131072 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.55 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'
```
Relevant Log Output:

```
Plaintext
(EngineCore pid=257) WARNING 06-06 16:17:06 [compilation.py:1407] CUDAGraphMode.FULL_AND_PIECEWISE is not supported with spec-decode for attention backend FlashInferBackend... setting cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE
(EngineCore pid=257) INFO 06-06 16:17:06 [gpu_model_runner.py:6283] Profiling CUDA graph memory: PIECEWISE=51 (largest=512)
(EngineCore pid=257) INFO 06-06 16:17:13 [gpu_model_runner.py:6369] Estimated CUDA graph memory: -35.69 GiB total
(EngineCore pid=257) INFO 06-06 16:17:14 [gpu_worker.py:469] Available KV cache memory: 72.44 GiB
```
Expected Behavior:
The CUDA graph memory profiling should return a positive value, properly subtracting from the total available GPU memory instead of causing an underflow/negative estimation that inflates the KV cache block allocator.

Steps to Reproduce:

Load a >30B parameter model using fp8 kv-cache.

Enable chunked prefill.

Enable MTP speculative decoding with num_speculative_tokens: 3.

  PHB  = Connection traversing PCIe as well as a PCIe Host Bridge (typically the CPU)
  PXB  = Connection traversing multiple PCIe bridges (without traversing the PCIe Host Bridge)
  PIX  = Connection traversing at most a single PCIe bridge

initialization on 4×H200 with tensor parallelism 4.

candidates.title: GSM8K accuracy regression: nightly (0.26.1rc1.dev77) drops ~5% vs latest (0.26.0) on GLM-5.2-FP8 P/D
candidates.body:
## Summary

GSM8K accuracy drops ~5 percentage points when moving from `vllm/vllm-openai:latest` (v0.26.0) to `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` on the same cluster, same config, same benchmark command.

## GSM8K Results

### Setup

- **Benchmark**: [GSM8K](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/gsm8k) (grade school math, 1319 test examples)
- **Evaluator**: `lm_eval` v0.4.x, `local-chat-completions` model type
- **Few-shot**: 5-shot (`fewshot_as_multiturn=True`, default for chat completions)
- **Thinking**: Disabled (`enable_thinking: false` via `chat_template_kwargs`)
- **Sampling**: Greedy (`temperature=0.0`, `do_sample=False`)
- **Stop tokens**: `['Question:', '</s>', '<|im_end|>']`
- **Tokenizer**: HuggingFace backend

### Raw results

**`vllm/vllm-openai:latest`** (v0.26.0, commit [`ffd46bfab`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ffd46bfab2128bb84146050e98b51a617c6575ab)):

```
|Tasks|Version|     Filter     |n-shot|  Metric   |   |Value |   |Stderr|
|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|
|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9447|±  |0.0063|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9386|±  |0.0066|
```

Tested across concurrency 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384 — all consistently ~94.5%.

**`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`** (0.26.1rc1.dev77, commit [`6f91edf96`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/6f91edf96d3f3272945809c04702380053bff4de)):

```
|Tasks|Version|     Filter     |n-shot|  Metric   |   |Value |   |Stderr|
|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|
|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.8931|±  |0.0085|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.8855|±  |0.0088|
```

At 512 concurrency. 377 commits between the two versions.

### Regression summary

| Metric | latest (0.26.0) | nightly (0.26.1rc1.dev77) | Delta |
|--------|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| flexible-extract | 94.47% ± 0.63 | 89.31% ± 0.85 | **−5.16%** |
| strict-match | 93.86% ± 0.66 | 88.55% ± 0.88 | **−5.31%** |

### Null content warnings

The nightly run produced 3 instances of this warning (not seen on `latest`):

```
WARNING  [models.api_models:546] API returned null content. Content filled with
`LMEVAL_MODEL_NONE_ANSWER_PLACEHOLDER = `. Check reasoning_content field or generation limits.
```

These empty completions count as incorrect answers and partially contribute to the score drop.

### Benchmark command

```bash
lm_eval \
  --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args "model=zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8,base_url=http://localhost:8081/v1/chat/completions,tokenizer_backend=huggingface,num_concurrent=512,timeout=120" \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --apply_chat_template \
  --gen_kwargs '{"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false}}'
```

Accessed via `kubectl port-forward svc/llm-d-inference-gateway-istio 8081:80`.

## Hardware & Topology

- **GPU**: 8× NVIDIA H100 SXM per node
- **Prefill**: 1 replica × 4 nodes (32 GPUs total, expert-parallel across nodes)
- **Decode**: 1 replica × 4 nodes (32 GPUs total, expert-parallel across nodes)
- **Orchestration**: LeaderWorkerSet (LWS) on Kubernetes, P/D disaggregation with NixlConnector

candidates.title: [Bug]: NVFP4 KV writes V block scales in the SM100 trtllm-gen swizzle unconditionally, silently corrupting the SM120 FlashInfer XQA route
candidates.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```
GPU:        NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (32,607 MiB), compute capability 12.0 (SM120)
Driver:     610.62, CUDA 13.0
Host:       Windows + WSL2
vLLM:       v0.25.1 (upstream commit 752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34)
FlashInfer: 0.6.15.post1
PyTorch:    2.11.0+cu130
Power cap:  575 W (default), persistence enabled
```

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`reshape_and_cache_nvfp4_kernel` writes **K** block scales linearly but writes **V** block scales in the 4×4 swizzle required by the SM100 `trtllm-gen` MHA kernel — **unconditionally, for every architecture**.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/csrc/libtorch_stable/nvfp4_kv_cache_kernels.cu#L155-L173

```cpp
      // Write block scale to scale cache.
      // K (kv==0): linear layout (no swizzle).
      // V (kv==1): swizzled layout for SM100 trtllm-gen MHA kernel.
      if (sf_out_ptr != nullptr) {
        int scale_idx = group_in_head;
        uint8_t* __restrict__ scale_dst;
        if (kv == 0) {
          ...
        } else {
          int swizzled_offset =
              swizzle_scale_offset(block_offset, scale_idx, scale_dim);
```

On SM120 the NVFP4 KV route (FA2 prefill + FlashInfer **XQA** decode, discussed in #49011) consumes K and V scale tensors through **ordinary NHD tensor strides**. The XQA wrapper takes `[pages, page_size, kv_heads, head_dim/16]` scale tensors and passes the real page/token/head strides straight through; the XQA CUDA code contains **no V-scale de-swizzle**. FlashInfer's own paged-NVFP4 quantizer documents its V-scale swizzle as being *for `trtllm-gen` MHA* — that layout is not the XQA layout.

So the SM120 route wires a **swizzled producer to a linear consumer**. Every tensor has the correct shape, dtype and alignment, no kernel errors, no NaNs — the values are simply read in the wrong order. The result is a silently degraded model rather than a crash.

This is separate from #43562 (trtllm-gen FP4 FMHA has no sm_120 build). It sits *below* the read-side view work in #49011 / #44851 — those fix which kernels get selected and how the views are bound; this is the layout the data was written in to begin with.

---

### Evidence

All probes are model-free: deterministic BF16 inputs written through the installed `reshape_and_cache_flash` binding, then independently unpacked and dequantized.

**1. Synthetic round trip.** Normal NVFP4 loss in this exercise is ≈0.095 relative L2 (what K shows). V is far outside that, and linearizing *only* the V scales restores it:

| KV heads / Q heads | K rel-L2 | V rel-L2 (current) | V rel-L2 (scales linearized) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 / 8 | 0.0952 | **0.7625** | 0.0953 |
| 2 / 16 | 0.0954 | **0.7615** | 0.0949 |
| 4 / 24 | 0.0948 | **0.7876** | 0.0957 |
| 8 / 48 | 0.0946 | **0.7649** | 0.0953 |

No NaN/Inf. Per-head matching selected the identity mapping in all cases; no head swap.

**2. Direct XQA.** Two pages, page size 16, non-trivial block table `[1, 0]`, sequence length 23 — so page metadata and indexing are exercised too:

| KV heads / Q heads | current vs correct ref | current vs *deliberately wrong-scale* ref | linear-V vs correct ref |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 / 8 | 0.8222 | **0.00211** | 0.00213 |
| 2 / 16 | 0.7861 | **0.00218** | 0.00219 |
| 4 / 24 | 0.7769 | **0.00216** | 0.00216 |
| 8 / 48 | 0.7453 | **0.00214** | 0.00212 |

XQA reproduces almost exactly a reference that *deliberately applies the current wrong V-scale order*. That isolates the failure to the layout contract, ahead of the XQA math kernel.

**3. Not a striding/contiguity artifact.** Copying the four split views into explicit contiguous buffers changed direct-XQA output by **exactly zero** for every head count. Changing only V scale values from swizzled to linear corrected it. Adding copies does not help.

**4. It is not two-KV-head specific.** Both 2 and 4 KV heads fail the same structural test and both recover when V scales are linear. A checkpoint that appeared healthy on this route was not evidence the layout was valid — it was less likely to expose the corruption on the prompts being run.

---

### Correction to an earlier characterization of mine

I want this on the record because I stated it publicly and it was wrong.

In my first write-up (comment on #49011, and a downstream discussion thread) I described the V write as **destructive** — "V stored only the first four source scales replicated across groups of four; twelve of sixteen values lost at write time." **That is incorrect.** It was an artifact of inspecting only token row 0.

The 4×4 transform is a **lossless bijection** jointly across token and scale-group coordinates — the other source scale groups are present, in destination token rows 1–3:

```
dest_token = (src_token // 4) * 4 + src_scale // (num_scales // 4)
dest_scale = (src_scale % (num_scales // 4)) * 4 + src_token % 4
```

Confirmation: the full 16-token × 16-scale plane contains all 15 representable distinct FP8 values from the structured probe (the nominal 13th and 14th both round to 2.25). Applying the joint inverse restores V stored-order relative L2 from **0.588793 → 0.026317**, *exactly* matching K.

The practical consequence is unchanged — SM120 reads V scales in the wrong order and the model degrades — but "information is destroyed at write time" and "information is permuted into a layout this consumer doesn't undo" are different bugs with different fixes, and only the second one is real. I'd rather correct it here than have a reviewer inherit the wrong mental model.

---

### Proposed fix

Keep the swizzle where its consumer needs it, and write linear V scales where the consumer reads linearly. Compile-time, no runtime cost, K unchanged:

```cpp
#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && \
    (__CUDA_ARCH__ == 1200 || __CUDA_ARCH__ == 1210)
        constexpr bool swizzle_v_scale = false;
#else
        constexpr bool swizzle_v_scale = true;
#endif
        if (kv == 0 || !swizzle_v_scale) {
          // linear
        } else {
          // existing TRT-LLM swizzle
        }
```

After rebuilding the corrected writer, stored V relative L2 is 0.026317 for both 2 and 4 KV heads — exactly matching K — and applying the *old* inverse transform now damages it to 0.592983, i.e. the layout really did flip. Integrated re-validation across KV heads 1/2/4/8:

| KV heads | K rel-L2 | patched V rel-L2 | XQA vs ref | strided vs contiguous |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.09517 | 0.09530 | 0.002135 | 0 |
| 2 | 0.09542 | 0.09493 | 0.002194 | 0 |
| 4 | 0.09478 | 0.09568 | 0.002159 | 0 |
| 8 | 0.09457 | 0.09533 | 0.002121 | 0 |

I'll follow up with a PR referencing this issue. It also tightens the kernel tests, which currently pass with a loose elementwise tolerance that this class of layout error slips straight through — they should assert the expected layout per capability and carry a relative-L2 regression guard.

### End-to-end effect

150-scenario agentic/quality benchmark suites on a Qwen3.6-derived 27B NVFP4 checkpoint over the SM120 NVFP4-KV route, thinking-on, two draws per arm.

The **matched** comparison — same night, same image, same 131,072 context / 8 GiB pinned KV / 6 sequences, changing only `--kv-cache-dtype`:

| KV dtype (post-fix writer) | draws | mean |
|---|---|--:|
| FP8 E4M3 (control) | 121, 122 | 121.5 / 150 |
| **NVFP4** | 121, 124 | **122.5 / 150** |

Post-fix, FP4 KV lands on top of its FP8 control rather than below it.

For context — and I'll flag the confound rather than hide it — the same checkpoint on the **pre-fix** writer scored a 116/150 mean (232/300 at `--repeat 2`). That run used a 262,144 context envelope rather than 131,072, so it is *not* a matched arm and I won't claim the delta as a clean measurement. What it does indicate is direction: pre-fix, this route sat below its own FP8 control and read as ordinary quantization cost.

The wider point for anyone triaging this: the defect was silently costing quality on a configuration that passed every smoke test, needle-in-a-haystack retrieval to 246K tokens, and 1h40m of continuous load without a single error. There is no failure signature to grep for.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] I have made sure to search the existing issues and this is not a duplicate. This is distinct from #43562 (missing sm_120 trtllm-gen FMHA build) and sits below the read-side routing work in #49011 / #44851.

candidates.title: [Bug]: TP=2 spec-decode (qwen3_next_mtp / DFlash) on Qwen3.6 hybrid GDN crashes at gpu_model_runner.py:1927 num_accepted_tokens_event.synchronize() (cudaErrorIllegalAddress)
candidates.body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM: `0.19.2rc1.dev226+g53b9640fb` (built off PR #40898 head — DFlash + SWA support)
- GPU: 2× NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada Generation (sm_89, 48 GB each, no NVLink, P2P over PCIe)
- Driver: 580.126.09 / CUDA 13.0
- OS: Ubuntu, Linux 6.8.0-110-generic
- Python 3.12
- NCCL env: `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 NCCL_SHM_DISABLE=0 NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Enabling speculative decoding (tested both `qwen3_next_mtp` and `DFlash` methods) on a hybrid-GDN Qwen3.6-35B-A3B model with **TP=2** causes a hard crash on the very first chat completion request. The error is `cudaErrorIllegalAddress`, with the stack landing at `self.num_accepted_tokens_event.synchronize()` in `gpu_model_runner.py:1927`. Both TP0 and TP1 workers raise the same error, and the NCCL ProcessGroup watchdog thread subsequently terminates with the same illegal address exception.

Note: GDN prefill backend was auto-selected as **Triton/FLA** (not FlashInfer) in this build at the time of the crash, so this appears distinct from the FlashInfer-GDN line of bugs in #37729 and #37035, despite affecting the same model family.

### Reproduction

Launch:

```bash
vllm serve QuantTrio/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-AWQ \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --max-model-len 65536 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --port 8080 \
  --served-model-name qwen3.6-uncensored \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --attention-backend flash_attn \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_next_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'
```

Also tested with `--speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash","num_speculative_tokens":15}'` — same crash at the same line.

Server starts cleanly (`Application startup complete`), but **any** chat completion request triggers the crash immediately.

### Stack trace

```
(Worker_TP1) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:962] WorkerProc hit an exception.
(Worker_TP1) ERROR   File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 3496, in synchronize_input_prep
(Worker_TP1) ERROR     yield
(Worker_TP1) ERROR   File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 3875, in execute_model
(Worker_TP1) ERROR     logits_indices, spec_decode_metadata = self._prepare_inputs(
(Worker_TP1) ERROR   File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 1927, in _prepare_inputs
(Worker_TP1) ERROR     self.num_accepted_tokens_event.synchronize()
(Worker_TP1) ERROR torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
  File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 3498, in synchronize_input_prep
    self.prepare_inputs_event.record()
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered

[rank0]:[E ProcessGroupNCCL.cpp:2119] [PG ID 2 PG GUID 3 Rank 0] Process group watchdog thread terminated with exception: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

### Test matrix

| spec method      | TP | num_spec_tokens | cudagraph_mode | GDN backend     | result          |
|------------------|----|-----------------|----------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| qwen3_next_mtp   | 2  | 1               | full           | triton (auto)   | CRASH           |
| qwen3_next_mtp   | 2  | 2               | full           | triton (auto)   | CRASH           |
| qwen3_next_mtp   | 2  | 2               | piecewise      | triton (auto)   | CRASH           |
| qwen3_next_mtp   | 2  | 2               | none (eager)   | triton (auto)   | CRASH           |
| dflash           | 2  | 15              | full           | triton (auto)   | CRASH (same line) |

Neither `cudagraph_mode`, `num_speculative_tokens`, nor the choice of spec method affects the crash.

### What I observed at TP=1 (NOT a confirmed workaround)

Under a different configuration — an NVFP4-quantized variant of the same model family, TP=1, qwen3_next_mtp with `num_speculative_tokens=2`, and explicit `--gdn-prefill-backend triton` — no crash occurred. However, too many variables changed simultaneously (TP, model, quantization, context length, gpu_memory_utilization) to call TP=1 a confirmed workaround.

Side note: in that TP=1 test, qwen3_next_mtp acceptance rate was 0% (2021 drafts, 0 accepted), but this appears to be a separate issue likely caused by the abliterated/distilled MTP head, and is unrelated to the crash discussed here.

### Related issues

- #37729 — V1 engine silent deadlock under concurrent load, root-caused to the FlashInfer GDN prefill kernel. Different surface from this bug (deadlock vs hard crash), and our crash occurred with Triton GDN, not FlashInfer GDN — but same model family.
- #37035 — `gdn_attn.py:237` OOB at `num_speculative_tokens>=5` (FlashInfer GDN kernel). Different crash location and different threshold for spec-tokens.
- #37750 — Closed PR that attempted to fix #37729 by adding a `device=` parameter to `torch.Event(...)` calls, including `num_accepted_tokens_event`. The fix turned out not to address the root cause and was not merged, but the same event object is the one crashing here.

### Hypothesis (unverified)

`num_accepted_tokens_event` requires cross-rank coordination at TP>1. The fact that this event is the crash point — and that #37750 specifically called out its `torch.Event(device=...)` initialization as suspect — suggests a multi-rank event lifetime or ordering bug in the spec-decode preparation path. A fruitful place to look might be how spec-decode metadata is broadcast across ranks via the multiproc executor before this first `synchronize()` call, and whether the event's device-side state can be invalidated between `record()` and `synchronize()` under TP>1.

### Workaround currently in production

Disabled `--speculative-config` entirely. Pure-decode runs cleanly at 174 tok/s short / 141 tok/s long on this hardware.

candidates.title: [Bug]: GLM-5.2-NVFP4 produces garbled/incorrect output and hits NotImplementedError in forward_mha on GB10 (SM121a) with FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120
candidates.body:
## Environment
- Hardware: 6× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, SM121a — compute_121a), switchless ring topology, dual-rail 200G RoCE (NCCL over RDMA, patched NCCL for topology-aware routing)
- vLLM: v0.26.0
- flashinfer-python / flashinfer-cubin: 0.6.14 / 0.6.14 (confirmed matched, installed via flashinfer.ai/whl since flashinfer-cubin==0.6.14 was not yet on PyPI at time of testing)
- Model: `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` (resolved local checkpoint, 432.90 GiB total)
- Parallelism: Pipeline Parallel = 6 (one node per stage), Tensor Parallel = 1, native `mp` distributed executor (not Ray)
- Flags: `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --moe-backend marlin --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75`
- Attention backend selected automatically: `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` (only candidate listed — no fallback available)
- MoE backend forced to `marlin` (see rationale below)



### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Summary

After working around several unrelated infrastructure issues (documented
below for context, since they may affect others trying GLM-5.2 on GB10
clusters), the model **loads and serves successfully** (`Application
startup complete`), but:

1. **Generated output is garbled/nonsensical** on the very first request,
   even for a trivial prompt (`"Merhaba, kendini tanıtır mısın?"`).
2. **A later request crashes the engine** with `NotImplementedError` in
   `vllm/v1/attention/backend.py:1040` (`forward_mha`), apparently
   because a different request (longer prompt / different batch shape)
   takes a prefill code path that isn't implemented for this attention
   backend, whereas earlier requests silently used the `forward_mqa`
   (decode) path.

This appears consistent with the known, still-open issues:
- #49421 (GLM-5.2 NVFP4 support on SM120 — open)
- #49026 (flashinfer `sparse_mla_sm120` livelocks on GB10, adding
  `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` as fallback — open)
- #46726 (sparse-MLA indexer error with GLM-5.2 NVFP4 on SM120 — open)
- #48054 (DeepSeek-V4 sparse-SWA decode passes flashinfer 0.6.14-only
  kwargs while pin is 0.6.13 — open; we hit and resolved the version
  mismatch symptom described here by installing matched 0.6.14/0.6.14
  from flashinfer.ai/whl, but this did **not** fix the garbled output)

We're filing this because our repro is on a 6-node **PP=6** RDMA setup
(rather than the single/multi-GPU SM120 workstation setups in the issues
above), and confirms the garbled-output symptom persists **even with
fully matched flashinfer-python/flashinfer-cubin versions**, which may
help narrow down whether the root cause is in the `sparse_mla_sm120`
kernel itself (as #49026 suggests) rather than a version-mismatch
artifact.

## Reproduction

```bash
# All 6 nodes: flashinfer-python==0.6.14, flashinfer-cubin==0.6.14 (matched)
vllm serve /path/to/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 6 --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --nnodes 6 --node-rank <N> \
  --master-addr <addr> --master-port 29501 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --moe-backend marlin \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \
  --trust-remote-code
```

First request:
```bash
curl http://localhost:7001/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "GLM", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Merhaba, kendini tanıtır mısın?"}], "max_tokens": 100}'
```

Output (garbled, `finish_reason: length`):
```
"...,Y27 <ahan yaar ya fab25) zhouff232 DK58 ... Yokluz, ben50 a önemli
işçilik effectink7 ... da çokonaisu kelumeliyediğ gibi gibi uzunluk d
dahaveya ... fundasyon veya .. kansilityeri için oluşmuaz1ır Kamını..27
bk ..."
```

A subsequent request (different prompt/length) crashes the engine:
```
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py", line 785, in forward_impl
    self.impl.forward_mha(
File "vllm/v1/attention/backend.py", line 1040, in forward_mha
    raise NotImplementedError
NotImplementedError
```
followed by `EngineDeadError` and full server shutdown.

## Notes on ruling out other causes

- **KV cache memory sizing**: initially hit `ValueError: No available
  memory for the cache blocks` at `--gpu-memory-utilization=0.6`;
  resolved by raising to `0.75` (`Available KV cache memory: 21.18 GiB`).
  Not related to the garbled output.
- **MoE JIT compile storm**: the default `auto` MoE backend selects
  `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS`, which JIT-compiles CUTLASS grouped-GEMM kernels
  for the GB10-specific `compute_121a` arch (no precompiled cubin ships
  for this variant) — with 6 nodes compiling simultaneously, host RAM is
  exhausted and all nodes become unresponsive (not even ping). Forcing
  `--moe-backend marlin` avoids this entirely. Unrelated to the garbled
  decode output (MLA attention backend, not MoE).
- **flashinfer-python/flashinfer-cubin version mismatch**: initially hit
  `RuntimeError: flashinfer-cubin version (0.6.13) does not match
  flashinfer version (0.6.14)`. We resolved this properly (not via
  `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK`) by installing matched 0.6.14/0.6.14
  from `https://flashinfer.ai/whl` (not yet on PyPI at time of testing).
  **The garbled output persisted identically** after this fix, suggesting
  the root cause is not the version mismatch itself.
- **Swap/host-memory thrashing**: separately, we found that leaving swap
  enabled on these nodes causes CUDA/NCCL timing-sensitive steps to stall
  under memory pressure, manifesting as full node hangs (not even SSH/ping
  responsive) rather than clean errors. `swapoff -a` on all nodes converts
  hangs into clean, diagnosable errors — this is what allowed us to reach
  the actual `NotImplementedError` traceback above instead of a hang.

## Question for maintainers

Given #49026 proposes adding `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` (Triton) as a fallback
specifically because `sparse_mla_sm120` livelocks on GB10 — is it
possible the "livelock" also manifests as silent numerical corruption
(rather than an outright hang) in some code paths, which would explain
our garbled-but-completing output? Is there a way to force the
`FLASHMLA_SPARSE`/Triton path today (pre-merge) via an env var or CLI
flag, to test whether it resolves both the garbled output and the
`forward_mha` `NotImplementedError` on our setup?

Happy to test any patches/flags on our 6-node GB10 ring if useful for
validating a fix.

candidates.title: [Bug]: Running DeepSeek-V4 fails with  CUDA error: unspecified launch failure  in  synchronize_input_prep

labels.name: unstale
labels.description: Recieved activity after being labelled stale

candidates.body:
### Your current environment

 **Model**: `DeepSeek v4 flash
- CUDA version: 13.0
- GPU model: H100*8
- OS: `Ubuntu 20.04 LTS`
- Container runtime: Docker  deepseekv4 cu130

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## vLLM fails to run DeepSeek-V4 with CUDA launch failure

When trying to serve **DeepSeek-V4** using vLLM, the worker process crashes immediately with a `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure` error. The stack trace points to `synchronize_input_prep` in `gpu_model_runner.py`, and the process hangs before any requests are processed.

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1.  Run the following vLLM command to serve DeepSeek-V4:
    ```bash
    docker run --runtime=nvidia --gpus all \
    --name deepseek-v4 \
    -v /mnt/data/modelscope/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash:/model \
    --env CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \
    --env VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1 \
    -p 8025:8000 \
    --ipc=host \
    --shm-size=32g \
    vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv4-cu130 \
    --model /model \
    --served-model-name deepseek-v4 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
    --max-num-seqs 8 \
    --max-model-len auto \
    --block-size 256 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --enable-chunked-prefill \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager
    ```
2.  The server starts but immediately throws the following error and hangs:
    ```
    File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 3492, in synchronize_input_prep
        self.prepare_inputs_event.synchronize()
    torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure
    Search for 'cudaErrorLaunchFailure' in https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html for more information.
    CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call, so the stacktrace below might be incorrect.
    For debugging consider passing CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1
    Compile with `TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA` to enable device-side assertions.

    prompt throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Running: 2 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 1.8%, Prefix cach...
    broadcast block found in 60 seconds. This typically happens when some processes are hanging or doing some time-consuming work
    ``
### Additional context
- The error occurs even with minimal inference requests; GPU utilization and memory usage are low at the time of the crash.
- I have tried setting `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` and `TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA`, but the issue persists.
