candidates.title: [Bug]: PCP (#46570) broken for non-compress models (GLM-5.2, compress_ratio=1) — multiple crash paths
candidates.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text - vLLM version: `v0.23.1rc1.dev1327+gf25953cc5` (Jul 21 nightly, includes merged #46570) - Model: `GLM-5.2-NVFP4` (256 routed experts, hidden=6144, kv_lora_rank=512, `compress_ratio=1`) - Hardware: 8×H200 (141GB), `kv-cache-dtype: fp8_ds_mla`, `attention-backend: FLASHMLA_SPARSE` - Config: `TP=4, PCP=2, DCP=2, EP=8, MTP-5` - Speculative: `method=mtp, num_speculative_tokens=5` ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug PCP (#46570) does not work with GLM-5.2-NVFP4 (`compress_ratio=1` path). Multiple asserts/crashes occur when running `TP=4, PCP=2, DCP=2` on 8×H200. All paths were tested on nightly `v0.23.1rc1.dev1327+gf25953cc5` (post-merge #46570). ## Bug 1: Cudagraph warmup crashes with `assert 0 <= num_decode_tokens <= local_num_tokens` **Severity**: blocks startup without `--enforce-eager` **File**: `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/pcp.py:19` **Context**: `_gather_prefill_cache_inputs()` called during `_dummy_run()` → `_warmup_and_capture()` ``` sparse_attn_indexer.py:388 → maybe_gather_indexer_k() → pcp.py:19 assert fails ``` **Root cause**: During cudagraph warmup, `_dummy_run()` creates a dummy `InputBatch` via `InputBatch.make_dummy()` without PCP partitioning. The `attn_metadata_narrowed.num_decode_tokens` is the global decode token count, but `k` is truncated to PCP-local size. The value comparison fails. **Workaround**: `--enforce-eager` ## Bug 2: `sparse_attn_indexer.py` incorrectly divides `num_tokens` by `pcp_world_size` when `compress_ratio=1` **Severity**: blocks all inference with PCP (eager or cudagraph) **File**: `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py:380-384` ```python num_tokens = slot_mapping.shape[0] if use_pcp: num_tokens //= get_pcp_group().world_size # ← Wrong when compress_ratio=1 if k is not None: k = k[:num_tokens] ``` **Root cause**: When `compress_ratio == 1`, `slot_mapping` is **not** all-gathered across PCP — it stays local (`size = local_num_tokens`). But the division by `pcp_world_size` assumes the slot_mapping was gathered (as done for `compress_ratio > 1` in `indexer.py:843-846`). This truncates `k` to `local_num_tokens / pcp_world_size`, making it too small. The fix should conditionally divide only when the slot_mapping was actually gathered, e.g.: ```python if use_pcp and k is not None and slot_mapping.shape[0] > k.shape[0]: num_tokens //= get_pcp_group().world_size ``` ## Bug 3: `split_decodes_and_prefills()` asserts `is_prefilling is not None` in MTP drafter path **Severity**: blocks all inference with MTP + PCP (first non-startup forward) **File**: `vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py:624` ``` llm_base_proposer.py:999 build_per_group_and_layer_attn_metadata → indexer.py build_for_drafting() → build() → split_decodes_and_prefills(treat_short_extends_as_decodes=False) → assert common_attn_metadata.is_prefilling is not None ``` **Root cause**: PCP mode sets `treat_short_extends_as_decodes=False` which requires `is_prefilling` to be present in `CommonAttentionMetadata`. However, the MTP drafter's metadata builder path (`build_for_drafting()` → `build(fast_build=True)`) does not set `is_prefilling` — it's only set by `DefaultModelState.prepare_inputs()` during the main model forward. **Fix**: Gracefully handle `None`: ```python if not treat_short_extends_as_decodes: if common_attn_metadata.is_prefilling is not None: is_prefill |= common_attn_metadata.is_prefilling ``` ## Bug 4: `_gather_prefill_cache_inputs()` assumes slot_mapping is all-gathered **Severity**: blocks actual inference (after fixing Bug 2 & 3) **File**: `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/pcp.py:30,38` ```python gathered_slot_mapping = slot_mapping[: pcp_size * local_num_tokens] # line 30 ... rank_slot_mappings = gathered_slot_mapping.view(pcp_size, local_num_tokens) # line 38 ``` **Root cause**: This function assumes the caller already all-gathered the slot_mapping across PCP (`size = pcp_size * local_num_tokens`). For `compress_ratio > 1`, the indexer does this gathering. For `compress_ratio == 1` (GLM-5.2), it doesn't. When the function all-gathers the local slot_mapping internally, the sizes don't match — because in the MLA KV cache path (`maybe_gather_mla_latent_cache_inputs`), `slot_mapping.shape[0]` (e.g., 20) is **not equal** to `local_num_tokens` (e.g., 24). The indexer KV write path's slot mapping may exclude some tokens (e.g., indexer-only tokens with no MLA cache write), creating a size mismatch that `all_gather` cannot compensate for. ## Bug 5 (cascading from Bug 4): MLA KV cache update path slot_mapping size mismatch **Severity**: blocks MLA attention after fixing Bugs 1-4 **File**: `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/pcp.py:41` ``` RuntimeError: shape '[2, 24]' is invalid for input of size 40 ``` **Root cause**: `maybe_gather_mla_latent_cache_inputs` calls `_gather_prefill_cache_inputs` with `slot_mapping` from `FlashMLASparseMetadata`. The `slot_mapping` for MLA KV writes has `size ≠ local_num_tokens`, unlike the indexer path where they match. When PCP all-gathers this mismatched-size tensor, the result doesn't align with `pcp_size * local_num_tokens` needed for the `view` call. ## Root cause summary PCP (#46570) was designed and tested exclusively with models using `compress_ratio > 1` (DeepSeek V4 variants). The compressed path includes slot_mapping all-gather logic at the metadata builder level (`indexer.py`), which the non-compressed path (`compress_ratio = 1`, used by GLM-5.2) lacks. Several downstream consumers (`sparse_attn_indexer.py`, `pcp.py`, `utils.py`) implicitly depend on this gathering having been done. ## Desired behavior PCP should work for all MLA models, regardless of `compress_ratio`, without requiring `--enforce-eager`. The slot_mapping all-gather should happen in the metadata builder for both paths, and all downstream code should handle the gathered/local distinction correctly. ## Reproduction ```bash # Start server vllm serve /path/to/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 \ --decode-context-parallel-size 2 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \ --max-model-len 1048576 \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 5}' \ --enforce-eager \ --trust-remote-code # Send any request → crash at Bug 2 ``` ## Related - PR #46570: [Core] Add MRV2 virtual-batch PCP for MLA - All benchmarks in #46570 used `--enforce-eager` and did not test `compress_ratio=1` models CC: @LucasWilkinson @MatthewBonanni ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

candidates.title: [Bug]: Eagle 2/3 acceptance length regression over time
candidates.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
See below
</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

# Problem

Speculative decoding acceptance length (AL) smoothly and monotonically regresses over time when serving models with Eagle/Eagle3 draft models in vLLM 0.17.1. AL never recovers — only a full service restart resets it to the initial high value. The degradation correlates with traffic volume per prompt type — only high-volume prompt types are affected.

# Setup

* vLLM 0.17.1, v1 engine, async scheduling enabled
* 4x H200 GPUs (564GB total), gpu_memory_utilization=0.9 (all models executed with TP=4)
* Model ~250GB, leaving ~257GB for KV cache (~5M tokens capacity, ~312K blocks at block_size=16)
* KV cache dtype: GPT OSS 120B - BF16 (auto), ~50KB per token, other models uses FP8
* Block size: 16
* Prefix caching enabled
* Traffic: ~10-20 RPS
* ~60 different prompt types, average ~30K tokens each
* Per type: ~27K tokens cacheable (unique to that type), ~3K tokens unique per request
* First 4K tokens shared across all types, remaining 23K unique per type
* Traffic distribution: 5 types occupy ~50% of traffic, other 55 types share the rest
* Average OSL: 40 tokens

# Observations

1. Model A (BF16 weights and KV, Eagle2, 4 draft tokens, batch_size=2): AL starts at ~3.07, smoothly regresses to ~2.8 over hours. Only 2-3 highest-volume types affected.
2. Model A (BF16 weights and KV, Eagle3, 4 draft tokens, batch_size=2): AL starts at ~3.07, smoothly regresses to ~2.8 over hours. Only 2-3 highest-volume types affected.
3. Model B (FP8 weights&activation&KV cache, Eagle3, 5 draft tokens, batch_size=4): AL starts at ~4.5, smoothly regresses to ~2.8. All high-volume types affected, low-volume types unimpacted.
4. Model B (FP8 weights&activation&KV cache, Eagle3, 5 draft tokens, batch_size=2): AL starts at ~4.2, regresses to ~3.8. Reducing speculation length to lower values does NOT change the regression behavior.
5. Model C (FP8 weights&activation&KV cache, Eagle3, 5 draft tokens, batch_size=2) with vLLM: AL starts at ~3.9, regresses to ~3.5 vs with TRT-LLM: AL is stable and does not regress.
6. Restart resets AL immediately to the initial high value, regardless of current traffic level.
7. TRT-LLM: slight AL regression at peak traffic but recovers during low traffic. vLLM only regresses, never recovers.
8. Both Eagle2 and Eagle3 shows regression of AL over time.
9. TTFT and prefix cache hit rate appear stable.
10. Running Model B with newer vLLM version 0.19.1 does not fix the problem, regression is still observed.


# Relevant GitHub Issues/PRs

* Issue #14649: "EAGLE / MTP Doesn't Overwrite Approximated Hidden States / KV Cache" — describes the fundamental problem. Unfixed in v0, but v1's first pass mechanism largely addresses it (small residual gap).
* PR #14990: "Enhance EAGLE Architecture with Proper RMS Norms" — merged Mar 2025, adds proper norm handling to Eagle model.
* PR #16370: "[V1][Spec Decode] KV cache slots for eagle heads" — merged, shows v1 gap is small in offline benchmarks (2.43 vs 2.48 for 5 spec tokens on Llama 3.1 8B).
* PR #14464: "EAGLE output norm bug" — merged, fixes return x + residual, None vs return x, residual in Eagle model.
* PR #29845: "Simplified alternative padded-speculation acceptance rate fix" — merged, adds num_rejected_tokens_gpu adjustment to seq_lens before sequential drafting loop.

# Experiments we are running now (will be updated with new observations)
- Disabling prefix caching
- Disabling async scheduling
- Run with batch size=1

candidates.title: [Bug]: MiniMax M3 Triton path misinterprets token-major top-k buffer
candidates.body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM: v0.25.1 and current `main`
- Model: MiniMax-M3-MXFP8
- Hardware: 8x NVIDIA A100 (SM80)
- Tensor parallel size: 8

### Model Input Dumps

No model input dump is required to reproduce the layout mismatch. It occurs when the MiniMax M3 Triton indexer receives the model's persistent top-k output buffer.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The NVIDIA MiniMax M3 model allocates `topk_indices_buffer` in token-major `[T, H, K]` layout for the MSA path. The common Triton indexer and sparse-attention paths still slice that buffer as if it were head-major `[H, T, K]`.

During inference this reaches `minimax_m3_index_topk` / `_topk_index_kernel` with incorrect shape and strides and eventually fails with:

```text
RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

The failure occurs in the call chain:

```text
minimax_m3/nvidia/model.py
  -> common/indexer.py
  -> common/ops/index_topk.py
  -> _topk_index_kernel
```

The proposed fix keeps one token-major persistent layout across NVIDIA and AMD and passes transposed head-major views at the Triton write/read boundaries. No Triton kernel algorithm is changed.

A100 validation after applying the fix:

- Model initializes successfully.
- 100/100 long-context benchmark requests complete successfully.
- LMCache registers all 117 MiniMax M3 KV tensors and inference remains stable.

The A100 Triton path has been tested. SM100 MSA and ROCm require CI or maintainer hardware validation.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary I first observed this issue during normal use through Open WebUI. With automatic prefix caching enabled, the model would sometimes stop seeing some of the configured tools after the first requests. The model could initially list all tools correctly, then omit some of them in later requests. To determine whether Open WebUI was responsible, I created a standalone deterministic script that calls the vLLM OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint directly. The standalone script reproduces the issue without Open WebUI and without MTP. The problem occurs with the following combination: * Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 * automatic prefix caching enabled; * native KV offloading enabled; * MTP disabled; * a sufficiently long request sharing the same prefix as a shorter request. An identical request produces a different interpretation of its tool context after another request extends the same shared prefix. ## Minimal reproduction The script sends the following sequence using the same: * model; * deterministic tool definitions; * system-message prefix; * sampling parameters; * seed; * `cache_salt`. Sequence: 1. Request A: 20 deterministic tools and no system-message padding. 2. Request B: the same tools, with 512000 deterministic padding characters appended to the system message. 3. Request A again, identical to the initial request A. Run: ```bash python3 vllm_prefix_cache_tool_probe_v3.py \ --base-url http://localhost:8000/v1 \ --tool-count 20 \ --padding-sequence 0,500k,0 ``` Reproduction script: https://gist.github.com/raoulprevost/6823cfde04df73f7778a343be73c7e74 The script generates a new random `cache_salt` for each complete run and uses the same salt for every stage of that run. ## Observed result ```text A: 20 tools, no padding -> 20/20 tools B: 20 tools, 512000 chars -> 20/20 tools A: identical to initial A -> 16/20 tools ``` Full relevant output: ```text Sequence : A(0 chars) -> B(512000 chars) -> A(0 chars) Tools : 20 (11692 compact JSON chars) Step 1/3 [A] padding=0 chars Run 1/2: PASS | TOTAL=20 | found=20/20 | missing positions=- | prompt_tokens=4611 Run 2/2: PASS | TOTAL=20 | found=20/20 | missing positions=- | prompt_tokens=4611 Stage result: 2/2 passed Step 2/3 [B] padding=512000 chars Run 1/2: PASS | TOTAL=20 | found=20/20 | missing positions=- | prompt_tokens=104603 Run 2/2: PASS | TOTAL=20 | found=20/20 | missing positions=- | prompt_tokens=104603 Stage result: 2/2 passed Step 3/3 [A] padding=0 chars Run 1/2: FAIL | TOTAL=16 | found=16/20 | missing positions=17-20 | prompt_tokens=4611 Run 2/2: FAIL | TOTAL=16 | found=16/20 | missing positions=17-20 | prompt_tokens=4611 Stage result: 0/2 passed RESULT: REPRODUCED Variant A passed before the intervening request(s) and failed afterwards. Final-stage missing positions: 17-20 ``` Both final A responses omit exactly the same four tools. The initial and final A payloads are identical and both report: ```text prompt_tokens=4611 ``` Request B itself correctly sees all 20 tools. ## Expected behavior The final request A is identical to the initial request A and should interpret the same 20 tool definitions. Processing another request that shares and extends the same prefix must not change the interpretation of the original request. ## Actual behavior The initial A request correctly lists all 20 tools. The longer B request also correctly lists all 20 tools. After B has been processed, the exact same A request consistently lists only 16 tools. The server does not crash or return an error. It returns a normal but semantically incorrect response. The tool definitions are only deterministic markers used to make the context-interpretation problem measurable. This reproduction does not establish that the affected context is limited to tool definitions. ## Configuration Model: ```text nvidia/Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 ``` vLLM: ```text vLLM 0.25.1 Docker image: vllm/vllm-openai:latest Docker image ID: sha256:e4f88a835143cd22aee2397a26ec6bb80b3a4a6fe0c882bcbc63822904766089 ``` Hardware and software: ```text GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 NVIDIA driver: 595.71.05 CUDA runtime: 13.0.88 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 Transformers: 5.13.1 ``` Relevant vLLM arguments: ```text nvidia/Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 --served-model-name TeSA-Fondation --quantization modelopt --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len auto --gpu-memory-utilization 0.93 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml --chat-template /templates/qwen3.6-enhanced.jinja --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 4 --trust-remote-code --scheduler-reserve-full-isl --mm-processor-kwargs '{"min_pixels": 784, "max_pixels": 1605632, "fps": 1}' --tensor-parallel-size 1 --enable-chunked-prefill --enable-prefix-caching --kv-offloading-backend native --kv-offloading-size 16 ``` MTP/speculative decoding is not enabled in this reproduction. ## Isolation tests Removing native KV offloading while keeping prefix caching enabled prevented the standalone reproduction in my tests. Re-enabling: ```text --kv-offloading-backend native --kv-offloading-size 16 ``` made the problem reproducible again without MTP. The result also appears to depend on the length of request B. With 20 tools: ```text B prompt_tokens=84638 -> not reproduced B prompt_tokens=104603 -> reproduced ``` With 55 tools: ```text B prompt_tokens=91865 -> not reproduced B prompt_tokens=111830 -> reproduced B prompt_tokens=131730 -> reproduced B prompt_tokens=171706 -> reproduced ``` I do not assume that there is an exact token threshold; these values only show that the problem appeared when the longer request caused sufficient cache pressure in this configuration. ## Possibly related issues * #41514 also reports that a subsequent Qwen3.6 request fails only when KV offloading and prefix caching are enabled. However, that report uses MTP and TP=2 and results in an engine crash. This reproduction uses no MTP, TP=1, and produces silent semantic corruption instead of a crash. * #44585 reported another inconsistency involving native CPU KV-offload prefix-cache reads, but it concerned `skip_reading_prefix_cache`. * #41612 concerns a crash involving pipeline parallelism and asynchronous scheduling. I could not find an existing report reproducing a silent change in tool visibility for an identical request after a long shared-prefix request, with native KV offloading enabled and MTP disabled. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary Server runs healthy for hours under sustained concurrent load, then enters a livelock state: `Running: N reqs`, `Avg generation throughput: 0.0 tokens/s`, indefinitely. No crash, no traceback, no `EngineDeadError`. GPU (`nvidia-smi`) shows `utilization.gpu ~96%`, `utilization.memory 0%`, power draw far below TDP (~17W observed) — consistent with a spin-wait, not active compute. No Xid errors in `dmesg`/`journalctl` at the time of the incident. Only a container/process restart recovers service. Reproduced 6 times independently across different mitigation attempts and configs (see below), including once after a simple `docker restart` with no config change (livelock recurred after only ~3.5 minutes under organic production load) and once after reverting to a config close to defaults (`--attention-backend auto`, prefix caching enabled, no forced kernel backends). In the first 3 occurrences, onset coincided with `Running` reaching the configured `--max-num-seqs` ceiling. In later occurrences `Running` stalled below the ceiling with a `Waiting` backlog — the livelock is not tied to reaching the configured concurrency ceiling itself. Across all occurrences, the metrics immediately preceding the stall show an `Avg prompt throughput` spike (a prefill burst) in the 1-2 scheduler ticks (10s each) before generation throughput collapses to 0. This points to concurrent prefill+decode mixing as the trigger, independent of absolute concurrency count and, per the 6th occurrence, independent of which kernel backends are in use. ## Startup config (final attempt, most restrictive) ``` --quantization modelopt --attention-backend flash_attn --moe-backend marlin --linear-backend torch --ir-op-priority '{"rms_norm": ["native"], "fused_add_rms_norm": ["native"]}' --max-num-seqs 12 --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --enable-chunked-prefill --no-enable-prefix-caching --enforce-eager ``` Env: `VLLM_MARLIN_USE_ATOMIC_ADD=1` ## Diagnostic timeline / ruled-out causes 1. **Initial hard crash** (different bug, now fixed): `FlashInferFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel.is_supported()` in `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/flashinfer.py` only checks `compute_capability < 100`, which incorrectly passes SM121 (121 >= 100) into a cuDNN GEMM path (`fp8_gemm_sm100`) hard-coded for SM100 tensor core layout → `CUDNN_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED_CUDA_DRIVER`. Worked around with `--linear-backend torch` (forces `PerTensorTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel`). This is a separate, reproducible, deterministic bug — happy to file separately if useful, but flagging here since it may be architecturally related (SM121 not being treated as its own family in enough places). 2. **After the above fix, the livelock described in this issue appeared instead** (soft hang, no crash) under sustained load at full `--max-num-seqs` concurrency. 3. Captured `py-spy dump --pid --locals` on **four independent occurrences**. Three (before/after forcing `--ir-op-priority native`, and after a plain `docker restart`) show the byte-for-byte identical frame: MainThread active inside `fused_add_rms_norm` → `GemmaRMSNorm.forward_native/forward_cuda` → `Qwen3_5DecoderLayer.forward` (`layer_idx: 19` in all three captures) → ... → `step_with_batch_queue`. The fourth (different config, see 6th occurrence below) instead shows `torch.cuda.Event.synchronize()` inside the async-scheduling output path (`AsyncGPUModelRunnerOutput.get_output`) — a different frame entirely. 4. Forcing `rms_norm`/`fused_add_rms_norm` to `native` (pure PyTorch, no custom CUDA kernel) did **not** change the observed hang location or prevent recurrence. This strongly suggests RMSNorm is not the actual culprit — see next point. 5. Cross-referencing a separate, unrelated report on the NVIDIA DGX Spark forum (**FlashInfer sparse-MLA mbarrier livelock on GB10**, forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/377334, filed 2026-07-18 against a different model/kernel — GLM-5.2, `sparse_mla_sm120`, multi-node TP=4) describes the same class of failure with near-identical telemetry signature: `utilization.gpu 96%, power ~18W, utilization.memory 0%`, confirmed via `cuda-gdb` attach to be a resident kernel spin-looping on an mbarrier phase check (`SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT`) that never resolves — a TMA/`cp.async.bulk` expect-tx accounting race. Critically, that report explicitly notes: *"the Python-level frame is arbitrary (marlin_gemm, MoE workspace, triton launcher — bystanders)"* — i.e. once one kernel is wedged, every subsequent kernel launch queues behind it, and whatever Python code happens to be issuing the next launch is what `py-spy` shows, regardless of where the actual bug lives. 6. Given (4) and (5), we suspect our two RMSNorm frames are likewise **bystanders**, not the root cause. The model uses the GDN (Gated DeltaNet) hybrid linear-attention architecture (`vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py`), and our startup log shows: ``` Using Triton/FLA GDN prefill kernel (requested=auto, head_k_dim=128). ``` Inspecting `_resolve_gdn_prefill_backend()`: on SM121, `is_device_capability_family(100)` correctly excludes both the FlashInfer and CuteDSL GDN prefill paths (family check is 100–109, SM121 falls outside), leaving Triton/FLA as the *only* available backend — there is no config flag to select an alternative. This Triton kernel is comparatively new/untested code on SM121 specifically (per Qwen3.5 HF model card, upstream `fla`/`causal_conv1d` packages ship no SM121 build at all; vLLM's in-tree Triton port is the only path). We were not able to find a flag equivalent to `--max-num-partial-prefills` in this build (checked `--help`) to isolate prefill from concurrent decode for a cleaner repro. ## What we're asking - Has anyone observed similar Triton/FLA GDN prefill livelocks on SM121 specifically (vs. SM90/SM100 where this path is presumably better exercised)? - Is there a way to force the pure-PyTorch GDN fallback path (bypassing Triton entirely) to test this hypothesis, similar to `--linear-backend torch` for the FP8 GEMM kernel? We could not find one via `--help`. - Given the FlashInfer sparse-MLA precedent, could this be the same underlying class of mbarrier/synchronization bug appearing in a different in-tree Triton kernel rather than FlashInfer specifically? ## Log excerpt, 4th occurrence (2026-07-20, `--max-num-seqs 12`, `Running` stalled at 8/12) ``` 11:45:52 Running: 7 prompt: 118.6 tok/s gen: 61.9 tok/s 11:46:02 Running: 8 prompt: 2837.0 tok/s gen: 66.9 tok/s <- prefill burst 11:46:12 Running: 8 prompt: 3929.2 tok/s gen: 101.0 tok/s <- larger prefill burst 11:46:22 Running: 8 prompt: 0.0 tok/s gen: 53.6 tok/s <- decode already degrading 11:46:32 Running: 8 prompt: 0.0 tok/s gen: 0.0 tok/s <- fully wedged, indefinitely ``` ## Log excerpt, 5th occurrence (2026-07-20, fresh `docker restart`, no config change, organic production traffic, `--max-num-seqs 12`) Server ready at 12:41:44. Livelock at 12:45:11 — **~3.5 minutes uptime**, the fastest reproduction so far, under real (non-synthetic) traffic with a persistent `Waiting` backlog of 3-6 requests (scheduler continuously pulling new requests from queue, i.e. near-continuous prefill activity): ``` 12:44:51 Running:12 Waiting:4 prompt: 2901.9 tok/s gen: 117.3 tok/s <- large prefill burst 12:45:01 Running:12 Waiting:3 prompt: 82.4 tok/s gen: 23.9 tok/s <- sharp collapse 12:45:11 Running:12 Waiting:3 prompt: 0.0 tok/s gen: 0.0 tok/s <- fully wedged ``` `py-spy dump --pid ` immediately after: identical frame to the two prior captures (`fused_add_rms_norm`, `layer_idx: 19`, `GDNAttentionMetadata`), `num_scheduled_tokens: 12`, `max_num_scheduled_tokens: 1` — confirming the hang was caught mid-decode-step (1 token/request), consistent with the "bystander" theory: an earlier prefill-triggered kernel wedged the stream, and the next decode step's kernel launch queued behind it. ## Log excerpt + py-spy, 6th occurrence — different config, different bystander frame (2026-07-21) This occurrence used a **substantially different, closer-to-default config** (reverted several of our earlier workarounds to test whether they mattered): ``` --attention-backend auto (was: flash_attn) --enable-prefix-caching (was: --no-enable-prefix-caching) --max-num-seqs 8 # no --linear-backend override, no --ir-op-priority override ``` Same prefill-precedes-collapse pattern: ``` 06:58:05 Running:7 prompt:102.6 tok/s gen:175.4 tok/s 06:58:15 Running:7 prompt:340.1 tok/s gen:215.6 tok/s <- prefill burst 06:58:25 Running:6 prompt:0.0 tok/s gen:203.4 tok/s <- decode degrading 06:58:35 Running:5 prompt:0.0 tok/s gen:174.9 tok/s 06:58:45 Running:4 prompt:0.0 tok/s gen:73.4 tok/s 06:58:55 Running:4 prompt:0.0 tok/s gen:0.0 tok/s <- fully wedged ``` **Critically, this time `py-spy dump --locals` shows a completely different frame** — not `fused_add_rms_norm` at all: ``` Thread 249 (active): "MainThread" synchronize (torch/cuda/streams.py:254) Arguments: self: get_output (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:306) Arguments: self: result (vllm/v1/executor/uniproc_executor.py:38) Arguments: self: step_with_batch_queue (vllm/v1/engine/core.py:604) ``` This is `torch.cuda.Event.synchronize()` blocking forever inside vLLM's async-scheduling overlap output path (`AsyncGPUModelRunnerOutput.get_output`), waiting on a CUDA event that never fires. **We consider this the strongest evidence yet for the "arbitrary bystander frame" theory** (per the NVIDIA forum precedent cited above): two different configs, using different kernel backends (native RMSNorm + flash_attn in occurrences 1-5 vs. auto attention-backend + prefix caching + default RMSNorm here), produce the *same* prefill-preceded collapse signature but *different* Python-visible frames. This strongly suggests the actual wedge is a CUDA stream/kernel-level event (most likely inside the GDN Triton kernel or the attention kernel actually resolved by `auto`, neither of which appear directly in either captured stack) that manifests wherever the next synchronization point in the code happens to be — RMSNorm's op call in one config, the async output event wait in another. This is consistent with, though not proof of, an mbarrier-class synchronization bug similar to the one documented for FlashInfer's sparse-MLA kernel on the same hardware family. This also means our earlier mitigations (`--linear-backend torch`, `--ir-op-priority native`) likely never addressed the actual root cause — they may have only changed which bystander frame gets caught, not whether the underlying wedge occurs. ## Attachments available on request - Full `py-spy dump --locals` output x2 (pre/post `--ir-op-priority native` change) - `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,PERFORMANCE,CLOCK,POWER,TEMPERATURE` snapshot during live hang - `dmesg`/`journalctl` excerpts (no Xid present) - Full startup config dumps (`KernelConfig`, `IrOpPriorityConfig` resolved values) for both attempts ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

candidates.title: [RFC]: Unified Device Capability Abstraction for Cross-Platform Feature Detection
candidates.body:
### Motivation.

This is an AI-generated proposal, there may be some error. appreciate if you can point out. 

## 1. Problem Summary

As raised by @tjtanaa in [#39158](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39158), the current `has_device_capability(int)` / `is_device_capability_family(int)` API is **fundamentally CUDA-centric** and does **not** translate correctly to ROCm or XPU.

### 1.1 Problem A: `device_capability` is inherently a CUDA concept

`torch.cuda.get_device_capability()` returns `(major, minor)` tied to NVIDIA's SM (Streaming Multiprocessor) versioning. **ROCm and XPU have completely different hardware models** — any mapping to CUDA-style numbers is artificial and lossy:

| Platform | Capability Model | How it works |
|----------|-----------------|--------------|
| **CUDA** | SM version `(major, minor)` e.g. `(8,9)`, `(9,0)`, `(10,0)` | Native `torch.cuda.get_device_capability()` |
| **ROCm** | GCN arch string (e.g. `gfx942`) → **artificially mapped** to `(major, minor)` | Semantic mismatch: `gfx90a` maps to `(9,0)` but has NO FP8, while CUDA's `(9,0)` = Hopper = has FP8 |
| **XPU** | No capability model → always returns `None` → all checks = `False` | All feature gates broken |
| **CPU/TPU** | No capability model → returns `None` | N/A |
| **OOT** | No capability model → returns `None` | N/A |

### 1.2 Problem B: Same CUDA generation, different capability numbers across SKU tiers

Even within NVIDIA's own ecosystem, **the same architecture generation has different compute capability numbers** depending on the product tier (server / workstation / client):

| Platform | Device | Compute Capability | Data Types Supported |
|----------|--------|-------------------|---------------------|
| **Server** | B200 / B300 | `(10, 0)` / `(10, 3)` | bf16 / fp8 / fp4 |
| **Workstation** | RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell | `(12, 0)` | bf16 / fp8 / fp4 |
| **Client** | RTX 5090 | `(12, 0)` | bf16 only |

This is particularly problematic because:

1. **Same generation, different numbers**: B200 (`10,0`) and RTX PRO 6000 (`12,0`) are both Blackwell, both support FP8/FP4, but have completely different capability numbers. Code using `is_device_capability_family(100)` to gate Blackwell features will **miss** RTX PRO 6000.

2. **Same number, different features**: RTX PRO 6000 and RTX 5090 both report `(12,0)`, but RTX PRO supports FP8/FP4 while consumer RTX 5090 does **not**. Code using `has_device_capability(120)` to gate FP8 would be **wrong** on RTX 5090.

3. **Maintenance burden**: Every new GPU SKU tier requires auditing all numeric capability checks. The current codebase already handles `is_device_capability_family(100)` and `is_device_capability_family(120)` separately (e.g., in `cutlass_moe.py`), and this will only get worse.

### 1.3 Problem C: Cross-platform semantic mismatch

The same numeric value means **completely different things** on different platforms:

| Capability Value | CUDA Meaning | ROCm Meaning |
|-----------------|--------------|--------------|
| `(9, 0)` | Hopper (H100/H200) — FP8 ✅, TMA ✅ | MI200 (gfx90a) — FP8 ❌, BF16 only |
| `(9, 4)` | N/A | MI300 (gfx942) — FP8 ✅ (FNUZ) |
| `(9, 5)` | N/A | MI355 (gfx950) — FP8 ✅, FP4 ✅ |
| `(12, 0)` | Blackwell consumer (RTX 5090) — BF16 only | RDNA4 (gfx1201) — BF16 only |

### 1.4 Scope observation: where capability checks are used

Most usage of `has_device_capability` / `get_device_capability` falls into:

| Location | Usage Pattern | Notes |
|----------|--------------|-------|
| **tests/** and **benchmarks/** | Test skip / gating | ~60% of call sites. vLLM CI always uses NVIDIA server GPUs, so numeric checks "happen to work" but are not correct for community contributors on consumer/workstation GPUs |
| **Kernel selection code** (`model_executor/layers/`) | Dispatch to optimal kernel implementation | ~30%. Inherently platform-specific (CUTLASS, Marlin, etc.) |
| **Config / runtime** (`vllm/config/`, `vllm/v1/`) | Feature availability checks | ~10%. Should be cross-platform |

This distribution suggests the migration can be prioritized: **fix tests/config first** (highest cross-platform impact), then gradually migrate kernel dispatch code.

---

## 2. Analysis of Current Codebase

### 2.1 How capability is actually used (282 call sites)

Analyzing all `has_device_capability` / `is_device_capability*` call sites across the codebase, they fall into **three distinct categories**:

#### Category A: Testing for a *hardware feature* (~60%)

```python
# "Does this device support FP8?"
current_platform.has_device_capability(89)   # Actually means: supports_fp8()

# "Does this device support BF16?"
current_platform.has_device_capability(80)   # Actually means: supports_bf16()

# "Does this device support TMA / warp-group MMA?" 
current_platform.has_device_capability(90)   # Actually means: supports_hopper_features()

# "Does this device support Blackwell features (FP4, TMA v2)?"
current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100)  # Actually means: supports_blackwell_features()
```

These should be **feature queries**, not numeric comparisons.

#### Category B: Selecting a *kernel implementation* (~30%)

```python
# "Use CUTLASS 3.x path for SM90+"
if current_platform.has_device_capability(90): use_cutlass3()

# "Use Blackwell-specific GEMM kernel"
if current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100): use_blackwell_gemm()

# "Use CUTLASS MoE for Blackwell server OR workstation"
if p.is_device_capability_family(100) or p.is_device_capability_family(120): ...
```

These are CUDA-kernel-specific dispatch decisions. They are inherently platform-specific and **do not need** cross-platform abstraction — they are always guarded behind `is_cuda()` check already. However, even here the Blackwell SKU split causes issues (see Section 1.2).

#### Category C: FP8 weight-only quantization fallback (~10%)

```python
# fbgemm_fp8.py — Marlin WOQ fallback for non-FP8 hardware
self.use_marlin = not current_platform.has_device_capability(89)

# marlin.py — FP8 Marlin works on SM ≥ 7.5 (Turing+)
def is_fp8_marlin_supported():
    return current_platform.has_device_capability(75)
```

This pattern reveals that **FP8 "support" is not binary** — there are two distinct levels:
- **Native FP8 compute**: Hardware tensor cores that natively compute in FP8 (SM ≥ 89 on CUDA, gfx942/gfx950 on ROCm)
- **FP8 weight-only quantization (WOQ)**: Kernels like Marlin that can load FP8-quantized weights and dequantize them to FP16/BF16 for compute (works on SM ≥ 75 on CUDA, i.e., Turing+)

The current `supports_fp8()` doesn't distinguish between these, which leads to suboptimal decisions. For example, `FBGEMMFp8Config` uses `has_device_capability(89)` to decide whether to use native FP8 compute vs Marlin fallback, but this is incorrect on RTX 5090 (`(12,0)`) which has `has_device_capability(89)` = True but may not actually have native FP8 tensor cores for all operations.

### 2.2 Existing feature-level APIs (the right pattern)

The codebase already has the correct abstraction for some features:

```python
# vllm/platforms/interface.py — base class
Platform.supports_fp8()    → bool   # ✅ Cross-platform
Platform.supports_mx()     → bool   # ✅ Cross-platform
Platform.support_deep_gemm() → bool # ✅ Cross-platform
Platform.fp8_dtype()       → dtype  # ✅ Cross-platform
Platform.is_fp8_fnuz()     → bool   # ✅ Cross-platform
```

Each platform overrides these with the correct implementation:
- **CUDA**: `supports_fp8() → has_device_capability(89)`
- **ROCm**: `supports_fp8() → "gfx94" in arch or "gfx95" in arch or "gfx12" in arch`
- **XPU**: inherits `False` (or could override when XPU gains FP8)

**This is the pattern that should be expanded** — but with finer granularity (see Section 3).

### 2.3 Missing feature-level APIs

| Feature | How it's checked today | Missing `Platform` method |
|---------|----------------------|--------------------------|
| BF16 support | `has_device_capability(80)` (CUDA-only) | `supports_bf16()` |
| FP8 native compute vs WOQ | Implicit: `has_device_capability(89)` vs `has_device_capability(75)` | `supports_fp8_native()` / `supports_fp8_woq()` |
| FP4 / NVFP4 | C++ `cutlass_scaled_mm_supports_fp4()` (CUDA-only) | `supports_fp4()` |
| Hopper features (TMA, wgmma) | `has_device_capability(90)` | `supports_tma()` or architecture family check |
| Blackwell features | `is_device_capability_family(100)` — misses SM 12.0 workstation | `supports_blackwell_features()` |
| Flash attention FP8 | `has_device_capability(89)` | Covered by `supports_fp8_native()` |
| CUTLASS GEMM dispatch | `has_device_capability(75/80/89/90/100)` | Platform-specific, keep as-is |

---



### Proposed Change.

## 3. Proposal: Two-Layer Capability Model

### Layer 1: Feature-Based Queries (Cross-Platform) — **PRIMARY**

Expand the existing `Platform` base class with **semantic feature queries** that each platform implements correctly:

```python
# vllm/platforms/interface.py

class Platform:
    # === Existing (keep) ===
    def supports_fp8(cls) -> bool: ...      # keep for backward compat, alias to supports_fp8_native()
    def supports_mx(cls) -> bool: ...
    def support_deep_gemm(cls) -> bool: ...
    
    # === New feature queries ===
    
    @classmethod
    def supports_bf16(cls) -> bool:
        """Returns whether the current platform supports BF16 compute."""
        return False
    
    @classmethod
    def supports_fp8_native(cls) -> bool:
        """Returns whether the current platform has native FP8 tensor core compute.
        
        This means the hardware can natively perform matrix multiplication in FP8
        (e.g., NVIDIA SM ≥ 89 Ada/Hopper/Blackwell server, AMD gfx942/gfx950).
        Used for: native FP8 GEMM, FP8 KV cache, FP8 attention.
        """
        return False

    @classmethod
    def supports_fp8_woq(cls) -> bool:
        """Returns whether the platform supports FP8 weight-only quantization.
        
        This means kernels like Marlin can load FP8-quantized weights and 
        dequantize them to FP16/BF16 for compute. Works on significantly older
        hardware than native FP8 (e.g., NVIDIA SM ≥ 75 Turing+).
        Used for: Marlin FP8, fbgemm FP8 fallback path.
        """
        return False

    @classmethod
    def supports_fp4(cls) -> bool:
        """Returns whether the current platform supports FP4 quantization 
        (native compute or equivalent)."""
        return False

    @classmethod
    def supports_tma(cls) -> bool:
        """Returns whether the current platform supports 
        Tensor Memory Accelerator (or equivalent async copy engine)."""
        return False

    @classmethod
    def supports_fp8_kv_cache(cls) -> bool:
        """Returns whether the current platform supports FP8 KV cache."""
        return cls.supports_fp8_native()

    @classmethod
    def get_architecture_family(cls) -> str:
        """Returns human-readable architecture family name.
        
        Examples: 'hopper', 'blackwell', 'blackwell_consumer','cdna3', 
                  'rdna4', 'ponte_vecchio', 'unknown'
        """
        return "unknown"
```

### Why split FP8 into native vs WOQ?

The current `supports_fp8()` is ambiguous. In the codebase today:

```python
# fbgemm_fp8.py — decides whether to use native FP8 or Marlin fallback
self.use_marlin = not current_platform.has_device_capability(89)

# marlin_utils_fp8.py — Marlin FP8 works on much older hardware
def is_fp8_marlin_supported():
    return current_platform.has_device_capability(75)  # Turing+!
```

With the split:

```python
# fbgemm_fp8.py — clear intent
self.use_marlin = not current_platform.supports_fp8_native()

# marlin_utils_fp8.py — explicit WOQ check
def is_fp8_marlin_supported():
    return current_platform.supports_fp8_woq()
```

This distinction matters for:
- **Testing**: A test for native FP8 GEMM should use `@requires_feature("fp8_native")`, while a test for Marlin FP8 WOQ should use `@requires_feature("fp8_woq")`
- **Consumer GPUs**: RTX 5090 (`SM 12.0`) may support FP8 WOQ via Marlin but not native FP8 tensor core compute
- **ROCm**: MI200 (gfx90a) has no FP8 at all, MI300 (gfx942) has native FP8-FNUZ, different Marlin support

### Layer 2: Numeric Capability (Platform-Specific) — **KEEP BUT DEPRECATE for cross-platform use**

Keep `has_device_capability()` / `is_device_capability()` / `is_device_capability_family()` **as-is** for platform-specific kernel dispatch, but:

1. **Document** that these are CUDA/ROCm-specific and must always be guarded by `is_cuda()` / `is_rocm()`.
2. **Deprecation warning** in tests when used without platform guard (enforce via lint rule).
3. XPU/CPU/TPU continue to return `None` / `False` — this is correct behavior.
4. **For kernel dispatch**: These remain the correct API when selecting between CUDA-specific kernel implementations (e.g., CUTLASS 2.x vs 3.x). Such code is inherently platform-specific and doesn't need cross-platform abstraction.

---

## 5. Migration Plan

### Phase 0: Add feature methods to Platform (this RFC)

| Task | Effort |
|------|--------|
| Add `supports_bf16()`, `supports_fp8_native()`, `supports_fp8_woq()`, `supports_fp4()`, `supports_tma()`, `supports_wgmma()`, `get_architecture_family()`, `get_device_tier()` to base `Platform` | Small |
| Implement in `CudaPlatformBase`, `RocmPlatform`, `XPUPlatform` | Small |
| Keep `supports_fp8()` as backward-compat alias → `supports_fp8_native()` | Trivial |
| Add `requires_feature()` to `tests/utils.py` | Small |

### Phase 1: Convert feature-gated capability checks in vllm/ source

Convert ~60% of `has_device_capability` calls that are actually feature checks:

```python
# Before
if current_platform.has_device_capability(89):
    # FP8 native path
elif current_platform.has_device_capability(75):
    # FP8 Marlin WOQ fallback

# After  
if current_platform.supports_fp8_native():
    # FP8 native path
elif current_platform.supports_fp8_woq():
    # FP8 Marlin WOQ fallback
```

**Priority conversion targets** (most impactful):
- `has_device_capability(89)` → `supports_fp8_native()` (~15 sites in vllm/)
- `has_device_capability(75)` for Marlin → `supports_fp8_woq()` (~3 sites)
- `has_device_capability(80)` → `supports_bf16()` (~8 sites)
- `is_device_capability_family(100)` → `supports_fp4()` or architecture check (~20 sites)
- `not has_device_capability(89)` for `use_marlin` → `not supports_fp8_native() and supports_fp8_woq()` (~5 sites)

### Phase 2: Convert test skip patterns

Integrate with the test skip RFC (#39158) to migrate test files:

```python
# Before (CUDA-only, broken on ROCm, wrong on consumer GPUs)
@pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.has_device_capability(89), reason="need fp8")

# After (cross-platform, correct on all SKUs)
@requires_feature("fp8_native")
```

**Note**: Since vLLM CI always uses NVIDIA server GPUs, the migration can be incremental — existing tests won't break, but new tests should use the feature-based API.

### Phase 3: Lint enforcement

Add pre-commit hook to warn on new `has_device_capability` usage in test files without a `is_cuda()` / `is_rocm()` guard.

---



### Feedback Period.

1-2 weeks.

### CC List.

@tjtanaa 

### Any Other Things.

## 6. Comprehensive Device Capability Reference

### 6.1 NVIDIA CUDA — `torch.cuda.get_device_capability()`

#### Server / Data Center GPUs

| Device | Compute Capability | Architecture | BF16 | FP8 Native | FP4 | TMA |
|--------|-------------------|--------------|------|------------|-----|-----|
| GB300 / B300 | `(10, 3)` | Blackwell | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| GB200 / B200 | `(10, 0)` | Blackwell | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| H100 / H200 | `(9, 0)` | Hopper | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |
| L4 / L40 / L40S | `(8, 9)` | Ada Lovelace | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| A40 / A10 / A16 / A2 | `(8, 6)` | Ampere | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| A100 | `(8, 0)` | Ampere | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| T4 | `(7, 5)` | Turing | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| V100 | `(7, 0)` | Volta | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

#### Workstation / Pro GPUs

| Device | Compute Capability | Architecture | BF16 | FP8 Native | FP4 | TMA |
|--------|-------------------|--------------|------|------------|-----|-----|
| RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell | `(12, 0)` | Blackwell (consumer SM) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅* |
| RTX 6000 Ada | `(8, 9)` | Ada Lovelace | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| RTX A6000 / A5000 / A4000 | `(8, 6)` | Ampere | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| Quadro RTX | `(7, 5)` | Turing | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

#### Consumer / GeForce GPUs

| Device | Compute Capability | Architecture | BF16 | FP8 Native | FP4 | TMA |
|--------|-------------------|--------------|------|------------|-----|-----|
| RTX 5090/5080/5070/5060/5050 | `(12, 0)` | Blackwell (consumer SM) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌* |
| RTX 4090/4080/4070/4060 | `(8, 9)` | Ada Lovelace | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| RTX 3090/3080/3070/3060/3050 | `(8, 6)` | Ampere | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| RTX 2080/2070/2060, Titan RTX | `(7, 5)` | Turing | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

> **Key insight**: RTX PRO 6000 and RTX 5090 both report `(12, 0)`, but RTX PRO supports FP8/FP4 while consumer RTX 5090 does not. **Capability number alone is insufficient for feature detection on SM 12.0.**

### 6.2 AMD ROCm — GCN Architecture → Mapped Capability

| Device | GCN Arch | Mapped Capability | Architecture | BF16 | FP8 Native | FP4 |
|--------|----------|------------------|--------------|------|------------|-----|
| MI4xx (future) | gfx1250 | TBD | CDNA next | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| MI355 | gfx950 | `(9, 5)` | CDNA4 | ✅ | ✅ (OCP+FNUZ) | ✅ |
| MI300/MI325 | gfx942 | `(9, 4)` | CDNA3 | ✅ | ✅ (FNUZ) | ❌ |
| MI200 | gfx90a | `(9, 0)` | CDNA2 | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| Radeon (RDNA4) | gfx12xx | `(12, 0)` | RDNA4 | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
| Radeon (RDNA3) | gfx11xx | `(11, x)` | RDNA3 | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |

> **Key insight**: ROCm's `(9, 0)` = MI200 (NO FP8) vs CUDA's `(9, 0)` = Hopper (HAS FP8). The same number has opposite meanings.

### 6.3 Feature to Capability Mapping — Why Numeric Checks Fail

| Feature | CUDA Numeric Gate | Why It Fails |
|---------|------------------|--------------|
| FP8 Native | `has_device_capability(89)` | ❌ RTX 5090 is `(12,0)` ≥ `(8,9)` but has no native FP8. ROCm MI200 maps to `(9,0)` ≥ `(8,9)` but has no FP8. |
| FP4 | `is_device_capability_family(100)` | ❌ Misses RTX PRO 6000 at `(12,0)`. |
| BF16 | `has_device_capability(80)` | ⚠️ Works for CUDA server/workstation, but returns `None` on XPU (which does support BF16). |
| Blackwell features | `is_device_capability_family(100)` | ❌ Misses workstation Blackwell at `(12,0)`. Includes some non-Blackwell if future families reuse. |

- Model: DeepSeek-V4-Pro
- Configuration: tensor_parallel_size=16, enable_expert_parallel=True, speculative decoding (dspark) with 7 draft tokens, block_size=256, fp8 KV cache, CPU offloading (`OffloadingConnector`)

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Start vLLM with DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 2 nodes with the following key arguments:
   - `--block-size 256`
   - `--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"greedy"}'`
   - `--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector", ..., "kv_connector_extra_config":{"block_size":256, ...}}'`
   - `--enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill`
   - other parameters as required by the model.

2. Observe that initialisation fails with the assertion error below.
3. Setting `block_size=128` allows the server to start successfully.

**Observed behaviour:**
All workers crash during offloading connector initialisation:
```
(Worker_TP5_EP5 pid=1701) ERROR 07-17 05:59:23 [multiproc_executor.py:1004] WorkerProc hit an exception.
...
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/kv_offload/base.py", line 558, in __init__
    assert len(gpu_block_sizes) == 1, (
AssertionError: If 'block_size' is specified in kv_connector_extra_config, there must be at least one KV cache group, and all groups must have the same block size.
```

**Expected behaviour:**
Eagle (draft) groups are not managed by CPU offloading. Their `block_size` should not prevent offloading from being configured. The assertion should ignore groups marked with `is_eagle_group=True`.

candidates.title: [Bug]: MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 produces garbage output + CUDA illegal memory access on Hopper (sm90) via Marlin FP4-MoE
candidates.body:
### Summary

Serving **MiniMax-M3-NVFP4** on **Hopper GPUs (H100 / H200, sm90)** loads and starts the server, but the FP4-MoE forward pass is broken in two independent ways:

1. **Incoherent output** — every request returns garbage (null bytes / repeated-token soup) instead of real text, even at concurrency 1.
2. **CUDA illegal memory access** — the engine crashes at concurrency ≈ 8 inside `fused_marlin_moe`, killing the worker (`EngineDeadError`).

Both reproduce on the **v0.25.1 release** and on the current **nightly**. On Hopper the NVFP4-MoE selector falls back to **MARLIN** (the FlashInfer FP4 backends are Blackwell/SM100-only), and the Marlin FP4-MoE path is where both failures originate.

### Environment

- vLLM **v0.25.1** (also reproduced on a current nightly)
- GPU: **NVIDIA H200** and **H100** (Hopper, sm90)
- Model: `MiniMax-M3-NVFP4` (ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint; `hidden_act="swigluoai"`, `swiglu_limit` set)
- Selected backend (log): `Using 'MARLIN' NvFp4 MoE backend out of potential backends: ['FLASHINFER_TRTLLM', 'FLASHINFER_CUTLASS', 'MARLIN']`

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
vllm serve MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --trust-remote-code
```

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "MiniMax-M3-NVFP4",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}],
  "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 64 }'
```

**At concurrency 1:** the completion is garbage — e.g. 64× ``, or repeated-token soup like `" |,,,, | |,Cut,, Ta,,…"` — never "Paris". The same corruption appears via `/v1/completions` (no chat template), so the defect is in the forward pass, not templating.

**At concurrency ≈ 8:**

```
CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
  ... vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/marlin_moe.py
  ... vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/marlin_utils.py
EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue.
```

### Expected behavior

M3-NVFP4 serves coherent output on Hopper and remains stable across concurrency (no illegal memory access).

### Root cause

Hopper has no native FP4, so a clamped NVFP4-MoE model (M3 sets `swiglu_limit`) is routed to the **Marlin** weight-only path (enabled for non-Blackwell by #45836). That path has two independent defects for M3:

1. **Garbage output** — the Marlin MoE adapter substitutes plain-SiLU defaults instead of forwarding the model's **`swigluoai` activation parameters (alpha / beta / clamp)**. With the wrong activation the MoE output is numerically meaningless.
2. **Illegal memory access** — gated NVFP4/FP8 MoE whose **`moe_intermediate_size` is not aligned** to the Marlin kernel tile pads incorrectly, producing an out-of-bounds access under load (surfaces at concurrency ≈ 8).

The Marlin epilogue additionally mis-indexes per-row top-k weights (#48895) — the shared kernel-level defect — and M3's tile geometry is what turns it into an out-of-bounds access.

### The fix — two open PRs

Two independent fixes are needed; each addresses one symptom, and **both** are required (one alone is insufficient):

| PR | Resolves | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **#48929** | the **garbage output** | Forwards M3's `swigluoai` activation parameters (alpha / beta / clamp) to the Marlin MoE adapter, instead of substituting plain-SiLU defaults |
| **#48624** | the **illegal memory access** | Pads the gated-MoE intermediate when `moe_intermediate_size` isn't aligned to the Marlin kernel tile |

Both target `main` and are currently open. Applying both over v0.25.1 makes M3 serve coherently (correct "Paris"; correct Rayleigh-scattering explanation) and pass concurrency 8 with no illegal-memory-access, on the same MARLIN backend.

### Related

- **#48895** — Marlin `moe_wna16_marlin_gemm` mis-indexes per-row top-k weights (shared kernel-level defect)
- **#45836** — enabled Marlin-with-clamp on non-Blackwell (merged v0.24.0), which opened this path without the correctness/alignment fixes above

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Key Problem When sleep mode is enabled (and therefore custom CUDA allocators become part of the memory storage pathway), VLLM incorrectly estimates the amount of memory available for the KV cache and this can lead to OOM. ## Reproduction steps 1. Install/configure vllm (e.g., from commit bfde49e28) 2. Run the launch script below (on a dual-4090 system; may need to adapt the script to a single GPU, and, if so, use a smaller model that will fit in VRAM) 3. Observe out of memory error occurs and that launch reports "Available KV cache memory: 5.16 GiB" prior to crash" (**This estimate is incorrect and the root cause of the crash.**) 4. Run the same launch script without `--enable-sleep-mode` 5. Observe it loads correctly and that launch reports "Available KV cache memory: 3.17 GiB" (this is correct). Launch script: ```bash VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model hugging-quants/Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-AWQ-INT4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --dtype half \ --quantization awq_marlin \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --max-model-len 36000 \ --max-num-seqs 1 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 5555 \ --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --enforce-eager \ --enable-sleep-mode ``` ## Observed behavior Estimated available memory for the KV cache differs 1.99 GiB when `--enable-sleep-mode` is set (5.16 GiB) as compare to unset (3.17 GiB) ## Expected behavior Estimated available memory for the KV cache should be very similar (although perhaps not completely identical) when `--enable-sleep-mode` is set or unset. ## Underlying error and possible solution To calculate how much memory is available for the KV cache vLLM profiles memory usage (gpu_worker.py calling mem_utils.py's measure() function). The strategy vllm has been using is outlined in `MemoryShapshot.measure()`, which profiles the memory usage in terms of torch-related memory and non-torch memory. (This is because it also needs to keep track of peak torch memory, which may be transiently higher during the forward pass of a model). The strategy vllm had been using is to measure torch memory using `torch.accelerator.memory.memory_reserved`. However, there were changes accepted to enable sleep mode recently. To support sleep mode, this uses a custom CUDA allocator that allows vllm to selectively discard some parts of GPU memory during sleep. Unfortunately, when custom allocators are used, this causes the `measure()` method to over-estimate torch memory use. This is because `torch.accelerator.memory.memory_reserved` becomes an unreliable estimate of torch-related memory once custom allocaters are being used. In some cases, this estimate can exceed all CUDA memory use, causing `measure()` to incorrectly report that non-torch memory is negative. This is obviously incorrect and can lead to out of memory errors because vllm believes it has more memory to allocate to the KV cache than is truly available. I think this can be remedied by changing, within `MemoryShapshot.measure()` the estimate of torch memory to be given by: ```python stats.get("allocated_bytes.all.current", 0) ``` Where stats is: ```python stats = torch.accelerator.memory_stats(device) ``` The problem can be illustrated by observing the intermediate variables in `measure()` on one CUDA device during | Measurement | Sleep off old code | Sleep on old code | | ----------------------------------------------- | -----------------: | ----------------: | | Torch Peak | 19.73 | 19.73 | | Total memory | 23.52 | 23.52 | | Free memory | 3.98 | 4.02 | | Cuda memory | 19.54 | 19.5 | | Torch memory (old: memory_reserved) | 18.92 | **20.87 ←** | | Torch memory (new: allocated_bytes.all.current) | 18.71 | 18.71 | | Non-torch memory | 0.62 | **-1.36 ←** | Implementing this fix leads to the following result: | | Sleep off | Sleep off | Sleep on | Sleep on | | ----------------------------------- | -----------: | -----------: | -----------: | -----------: | | **Measurement (GiB)** | **Old code** | **New code** | **Old code** | **New code** | | Torch Peak | 19.73 | 19.73 | 19.73 | 19.73 | | Total memory | 23.52 | 23.52 | 23.52 | 23.52 | | Free memory | 3.98 | 3.98 | 4.02 | 4.02 | | Cuda memory | 19.54 | 19.54 | 19.5 | 19.5 | | Torch memory (old: memory_reserved) | 18.92 | 18.92 | **20.87 ←** | **20.87 ←** | | Torch memory (new: bytes_allocated) | 18.71 | 18.71 | 18.71 | 18.71 | | Non-torch memory | 0.62 | 0.83 | **-1.36 ←** | 0.79 | I will file a PR proposing this change shortly. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

candidates.title: [Bug]: #48036 auto-enables sequence-parallel MoE on TP+EP without DP — −19% throughput, −24% KV cache, and no way to opt out
candidates.body:
### Summary

#48036 removed `and self.data_parallel_size > 1` from `ParallelConfig.use_sequence_parallel_moe` (`vllm/config/parallel.py`). As a side effect, sequence-parallel MoE is now auto-enabled on **every** EP + TP deployment that has no data parallelism (`dp=1`) — a configuration it was previously never applied to.

On our TP=4 / EP / dp=1 setup this is a sizeable regression in both throughput and KV-cache capacity, and there is currently **no way to turn it off** short of switching `all2all_backend` away from the default `allgather_reducescatter`, which changes the expert-exchange mechanism entirely.

### Measurements

GLM-5.2-NVFP4 (MoE, `glm_moe_dsa`) on 4×H200, TP=4, `--enable-expert-parallel`, dp=1, DCP=4, MTP=1, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.945`, CPU KV offload on. The **only** difference between the two rows is whether `use_sequence_parallel_moe` returns True — same image, same commit, same flags:

| | GPU KV cache | N=1 | N=8 | N=32 (aggregate) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SP-MoE **off** (pre-#48036 behavior) | **1,032,448 tok** | **75 tok/s** | **407 tok/s** | **931 tok/s** |
| SP-MoE **on** (current `main`) | 784,300 tok | 61 tok/s | 353 tok/s | 875 tok/s |
| delta | **−24%** | **−19%** | **−13%** | **−6%** |

Method: 2 warm-up requests, then 3×N=1, 2×N=8, 2×N=32; 256 output tokens, `ignore_eos`, throughput = `completion_tokens / wall`. MTP acceptance length was identical (1.85–1.87) in both, so speculative decoding is not a factor.

The KV-cache loss is the more painful half for us: it directly cuts how many long sessions fit on the GPU.

### Why this configuration is not exotic

Serving one large MoE model on a single node with TP + EP and no data parallelism is a common single-replica setup — the model does not fit on one GPU, so TP is mandatory, and EP is the natural choice for the expert layers. Before #48036 such deployments simply never took the SP-MoE path; now they all do, silently, on upgrade.

### Ask

Two things would help:

1. **An explicit switch.** `use_sequence_parallel_moe` is a derived property with no override. A tri-state config (`auto` = today's heuristic, plus explicit `on`/`off`) would let deployments opt out without patching `parallel.py` or changing `all2all_backend`. Happy to send a PR for this.
2. **A second look at the heuristic itself** for the `dp=1` case: if SP-MoE reliably loses on TP-only + EP (our numbers suggest it does, at least for this model class), the auto-enable condition may want the `dp > 1` guard back, with #48036's `all_gather` fix retained (that fix is correct and orthogonal — it is what makes SP-MoE + MTP produce correct output at all).

We are currently carrying a local patch that restores the `dp > 1` guard, which is what the "SP-MoE off" row above measures.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to run the A/B and draft this report; the numbers are from real runs on our hardware.

candidates.title: benchmark_serving: throughput collapses at 50K+ context due to aiohttp read buffer and shared session
candidates.body:
## Bug: `vllm bench serve` throughput drops ~10x at long context (50K+) due to client-side bottleneck

### Summary

When running `vllm bench serve` with high concurrency at long context lengths (50K+ input tokens), throughput collapses dramatically — not because of the server, but because of the benchmark client's aiohttp session configuration.

### Evidence

We benchmarked the same server (MiniMax-M2.5, 8x RTX 6000, EP=8) with two different bench tools using identical parameters (`--random-output-len 256`, `ignore_eos=True`, same prompt sizes):

| Context (multi-user) | Tool A tok/s | vLLM bench tok/s | Tool A TTFT | vLLM bench TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8K | 503 | 494 | 1,493ms | 3,226ms |
| 32K | 591 | 640 | 790ms | 3,757ms |
| **50K** | **486** | **44** | 1,331ms | **134,173ms** |
| **100K** | **298** | **25** | 1,016ms | **97,115ms** |

At 8K/32K both tools report similar numbers. At 50K+ the vLLM bench tool collapses to ~10% throughput with TTFT exploding to 2+ minutes. **The server is identical** — this is purely a client-side measurement artifact.

### Root Cause (code analysis)

**1. aiohttp `read_bufsize` — default 64KB is too small**

`vllm/benchmarks/serve.py` creates the session with aiohttp's default `read_bufsize` (64KB):

```python
session = aiohttp.ClientSession(
    connector=connector,
    trust_env=True,
    timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=6 * 60 * 60),
)
```

At 50K+ context with many concurrent streaming requests, the server sends large chunks. The 64KB buffer fills up before the client can consume it, creating backpressure that cascades into the server's scheduling.

**2. Single shared session for all concurrent requests**

All concurrent requests share one `aiohttp.ClientSession`, meaning they compete for the same internal buffers and connection pool. This amplifies the backpressure at high concurrency with long-context responses.

### Suggested Fix

Add `read_bufsize` to the session creation in `vllm/benchmarks/serve.py`:

```python
session = aiohttp.ClientSession(
    connector=connector,
    trust_env=True,
    timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=6 * 60 * 60),
    read_bufsize=10 * 1024 ** 2,  # 10 MB — prevents backpressure at long context
)
```

### Environment

- vLLM bench: latest (cloned 2026-04-16)
- Server: MiniMax-M2.5 FP8, 8x RTX 6000 Pro Blackwell, EP=8
- Dataset: random, `--random-output-len 256`
- Multi-user: `--request-rate inf` (all at once)

### Impact

Anyone using `vllm bench serve` at long context (50K+) with high concurrency will see artificially low numbers — the bottleneck is the bench tool, not the server. This can lead to incorrect conclusions about server performance.

candidates.title: [Bug]: Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 crashes with CUDA illegal memory access on vLLM 0.11.2 (even with cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE)
candidates.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Summary When running Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 on vLLM v0.11.2, the engine crashes with: torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered deep_gemm::DGException: Assertion error: error == CUDA_SUCCESS or error == CUDA_ERROR_DEINITIALIZED This happens even when using the recommended workaround: --compilation-config {"cudagraph_mode": "PIECEWISE"} The crash occurs during generation (sample_tokens) with long sequences (~5400 tokens total). The process dies, and the API server returns EngineDeadError. This appears related but not identical to issue #28835, as the problem persists with PIECEWISE and with the FP8 variant of Qwen3-Next-80B. Environment vLLM version: v0.11.2 (vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.2 Docker image) Model: Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 GPU: NVIDIA H200 (CUDA 12.8 / 12.9) Driver: NVIDIA-SMI 580.95.05 Setup: single GPU (tensor_parallel_size=1) Docker Compose command: command: - --model - Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 - --served-model-name - Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B - --gpu-memory-utilization - "0.9" - --enable-auto-tool-choice - --tool-call-parser - hermes - --compilation-config - '{"cudagraph_mode": "PIECEWISE"}' Reproduction Steps Start vLLM with configuration above. Send a chat completion request with a long prompt (> 4500–5000 tokens) or a streaming request that produces > 1000 generated tokens. After several steps of generation, the engine crashes with an illegal memory access. Observed in real usage with: num_computed_tokens=[5457, 245] Expected Behavior vLLM should generate tokens without triggering CUDA illegal memory access, or at minimum fail gracefully without killing the engine. Actual Behavior Crash logs: torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered File ... gpu_model_runner.py line 5101: self.transfer_event.synchronize() Then: deep_gemm::DGException: Assertion error: error == CUDA_SUCCESS or error == CUDA_ERROR_DEINITIALIZED Finally: vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue The whole engine dies and must be restarted. Full stacktrace available upon request. Notes / Observations cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE does not prevent the crash. The pattern is consistent with behavior described in #28835 for inputs > 5k tokens. However: #28835 concerns the BF16 variant and long-context corruption (!!!!!), while this report concerns the FP8 variant and causes a fatal illegal memory access. The crash occurs inside: gpu_model_runner._to_list() CUDA event synchronization sometimes followed by DeepGEMM teardown errors. This might indicate: a FP8 kernel issue, or incorrect tensor shapes / offsets under long-sequence decode, or a memory lifetime problem between torch.compile + DeepGEMM + Qwen3-Next custom blocks. Questions Is this a known issue for the FP8 variant of Qwen3-Next-80B? Is there a recommended workaround besides disabling FP8? Should long-sequence (>5k tokens) support be considered unstable for this model in FP8? ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

Serve args (not covered by collect_env): ``` --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice --default-chat-template-kwargs={"thinking":true,"reasoning_effort":"high"} --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --trust-remote-code --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 262144 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 32 --attention_config.use_fp4_indexer_cache False --speculative-config={"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5} --compilation-config={"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"} ``` Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark`. `vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py` is byte-identical on current `main`, so this is not a stale-nightly artifact. ### The bug When the `deepseek_v4` reasoning parser is constructed with `thinking=true`, a response in which the model **never emits ``** has its **entire answer routed to `reasoning_content`, leaving `content` empty**. The trailing `<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>` (EOS) is also left un-stripped at the end of `reasoning_content`. The stray EOS is the visible symptom, but the misrouting is the actual bug: the user-facing answer never reaches `content`. Chat UIs render it as collapsed "thinking" text, and agents that read `message.content` receive nothing at all. Stripping the EOS alone would not fix this — it would leave the answer buried in the reasoning channel. Observed with a real client (`pi`), where a greeting rendered entirely as grey "thinking" text with no answer: ```json {"role": "assistant", "reasoning_content": "Good morning! How can I help you today?<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>", "content": ""} ``` Expected: `content` = `"Good morning! How can I help you today?"`, `reasoning_content` empty (the model did not deliberate), and no EOS in either field. ### Root cause In [`vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py#L128`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9e57de71/vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py#L128): ```python initial_state=ParserState.REASONING if thinking else ParserState.CONTENT, ``` With `thinking=true` the engine starts in `ParserState.REASONING`, and the only exit is the `THINK_END` (``) transition at [L160](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9e57de71/vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py#L160). DeepSeek-V4-Flash does not always emit `…`: on short replies it sometimes answers directly and hits EOS with no `` at all. The state machine then never leaves `REASONING`, so every chunk is emitted as `REASONING_CHUNK` and `content` stays empty. The terminal EOS is not dropped on that path either. The `initial_state` assumption holds only if the model is guaranteed to emit `` whenever thinking is enabled. It isn't — `thinking=true` gates the template/parser, not whether the model actually deliberates. I have **not** traced why the EOS specifically survives here; streaming carries real token ids, so the id-based drop would be expected to fire. Reporting that as observed rather than explained. ### Why clients hit this The parser reads `thinking` from `chat_template_kwargs` ([L220-L222](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9e57de71/vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py#L220-L222)). Any deployment setting `--default-chat-template-kwargs={"thinking":true,...}` (as the [DeepSeek-V4-Flash recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash) suggests) applies it to **every** request — including from OpenAI-compatible clients that never send `chat_template_kwargs` and have no notion of the kwarg. That is the common case for agent clients, so the server default silently puts all of their requests on the REASONING-start path. ### Reproduction Plain OpenAI-compatible streaming request, no `chat_template_kwargs` in the request (so the server default `thinking=true` applies): ```python body = { "model": "DeepSeek-V4-Flash", "stream": True, "messages": [ {"role": "system", "content": ""}, {"role": "user", "content": "good morning"}, ], } # Accumulate delta["content"] and delta["reasoning_content"] across the stream. # Misroute signature: content empty AND reasoning_content holds the answer + EOS. ``` Rates over 20-24 samples each, temperature 1.0 (the V4 default): | request | misrouted | |---|---| | agent system prompt + 50 tool defs (real client request) | 4/20 and 6/24 (~20-25%) | | same system prompt, tools removed | 2/24 | | generic short system prompt + the same 50 tool defs | 0/24 | | no system prompt (`"good morning"` alone) | 0/24 | | explicit `chat_template_kwargs={"thinking":false}` (CONTENT-start path) | 0/20 | It is sampling-dependent and provoked by a realistic agent system prompt that biases toward answering immediately; tool definitions raise the rate but do not trigger it alone. A long *synthetic* prompt (51k chars of repeated filler) did **not** reproduce it — prompt length is not the trigger, the instruction content is. That is why I can't reduce it to a self-contained prompt to paste here. Given that sampling dependence, the deterministic repro is at the parser level: construct the parser with `thinking=True` and feed it a model output containing no ``, e.g. `"Good morning! How can I help you today?<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>"`. Current behaviour routes all of it to reasoning; expected is `content`. ### Suggested fix Roughly in order of preference: 1. **Treat a response with no `` as content.** If generation ends while still in `REASONING` and no `THINK_START`/`THINK_END` was ever seen, flush the buffered reasoning to `content`. Fixes the "model didn't think" case without touching the deliberating case. 2. **Only enter `REASONING` on evidence of thinking** — keep `initial_state=CONTENT` and rely on the existing `(CONTENT, THINK_START) -> REASONING` transition. Depends on whether the chat template pre-fills an opening `` the parser never sees. 3. Independently, drop the terminal EOS on the reasoning path as is done on the content path. Happy to test a patch against this deployment and report rates back — it reproduces reliably enough at ~20-25% to validate a fix. ### Related - [#45877](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45877) — ported DeepSeek V4/V3.2 to the streaming parser engine (merged 2026-07-04). This report is against the merged code, not a regression from it. - [#46875](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46875) — general "special tokens don't leak in tool parsing" rework; does not cover this path.

milestone.title: torch==2.9.0 compilation improvements
milestone.description:
There are many improvements coming to pytorch compilation in torch 2.9. We should make sure we take advantage of all such improvements on day 0, as well as verify there aren't any additional bugs we'd have to wait until 2.10 to fix.

Some examples:
- piecewise cudagraph and fullgraph compilation compatibility
- Inductor bug fixes
- Inductor generated Triton improvements

\ --enable-dbo \ --dbo-decode-token-threshold 32 \ --kv_transfer_config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector", "kv_role":"kv_both"}' \ --max_num_seqs 256 ``` ### Original repro instructions: I'm deploying vLLM using the [llm-d WideEP well-lit-path](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/tree/007e8318525dd8fbbf8727217e1184ffdc7b8aea/guides/wide-ep-lws) See the decoder manifest here: https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/4970c7c2703dc23605719491c4fb380973b13517/guides/wide-ep-lws/manifests/modelserver/base/decode.yaml In particular this is the vLLM launch command. ``` exec vllm serve \ deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-0528 \ --port 8200 \ --disable-uvicorn-access-log \ --trust-remote-code \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --data-parallel-hybrid-lb \ --tensor-parallel-size $TP_SIZE \ --dbo-decode-token-threshold 32 \ --kv_transfer_config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector", "kv_role":"kv_both"}' ``` ### From investigations of @LucasWilkinson: the weird part is it is failing in [triton_poi_fused.to](http://triton_poi_fused.to/)_copy_add_constant_pad_nd_mean_mul_pow_rsqrt_2 and DBO isnt even running the fishy thing is torch compile appears to be rounding the input up to 4?
