candidates.title: [Roadmap]: PD Disaggregation with `NixlConnector` Roadmap
candidates.body:
## Description

This RFC tracks the current state and planned improvements for Prefill-Decode (P/D) Disaggregation using the NixlConnector, which enables high-performance KV cache transfer between prefill and decode instances using the NIXL library.


# Currently Supported Features

  Core Infrastructure

  - [x] NIXL Integration - Core P/D disaggregation framework (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/17751)

  **Async KV Cache Transfers**

  - [x] Fully asynchronous KV cache transfers
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/33377 - Bugfix for async scheduling + request abort + async KV transfer
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/28327 - Simplify async KV output aggregation
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/27648 - Async scheduling support
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/31583 - Fix resuming preempted requests after async load

  **Multi-Transport Backend Support**

  - [x] Multi-transport backend support - UCX (default), LIBFABRIC, and other NIXL plugins
    - ROCm support through RIXL library 
    - Support for OOT NIXL backends via kv_connector_extra_config (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/33552)

  **Tensor Parallelism**

  - [x] Homogeneous Tensor Parallelism - P and D instances with matching TP sizes (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/17751)
  - [x] Heterogeneous Tensor Parallelism - Support for different TP sizes between P and D
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/18833 - Base heterogeneous D TP > P TP support
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/20189 - Heterogeneous TP for FlashInfer
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/27274 - P TP > D TP support (including MLA use-case)

MLA
 - [x] Add support for MLA caches with different latent dim (Deepseek v3.2 Indexer)
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/25902

  **CPU Host Buffer Transfers**

  - [x] CPU host buffer transfers - Support for platforms without direct NIXL GPU-GPU transfer (D2H->H2D), for TPU, XPU and more.
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/18293 - Base CPU transfer support
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24690 - CUDA to CPU memory transfers
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/28356 - Pure CPU environment support

  **Heterogeneous Configurations** 
  The following also *partially* enable Hybrid hardware deployment among other use-cases. 
 - [x]  Support kernel_block_size != block_size (logical <> physical block_size mismatch)
      -  https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/30692 - 
  - [x] Heterogeneous block sizes - Different block sizes between P and D instances (cc @xuechendi )
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/26759 - Heterogeneous block_size support
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/30275 - Decoder-side post-processing for heterogeneous BlockSize
  - [x] Heterogeneous KV layout (experimental) - HND to NHD permutation via enable_permute_local_kv
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/27743 - Cross-layer KV blocks support
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/30275 - Heterogeneous layout handling

  **Reliability & Observability**

  - [x] Compatibility hash validation - Automatic P/D configuration compatibility checking
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29503 - Compatibility checking in NIXL handshake
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/30182 - Debug logging level for compatibility hash
  - [x] Transfer failure handling - Block invalidation and kv_load_failure_policy (fail/recompute)
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/32031 - Failure logging overhaul + early metadata free
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/28120 - Avoid NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT on prefill failure
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/32198 - Document fail kv_load_failure_policy
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29665 - Add remote_request_id for better tracking
  - [x] NIXL telemetry and metrics - Transfer duration, throughput, failure counters (Prometheus)
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/25388 - Expose NIXL metrics for CLI logging
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/22188 - KVTransferMetrics aggregation strategy
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/32340 - Track nixl_num_kv_expired_reqs in Prometheus
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/28309 - KV events infrastructure
  - [x] Request timeout/expiration - Automatic KV block release on P side via VLLM_NIXL_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/20139 - Remote consumer READ timeout for clearing blocks
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/32340 - Expired requests metric tracking
  - [x] Lease TTL renewals for improved freeing of kv blocks on P - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41383 (supersedes `VLLM_NIXL_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`)

  **Deployment Configurations Guides & Docs**

  - [x] Multi-instance deployments - Multiple P and D instances across hosts
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/28782 - Proxy server improvements for high concurrency
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24249 - Clearer deployment examples
  - [x] Data Parallel support - DP deployments with per-rank side channel ports
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/28782 - DP deployment documentation and proxy improvements
  - [x] Bidirectional KV Transfer - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43097
  - [x] KV Cache block Lease mechanism - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43099

Spec Decoding
   - [x] Speculative decoding integration - P/D disaggregation with speculative decoding +CI @ZhanqiuHu 
       - Fix for layer-by-layer transfer (not NIXL) https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35158
       - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35760
   - [x] HMA enabled Hybrid (SW) SD integration - example Kimi K2.5 Eagle3 see https://vllm-dev.slack.com/archives/C07RFT2UT16/p1773434620383319
      - Follows us from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35758 
   - [ ] Hybrid SSM + SD
     - [x] Qwen3.5+MTP - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42677
   - [ ] Clarify Spec Decoding compatibility matrix
   - [x] Fix PD async KV load lookahead handling for spec decode - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46694/

SSM
 - [x] NIXL+Hybrid Memory Allocator - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35758
 - [x] SSM (Mamba) support - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/34727
 - [ ] TP>1 async scheduling issue - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/37285
 - [x] Fix Mamba P/D workflow to avoid recomputing last token twice (both on P and D) - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37310
 - [x] Heterogeneous TP support for hybrid SSM models - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37635/
 - [x] Mamba1 support - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45019

#  Work in Progress
  - [ ] Avoid reading expired blocks in bidirectional turn-2 read
 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47021
  - [x] Enhanced error diagnostics - Structured logging with failure context for easier debugging
  - [ ] Enable drain scaledown mode for single process deployments - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/32420
  - [x] Speculative decoding integration - P/D disaggregation with speculative decoding +CI @ZhanqiuHu 
  - [x] CPU Offloading verification and CI tests - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39200
  - [ ] PD+CPU Offloading+Spec Decoding verification and CI tests
  - [ ] DecodeContextParallel support - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38433
  - [x] Bi-directional KV transfers with Nixl connector - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/32553
  - [x] GDN model support (Qwen3.5+) - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41869
  - [ ] Mamba prefix caching mode `align/all` - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42554 
  - [ ] Pipeline parallelism support - P/D disaggregation with pipeline parallelism https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40674 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43366
  - [x] NixlConnector Refactor:
    - [x] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39354
    - [x] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39529


  Planned
  - [ ] **Nixl + HMA support request failure handling**
  - [ ] Fix SpecDecoding asymmetric `num_speculative_tokens` UX - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43733#pullrequestreview-4370641549 (**will likely require roles to be defined at config time**)
  - [ ] Documentation improvements - Clarify PD feature matrix in docs with examples 
  - [ ] Multi-backend model support - Models with multiple attention backends (mostly validation of HMA feature coverage)
  - [ ] Hybrid hardware deployment - Supported in the measure tested by @xuechendi and team. Another AMD-Nvidia use-case reported https://uccl-project.github.io/posts/uccl-ep-full/. This is un-tested in CI and we should clarify capabilities and limitations.
  - [ ] FP8 kv cache support (attention-dependent for now, depending on how scales are stored) - Issue requesting support https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42179
  - [ ] nvfp4 kv cache support
 
  Backlog
  - [ ] HTTP-based handshake endpoint - Replace ZMQ side channel with HTTP for better observability
  - [ ] Transfer Failure handling for HMA
  - [ ] More efficient h2d `copy_blocks` operations for HMA groups
  - [ ] Heterogenous block size (blcok_size_ration > 1) HMA support

### NixlPushModeConnector
 - [x] Support "Push/WRITE" P->D mode - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35264 
 - [x] PP support for long context serving https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45880/

## RFCs
  - [x] Bi-directional KV transfers with Nixl connector - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/32733
  - [ ] Remove Per-Block KV Transfer Error Handling - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35780
  - [ ] `kv_both` role deprecation - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43807
  
### Known Issues/Bugs:
  - [x] Gemma3 heterogeneous TP accuracy drop - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/37333
  - [ ] TP-dependent block sizes break HMA heterogeneous TP  - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/41037
  - [ ] Bidirectional KV transfer produces incorrect results when reasoning traces are stripped between turns - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43094
  - [ ] PD+SD Prefix-cache trimming drops wrong block when P has extra lookahead block - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43996

### Bug Fixes
 - [x] Fix NIXL handshake failures not honoring  `kv_load_failure_policy` - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/33745
 - [ ] Fix multi-node TP (TP>8) - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39907
 - [ ] Fix CG dispatch for mamba PD to FULL_DECODE - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42430

###  Related Projects

  - Encoder-Prefill-Decode Disaggregation: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/25233
  - Mooncake Transfer Engine: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24718, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/31573

### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Describe the bug When serving **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** with the DeepSeek V4 parser stack enabled, responses are structurally correct under **sequential** load, but under **concurrent** load a subset of responses contain malformed parser output: unbalanced `` / `` tags, leaked reasoning/thinking markers in `content`, and occasionally raw malformed DSML / special-token fragments (e.g. `<|im_start|>`, `<|im_end|>`, nested `invoke name=` without proper closing). This appears to be a **concurrency-dependent parser/state-machine issue**, not a deterministic single-request DSML argument-parsing bug. It is **not** the same issue as #41240 (fixed in #41801): that issue was about DSML parameter semantics (`string="true|false"`, `arguments`/`input` unwrapping, end-of-stream flush) and does not require concurrent load to reproduce. #### Environment - **vLLM version**: `0.24.0` - **Model**: DeepSeek-V4-Flash (`served-model-name: DeepSeek_v4`) - **GPU**: 8× H100 - **Server flags**: ```bash --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --block-size 256 \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --max_num_seqs 32 \ --max-model-len 1000000 ``` #### Current behavior - **Sequential baseline (concurrency=1)**: 0% corruption rate (20/20 requests clean). - **Concurrent load (concurrency≥16)**: corruption appears in a non-trivial fraction of requests. - Observed failure modes include: - Unbalanced structural tags, e.g. `[UNBALANCED TAG] open=1 close=0` - Truncated / nested DSML tool-call markup left in the response body - Raw special tokens leaking into user-visible text, e.g. `<|im_start|>`, `<|im_end|>` - Reasoning/thinking content appearing in `content` instead of being fully separated into `reasoning_content` - **No cross-request content contamination** was detected (unique per-request markers never leaked across responses), so this does not look like KV-cache cross-talk between requests. - Server logs showed **no** obvious `Preempt` / `recompute` / error spikes during the runs. #### Reproduction matrix Each scenario is a timed soak test with long context (~8000 filler tokens), streaming enabled unless noted, and optional multi-turn tool-call loops. | Scenario | Concurrency | Tools | Stream | Rounds | Requests | Severe rate | Total corrupt rate | Cross-contam | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | baseline_sequential | 1 | yes | yes | 3 | 20 | 0.0% | 0.0% | 0 | | concurrency_16 | 16 | yes | yes | 3 | 181 | 2.8% | 9.4% | 0 | | concurrency_24 | 24 | yes | yes | 3 | 238 | 2.9% | 9.7% | 0 | | concurrency_40 (> max_num_seqs) | 40 | yes | yes | 3 | 253 | 1.2% | 9.5% | 0 | | concurrency_24_rounds6 | 24 | yes | yes | 6 | 174 | 2.3% | 13.2% | 0 | | concurrency_24_rounds8 | 24 | yes | yes | 8 | 152 | 4.0% | 16.4% | 0 | | concurrency_24_no_tools | 24 | **no** | yes | 1 | 151 | 0.7% | **29.8%** | 0 | | concurrency_24_no_stream | 24 | yes | **no** | 3 | 235 | 2.5% | 9.4% | 0 | Key observations from the matrix: 1. **Strong concurrency correlation**: 0% at c=1 vs up to 29.8% under concurrent load. 2. **Multi-turn accumulation**: at c=24, corrupt rate rises from 9.7% (3 rounds) to 16.4% (8 rounds). 3. **`reasoning_parser` is also affected**: disabling tools (`no_tools`) increases corrupt rate to 29.8%, so this is not limited to `tool_call_parser`. 4. **Non-streaming is also affected**: `no_stream` still shows ~9.4% corrupt rate, so streaming-only end-of-stream flush issues (as in #41240) do not explain the full behavior. #### Example corrupted output **Example 1** — nested / unclosed DSML tool calls (`concurrency_24`, req idx=86): ``` ... \n open=1 close=0` **Example 2** — mixed DSML formats, truncated mid-tag (`concurrency_24_rounds8`, req idx=105): ``` <｜DSML｜invoke name="search_file"> <｜DSML｜parameter name="keyword" string="true">短文 ... <｜DSML｜invoke na ``` **Example 3** — raw special tokens in content without tools (`concurrency_24_no_tools`, req idx=94): ``` ...两阶段提交（Two-Phase Commit，简称2PC）。 ... 如果操作失败，回复"中止" ``` Detected hits: `<|im_end|>`, `<|im_start|>` #### Expected behavior Under concurrent load, each request should receive the same structurally valid, parser-clean output as in the sequential baseline: - `content` and `reasoning_content` should remain properly separated. - No unbalanced `` / `` / thinking tags in the returned text. - No raw DSML fragments or bare special tokens (`<|...|>`) in user-visible fields. - Parser behavior should be **per-request isolated** and not degrade as concurrency or multi-turn depth increases. #### How to reproduce ```bash pip install openai --break-system-packages python vllm_corruption_matrix_bench.py \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:11111/v1 \ --model DeepSeek_v4 \ --duration-per-scenario 120 ``` Attachments: - `vllm_corruption_matrix_bench.py` — matrix soak harness with corruption / cross-contamination detectors - `raw_.jsonl` — per-scenario raw responses - Full report: `bench_results/vllm_repro_report.md` #### Relation to existing issues This is **not** a duplicate of #41240 / #41801. That fix addressed deterministic DSML argument parsing semantics. This report shows: - reproduction requires **concurrency** (0% sequential vs 9–30% concurrent), - **`reasoning_parser` fails even without tools**, - **non-streaming path is also affected**, - failures are **structural tag/markup corruption**, not incorrect tool-argument coercion. [vllm_corruption_matrix_bench.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29835933/vllm_corruption_matrix_bench.py) [vllm_corruption_matrix_bench.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29835948/vllm_corruption_matrix_bench.py) [raw_concurrency_24.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29835980/raw_concurrency_24.zip) ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

When the enforce_eager parameter is set to False, an anomalous behavior was observed where the service intermittently produced incorrect results for the initial query in certain operational contexts.

**Problem Description**
- In serial request scenarios involving single-data inputs, regardless of the total number of requests issued, the first request consistently returned erroneous outputs (refer to Figure for visual representation).
- When executing concurrent requests with single-data payloads, instances of incorrect outputs occurred randomly, with a significantly elevated frequency compared to serial execution.
- Restoration of normal functionality was observed for both serial and concurrent request scenarios when the enforce_eager parameter was set to True.
- This phenomenon was reproducibly observed across both online service deployments and offline engine testing environments.

**Problem Analysis**
A working hypothesis suggests that the instability may be attributed to the CUDA Graph's computational behavior during the initial capture of tensors with specific geometric configurations.

### 🐛 Describe the bug On AMD MI355X GPUs (gfx950), vLLM with prefix caching enabled produces **different output on the first request vs subsequent identical requests**. The first request (cache miss -> full prefill) returns a different result than subsequent requests (cache hit -> partial prefill with cached KV). This does **not** occur on AMD MI325X. ### Environment - **GPU**: AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) - **vLLM Version**: Current upstream (0.14.0rc2.dev293+g4561f1398.d20260125.rocm700) - **Model**: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B ### Bug Description When prefix caching is enabled on MI355X, the **first request computes attention from scratch** (no cached KV to reuse), while **subsequent identical requests reuse the cached KV prefix**. These two computation paths produce numerically different results on MI355X, causing the first request's output to differ from all subsequent requests. | Request | Cache Status | Computation Path | Output | |---------|--------------|------------------|--------| | Run 1 | ❌ Cache miss | Full prefill | `'The European Union consists of 27 member states'` | | Run 2 | ✅ Cache hit | Partial prefill + cached KV | `'The European Union (EU) consists of **2'` | | Run 3 | ✅ Cache hit | Partial prefill + cached KV | `'The European Union (EU) consists of **2'` | | Run 4+ | ✅ Cache hit | Partial prefill + cached KV | `'The European Union (EU) consists of **2'` | On MI325X, both computation paths produce identical outputs. ### Visual Comparison #### ✅ MI325X (Working Correctly) ``` vLLM+PC Run 1: 'The European Union (EU) consists of **2' vLLM+PC Run 2: 'The European Union (EU) consists of **2' vLLM+PC Run 3: 'The European Union (EU) consists of **2' vLLM+PC Run 4: 'The European Union (EU) consists of **2' vLLM+PC Run 5: 'The European Union (EU) consists of **2' ``` All runs identical ✓ #### ❌ MI355X (Bug Present) ```diff - vLLM+PC Run 1: 'The European Union consists of 27 member states' ← (DIFFERENT!) + vLLM+PC Run 2: 'The European Union (EU) consists of **2' + vLLM+PC Run 3: 'The European Union (EU) consists of **2' + vLLM+PC Run 4: 'The European Union (EU) consists of **2' + vLLM+PC Run 5: 'The European Union (EU) consists of **2' ``` **First request (cache miss) produces different output than cache-hit requests!** ### Root Cause On MI355X, the two attention computation paths diverge numerically: 1. **Full prefill** (no cached KV): Computes attention over entire sequence from scratch 2. **Partial prefill + cached KV**: Loads cached KV for prefix, computes only for new tokens These paths should be numerically equivalent but aren't on MI355X. The divergence is large enough to change the argmax token selection at position 3, causing completely different output sequences. **Token divergence point:** | Position | Cache Miss (Run 1) | Cache Hit (Run 2+) | |----------|--------------------|--------------------| | 0 | `'The'` | `'The'` | | 1 | `' European'` | `' European'` | | 2 | `' Union'` | `' Union'` | | 3 | **`' consists'`** 🔴 | **`' ('`** 🔴 | | 4 | `' of'` | `'EU'` | | 5+ | (diverged) | (diverged) | ### Key Evidence | Test | MI325X | MI355X | |------|--------|--------| | vLLM+PC: Run 1 == Run 2 | ✅ Yes | ❌ **No** | | vLLM-PC: All runs identical | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | | vLLM-PC Run 1 == vLLM+PC Run 1 | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | | vLLM-PC Run 1 == vLLM+PC Run 2 | ✅ Yes | ❌ **No** | This confirms the bug is specifically in the **cache-hit path** on MI355X. ### Reproduction
📋 Test Script (It's a new file - you have to create it) ```python """ Comprehensive test to diagnose prefix caching determinism issues on gfx950. Run with: pytest -v -s test_prefix_cache_debug.py """ import subprocess import pytest import pytest_asyncio import httpx import torch from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM from tests.utils import RemoteOpenAIServer MODEL_NAME = "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B" GEN_ENDPOINT = "/inference/v1/generate" def get_hf_reference(tokenizer, messages, use_cache=True, num_runs=1): """ Generate reference output using HuggingFace directly. Now captures top-5 logprobs for each position. """ cache_str = "WITH" if use_cache else "WITHOUT" print(f"\n{'='*80}") print(f"GENERATING HUGGINGFACE REFERENCE ({cache_str} KV CACHE)") print(f"{'='*80}") model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained( MODEL_NAME, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="auto", ) model.eval() token_ids = tokenizer.apply_chat_template( messages, add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=False, ) print(f"Input tokens: {len(token_ids)}") print(f"use_cache: {use_cache}") input_ids = torch.tensor([token_ids], device=model.device) results = [] for run_idx in range(num_runs): with torch.no_grad(): outputs = model.generate( input_ids, max_new_tokens=10, do_sample=False, return_dict_in_generate=True, output_scores=True, use_cache=use_cache, ) generated_ids = outputs.sequences[0, len(token_ids):].tolist() # Get top-5 logprobs for each generated token top5_logprobs = [] logprobs = [] for i, scores in enumerate(outputs.scores): log_probs = torch.log_softmax(scores[0], dim=-1) # Get top 5 top5_values, top5_indices = torch.topk(log_probs, k=5) top5_list = [ {'token_id': idx.item(), 'logprob': val.item(), 'token': tokenizer.decode([idx.item()])} for val, idx in zip(top5_values, top5_indices) ] top5_logprobs.append(top5_list) # Also store the logprob of the actual generated token token_id = generated_ids[i] logprobs.append(log_probs[token_id].item()) decoded = tokenizer.decode(generated_ids, skip_special_tokens=True) results.append({ 'run': run_idx + 1, 'tokens': generated_ids, 'logprobs': logprobs, 'top5_logprobs': top5_logprobs, 'decoded': decoded, }) print(f" Run {run_idx + 1}: '{decoded}'") if run_idx == 0: print(f" Tokens: {generated_ids}") print(f" Logprobs: {[f'{lp:.6f}' for lp in logprobs]}") # Check determinism across runs if num_runs > 1: all_same = all( tuple(r['tokens']) == tuple(results[0]['tokens']) for r in results ) print(f"\n HF Determinism ({num_runs} runs): {'✓ All same' if all_same else '✗ Differs'}") print(f"{'='*80}\n") # candidates.title: [Bug]: disable_flashinfer_q_quantization + fp8 KV + spec decode silently corrupts sliding-window models on SM100 (trtllm-gen); BF16-Q paths also mis-apply q/k/v scales
candidates.body:
### Your current environment

vLLM nightly `0.23.1rc1.dev843+g04adc8843` (relevant code identical on current `main`), flashinfer-python 0.6.14 (latest) + flashinfer-cubin 0.6.13, torch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13, 1× NVIDIA B200 (SM100).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Combination:** `--attention-backend FLASHINFER` + `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` + `--attention-config '{"disable_flashinfer_q_quantization": true}'` (BF16 query) + speculative decoding, on SM100, serving a **sliding-window** model (gemma-4-31B, 50/60 layers SWA window 1024).

**Symptom:** silently corrupted output — sporadic wrong tokens and short repetition loops in otherwise coherent generations, e.g. on a temp-0 summarization request:

> "...a Saga breaks a transaction into a sequence of a sequence of a sequence of local transactions..."
> "#### This implementation analysis of the an this Python API Gateway reveals several critical..."

With deeper speculation (k=64 suffix decoding) the same combination degenerates into full runaway repetition.

Attribution matrix (all temp-0, same prompts, gemma-4-31B NVFP4 + MTP `num_speculative_tokens=7`):

| config | output |
|---|---|
| fp8-Q (flag off), spec on | clean |
| bf16-Q (flag on), **no spec** | clean |
| bf16-Q (flag on), spec on, `-O3` cudagraphs | corrupted |
| bf16-Q (flag on), spec on, `--enforce-eager` | corrupted (not a cudagraph issue) |

**Root cause (kernel level):** flashinfer's trtllm-gen spec-as-decode kernel (`trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache`, `q_len_per_req=8`) with BF16-Q + FP8-KV mis-computes sliding-window attention once `seq_len > window` at certain seq_len/page alignments — errors up to ~1.8 confined to single (query-row, head) pairs, while FP8-Q / no-window / q_len≤4 controls on identical inputs are clean. Standalone repro + characterization filed at flashinfer-ai/flashinfer: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3864. vLLM routes spec-decode verify onto exactly this kernel when the flag is set (`use_trtllm_attention` forces trtllm for decode when `has_spec`), so the flag currently turns a supported-looking configuration into silent corruption for any SWA model.

Suggested action until the kernel is fixed: reject or warn on `disable_flashinfer_q_quantization=True` + quantized KV + speculative decoding + sliding-window layers on SM100.

### Secondary (independent) issue: q/k/v scales mis-applied on the BF16-Q paths

While reproducing this we found the BF16-Q scale bookkeeping in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py` is wrong whenever the checkpoint carries calibrated attention scales (inert for the common `_q_scale = _k_scale = _v_scale = 1.0` case, which is why it does not show up in the repro above):

1. `FlashInferImpl.forward` computes
   ```python
   self.bmm1_scale = self.scale
   if is_quantized_kv_cache(self.kv_cache_dtype):
       self.bmm1_scale *= layer._q_scale_float * layer._k_scale_float
   ```
   unconditionally — `_q_scale_float` is applied even when `disable_flashinfer_q_quantization` keeps Q in BF16 (no quantization happened, so there is nothing to de-scale). The XQA helper right above it (`get_xqa_bmm1_scale`) already implements the correct conditional ("only include q_scale when the decode query is actually FP8") — but it is only used for the XQA decode path, not for trtllm-gen decode or trtllm prefill.

2. The BF16-Q + FP8-KV trtllm **prefill** path dequantizes the KV cache into a BF16 mock cache using `layer._k_scale` / `layer._v_scale` (`trtllm_prefill_attn_kvfp8_dequant`) and then still passes `bmm1_scale = sm_scale * q_scale * k_scale` and `bmm2_scale = v_scale` to `trtllm_batch_context_with_kv_cache` — k/v scales get applied twice (and q_scale once too many) for calibrated checkpoints.

### Repro (serve level)

```bash
vllm serve RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-NVFP4 \
  --served-model-name gemma-4-31b \
  --attention-backend FLASHINFER \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"google/gemma-4-31B-it-assistant","method":"mtp","quantization":"fp8","num_speculative_tokens":7}' \
  --hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"use_bidirectional_attention":null}}' \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 1536 --enforce-eager \
  --attention-config '{"disable_flashinfer_q_quantization": true}'
```

then send any ~1k-token chat completion at temperature 0 and generate a few hundred tokens (the corruption needs `seq_len` to run past the 1024-token sliding window; short prompts stay clean). Drop the `--attention-config` line → clean output; drop the `--speculative-config` line (keeping the flag) → clean output.

### Your current environment


- vLLM version: v0.19.0 (also reproduced on `vllm/vllm-openai:gemma4-x86_64-cu130`)
- GPU: 8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (96GB GDDR7, SM 12.0)
- OS: Linux 5.15.0-171-generic
- CUDA: 13.0
- Python: 3.12
- Docker image: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.19.0-x86_64-cu130-ubuntu2404` (with `transformers>=5.5.0` installed for Gemma 4 support)

## Model

`google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` (Mixture-of-Experts, 25.2B total params, 3.8B active, 128 experts with 8 active per token)

## Command

```bash
vllm serve google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it \
  --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --quantization fp8 \
  --max-model-len 25600 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --trust-remote-code
```

GPUs assigned: 2 GPUs (device IDs 6 and 7).



### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Description

Gemma 4 MoE model crashes at runtime when `--data-parallel-size` is set to anything greater than 1. The model loads weights successfully, captures CUDA graphs, and starts API servers — but fails on the **first inference request** with an `AssertionError` inside the expert-parallel all-gather communication path.

This was also reproduced with `--quantization mxfp4` (which crashes earlier during weight loading) and `--quantization fp8` (crashes on first request after successful load).

**DP=1 works perfectly.** The issue is specific to DP > 1 with MoE models.

Dense models (e.g., `google/gemma-4-E4B-it`, `google/gemma-4-31B-it`) work fine with DP > 1.

## Error traceback

### Phase 1: Weight loading (with `--quantization mxfp4`)

When using `--quantization mxfp4`, the crash occurs during weight loading:

```
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/layer.py", line 1073, in weight_loader
    dim2 = loaded_weight.shape[2]
IndexError: tuple index out of range
```

This is covered by existing issues #35329 and #35324.

### Phase 2: Runtime crash (with `--quantization fp8`)

With `fp8`, weights load successfully and CUDA graphs are captured. The crash occurs on the first inference request:

```
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/cuda_communicator.py", in _all_gather_single
AssertionError: 1 != 36
```

The all-gather operation in the MoE expert dispatch expects a tensor dimension matching `sizes[rank]` (36 tokens) but receives 1. This suggests the MoE dispatch layer is incorrectly routing through expert-parallelism communication paths when running under data parallelism, causing a tensor shape mismatch between DP workers.

## Root cause analysis

The MoE fused expert layer appears to assume that multiple GPUs = expert parallelism (EP), triggering inter-GPU all-gather operations for expert routing. Under data parallelism, each GPU should run an independent full copy of the MoE model with no cross-GPU expert communication. The DP workers seem to be initializing with EP-style communication, leading to the shape assertion failure.

## Workaround

Run separate container instances, each with `--data-parallel-size 1` on its own GPU, with an external load balancer (e.g., Caddy, nginx) distributing requests round-robin across them. This provides effective data parallelism without triggering the MoE dispatch bug.

## Related issues

- #18567 — Single-node data parallel crash (general DP crash, not MoE-specific)
- #35329 — `quantization="mxfp4"` produces incorrect results for MoE at TP=1
- #35324 — FusedMoE.weight_loader MXFP4 crashes on standard HF MoE checkpoints
- #33014 — LoRA loading fails with Fused MoE when DP > 1


### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

candidates.body:
### Your current environment


- vLLM version: v0.19.0
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (96GB GDDR7, SM 12.0)
- OS: Linux 5.15.0-171-generic
- CUDA: 13.0
- Python: 3.12
- Docker image: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.19.0-x86_64-cu130-ubuntu2404` (with `transformers>=5.5.0`)

## Model

`google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` (MoE, 128 experts, 8 active per token)

## Command

```bash
vllm serve google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --quantization mxfp4 \
  --max-model-len 25600 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --trust-remote-code
```


### 🐛 Describe the bug

Runtime MXFP4 quantization (`--quantization mxfp4`) crashes during weight loading for the Gemma 4 MoE model, even with `--data-parallel-size 1`. The fused MoE weight loader at `layer.py:1073` attempts to access `loaded_weight.shape[2]`, but the weight tensor is 2D, not 3D, causing an `IndexError`.

This is effectively the same class of bug as #35329 and #35324, but specifically reproduced with `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` (Gemma 4 MoE). Filing separately because:

1. Those issues focus on other MoE architectures (DeepSeek, Qwen, Mixtral).
2. Gemma 4 MoE is a new model with a unique expert architecture (128 experts, 8 active) that may require specific attention in the weight loader.
3. The `mxfp4` quantization method is the recommended replacement for the deprecated `petit_nvfp4`, so it's critical that it works with newly released MoE models.

## Error traceback

```
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/layer.py", line 1073, in weight_loader
    dim2 = loaded_weight.shape[2]
IndexError: tuple index out of range
```

The weight tensor loaded from the Gemma 4 MoE checkpoint is 2D `(out_features, in_features)`, but the MXFP4 branch of `weight_loader` expects a 3D tensor `(num_experts, out_features, in_features)`. The MXFP4 quantization path doesn't reshape the weights before accessing the expert dimension.

## Expected behavior

`--quantization mxfp4` should correctly quantize Gemma 4 MoE weights at load time, producing a functional model with FP4 weights and FP16/BF16 compute.

## Actual behavior

Crash during weight loading with `IndexError: tuple index out of range`.

## Impact

There is currently **no working FP4 runtime quantization path for Gemma 4 MoE** in vLLM:

| Method | Status |
|---|---|
| `nvfp4` | Removed (unknown method error) |
| `petit_nvfp4` | Deprecated, crashes with deprecation error |
| `mxfp4` | Crashes during weight loading (this bug) |
| `fp8` | Works (2x compression, not 4x) |

For memory-bandwidth-limited hardware (e.g., GDDR7-based Blackwell RTX), FP4 quantization provides significant throughput improvements over FP8. The inability to use any FP4 quantization with the MoE model is a meaningful limitation.

## Workaround

Use `--quantization fp8` as a fallback. This provides 2x bandwidth savings over BF16 instead of the 4x that FP4 would offer.

For pre-quantized FP4, the **dense** model `nvidia/Gemma-4-31B-IT-NVFP4` with `--quantization modelopt` works correctly. However, there is no pre-quantized FP4 checkpoint available for the MoE variant that loads successfully with vLLM.

## Related issues

- #35329 — `quantization="mxfp4"` produces incorrect results / hangs for MoE models at TP=1
- #35324 — FusedMoE.weight_loader MXFP4 branch crashes on standard HuggingFace MoE checkpoints

candidates.title: [Bug]: GPT-OSS-120B gpt-oss MXFP4 on SM121 (Blackwell DGX Spark): Marlin kernel generates wrong first Harmony token, producing null content/reasoning

labels.name: unstale
labels.description: Recieved activity after being labelled stale

candidates.body:
### Environment

- **vLLM Version**: 0.16.0rc2.dev559+g4bf19f9bf
- **CUDA**: 13.0
- **GPU**: NVIDIA B200 / DGX Spark (SM121)
- **Model**: openai/gpt-oss-120b

**Server command:**
```bash
vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-120b \
  --quantization mxfp4 \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-model-len 2048 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.70 \
  --max-num-seqs 2 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --load-format fastsafetensors
```

---

### 🐛 Bug Description

When serving `openai/gpt-oss-120b` with MXFP4 quantization on a **single SM121 GPU** (NVIDIA B200 / DGX Spark), all chat completions return `content: null` and `reasoning: null` despite `completion_tokens` showing that tokens were generated.

**Request:**
```python
client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-oss-120b",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What is 2+2?"}],
    max_tokens=512,
)
```

**Response:**
```json
{
  "choices": [{
    "message": {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": null,
      "reasoning": null,
      "tool_calls": []
    },
    "finish_reason": "length"
  }],
  "usage": {
    "prompt_tokens": 74,
    "completion_tokens": 512,
    "total_tokens": 586
  }
}
```

512 tokens were generated but none surfaced as content or reasoning.

---

### Root Cause

**The Harmony prompt rendered for `gpt-oss-120b` ends with:**
```
<|start|>assistant        (tokens: 200006, 173781)
```

The model must generate `<|channel|>` (token **200005**) as its first completion token to begin a valid Harmony channel header (`<|channel|>analysis<|message|>...`).

**Instead, on SM121 with MXFP4 + Marlin fallback, the model generates token `181886` = `'farbe'` (German: "color") — a completely wrong non-Harmony text token.**

Verified via `return_token_ids: true`:
```json
"prompt_token_ids": [..., 200006, 173781],
"token_ids":        [181886, 87, 314, ...]
```

Decoded: `'farbex = 0.5\nWe need to produce the next token...'`

The Harmony `StreamableParser` immediately raises `HarmonyError` on token 181886 because it expects `<|start|>` (200006) or `<|channel|>` (200005), not a regular text token. The parser returns an empty result → `reasoning: null`, `content: null`.

**Server log evidence (before HarmonyError fix):**
```
HarmonyError during output parsing, returning partial result:
  Unexpected token 63248 while expecting start token 200006
```

---

### Why This Happens

SM121 (Blackwell) does **not** have native hardware FP4 support. The vLLM server logs confirm:

```
WARNING: Your GPU does not have native support for FP4 computation but FP4
quantization is being used. Weight-only FP4 compression will be used
leveraging the Marlin kernel. This may degrade performance for compute-heavy
workloads.
```

The `csrc/quantization/gptq_marlin/` directory contains only SM80-targeted kernels:
```
sm80_kernel_bfloat16_fe2m1f_bfloat16.cu
sm80_kernel_bfloat16_fe4m3fn_bfloat16.cu
...
```

No SM121-specific Marlin kernels exist. The SM80 Marlin MXFP4 kernel running on SM121 produces incorrect logits for the first assistant token, causing the model to sample a garbage text token instead of the Harmony control token `<|channel|>`.

---

### Relationship to Existing Issues

- **#31422** ([Bug]: SM120/SM100: gpt-oss gibberish with tp=2) — related but different: that issue is TP=2 + prefix caching. This bug reproduces on **single GPU, tp=1**, with prefix caching enabled or disabled.

---

### Secondary Bug: System Message Causes Hallucinated Reasoning

A second bug causes the model to produce hallucinated/off-topic reasoning when a **system message** is included in the request. With the broken prompt, the model sometimes generates tokens in the `analysis` channel, but the content is completely wrong (e.g., discussing Codeforces problems when asked "What is 2+2?", or outputting Russian/Unicode characters).

**Root cause:** `_make_request_with_harmony` was passing system-role messages directly to `parse_chat_inputs_to_harmony_messages`, which does not handle the `system` role in Harmony encoding format. The raw system tokens corrupt the Harmony token sequence, misdirecting the model's reasoning.

This is fixed in the linked PR.

---

### Steps to Reproduce

1. SM121 GPU (NVIDIA B200/DGX Spark)
2. Start vLLM with `openai/gpt-oss-120b --quantization mxfp4`
3. Send any chat completion request
4. Observe: `content: null`, `reasoning: null`, `finish_reason: length`
5. Enable `return_token_ids: true` — first completion token is not `200005` (`<|channel|>`)

---

### Expected Behavior

First completion token should be `200005` (`<|channel|>`), followed by valid Harmony channel content, producing non-null `reasoning` and/or `content`.

---

### Proposed Fix

Add SM121-targeted Marlin MXFP4 kernels in `csrc/quantization/gptq_marlin/` or route SM121 through FlashInfer's native MXFP4 path (if supported) rather than the SM80 Marlin fallback.

---

### Workaround

Remove `--quantization mxfp4` and use `--dtype bfloat16` (unquantized). This avoids the Marlin kernel entirely. Note: 120B model in bfloat16 requires ~240 GB VRAM.

The model's grounding capabilities (spatial understanding and object localization) show significant precision degradation compared to previous vLLM versions. The model produces incorrect bounding box coordinates and poor spatial reasoning results. ### Reproduction Deploy Code ``` nohup python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --model Qwen/Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct-FP8 --served-model-name qwen3-vl-235b-a22b-instruct --max-model-len 64K --tensor-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 --trust-remote-code --max-num-seqs 16 --dtype bfloat16 --enable-log-requests --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --async-scheduling --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --enable-expert-parallel --limit-mm-per-prompt.video 0 --mm_encoder_tp_mode="data" --mm_processor_cache_type="shm" & ``` ### Expected Behavior - Accurate bounding box coordinates ([x1, y1, x2, y2] format) - Precise spatial relationship descriptions - Consistent object localization ### Actual Behavior (vLLM 0.11.1/0.11.2) - Incorrect or invalid bounding box coordinates - Poor spatial reasoning accuracy - Inconsistent grounding results compared to vLLM 0.11.0 or direct Hugging Face implementation ### vllm 0.11.1/0.11.2 Grounding ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aa8c4dd9-a3e0-4c26-be9d-b18c6739d94d) vllm 0.11.0 Grounding ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e126168c-b635-40bf-b8ed-46b5b68bd0a9) The issue is reproducible with both FP8 quantization and standard precision ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

candidates.title: [Performance]: [Fused MoE] BLOCK_SIZE_K=128 decode default causes large slowdown on Volta/V100
candidates.body:
### Proposal to improve performance

I am filing this as a performance discussion rather than a bug report because V100 / `sm_70` is not a primary target for current vLLM wheels. The useful upstream part is a measured fused-MoE default/config finding that affects the V100-relevant vLLM line.

The focus is vLLM 0.19, because that is the last broadly practical vLLM line for Tesla V100 users. I also verified the same fused-MoE default shape in my 0.21 source-build path, but I am not asking vLLM to restore V100 wheel support here.

Summary:

1. **Finding**
   - On Tesla V100 / Volta (`sm_70`), the fused-MoE decode/small-M path using `BLOCK_SIZE_K=128` is much slower than expected.
   - The practical symptom is that FP16/BF16 sparse MoE decode can become slower than dense models of similar class.
   - This is not the hardware limit itself; it is a bad fallback/default for Volta.

2. **Measured fix**
   - For small-M decode on Volta, changing the MoE tile to `BLOCK_SIZE_K=64` removes the pathology.
   - In my A/B tests, output remained bit-identical.
   - This is a speed/config fix, not an approximation.

3. **Suggested upstream path**
   - If vLLM is willing to accept V100 config data, I can provide tuned config JSONs for Tesla V100.
   - I am not proposing an sm_70 support-policy change.
   - If heuristic code for sm_70 is not in scope, the data/config contribution may still be useful.

The main question for maintainers:

Would vLLM accept V100 fused-MoE config JSONs / performance data for the 0.19-era Volta path, or is this better kept as external documentation only?

### Report of performance regression

Environment:

- Hardware: 8x NVIDIA Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB
- Architecture: Volta / `sm_70`
- Main vLLM focus: vLLM 0.19.x, because this is the last broadly practical V100 line
- Also checked: vLLM 0.21 source-build path on CUDA 12.6
- Toolchain: CUDA 12.6 / cu126 source builds
- Serving mode: cudagraph decode

Observed symptom:

On V100, FP16/BF16 MoE decode with the stock fused-MoE default can be slower than dense models of similar class. This is backwards for sparse MoE decode, where only a small active subset of experts should move per token.

Measured examples on the same 8x V100 box:

| Model | Stock FP16 MoE | Patched/tuned MoE | Improvement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, C1 | ~15.6 tok/s | ~65.9 tok/s | ~4.2x |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, C8 aggregate | ~24.9 tok/s | ~173.9 tok/s | ~7.0x aggregate |
| Gemma-4-26B-A4B, C1 | ~10.9 tok/s | ~43.7 tok/s | ~4.0x |
| Gemma-4-26B-A4B, C8 aggregate | ~28.3 tok/s | ~155.9 tok/s | ~5.5x aggregate |

Root-cause summary:

- The initial suspect was `num_stages`, because Volta lacks `cp.async`.
- Sweeping `num_stages` did not explain the slowdown.
- The real lever was `BLOCK_SIZE_K`.
- The decode/small-M path using `BLOCK_SIZE_K=128` spills badly on Volta.
- `BLOCK_SIZE_K=64` removes the pathology.
- The A/B output was bit-identical in the tested cases.

Scope:

- FP16/BF16 fused-MoE decode.
- Small-M / decode regime.
- Volta / V100 evidence only.
- Does not affect dense models.
- Does not depend on my custom FP8 plugin.
- Not an MTP/speculative decoding result.

Reference write-up / evidence:

- https://github.com/KumphanartDansiri/v100-vllm-2026
- Chapter 2 documents this finding.
- The companion implementation/results repo is here:
  https://github.com/KumphanartDansiri/vllm-fp8-w8a16-sm70

### Misc discussion on performance

I am intentionally framing this narrowly.

I understand that current vLLM wheels do not target V100 / `sm_70`, and I am not asking for a policy reversal in this issue. The reason I am reporting it upstream is that vLLM 0.19 remains an important practical line for V100 users, and the fused-MoE default/config issue is large enough that it can make sparse MoE look incorrectly bad on Volta.

The possible outcomes I see are:

1. vLLM accepts Tesla V100 fused-MoE config JSONs as data.
2. vLLM decides this should remain external documentation because V100 is out of current support scope.
3. Maintainers suggest a better place or format for this finding.

If option 1 is acceptable, I can prepare a focused PR with only config data / documentation, avoiding any broad sm_70 support-policy change.

### Your current environment (if you think it is necessary)

Not a live-install bug report, so I did not run collect_env.py here.

The relevant measured environments are:

Hardware:
- 8x NVIDIA Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB
- Volta / sm_70
- NVLink box

Software / build context:
- vLLM 0.19.x source build as the primary V100-relevant line
- vLLM 0.21 source-build path also checked on CUDA 12.6
- CUDA 12.6 / cu126 torch path
- CUDAGraph decode serving setup

Models used in the MoE A/B:
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
- Gemma-4-26B-A4B

Reference repos:
- Write-up / benchmark matrix:
  https://github.com/KumphanartDansiri/v100-vllm-2026
- Companion code/results repo:
  https://github.com/KumphanartDansiri/vllm-fp8-w8a16-sm70

Notes:
- This is not a request to restore V100 wheel support.
- This is not related to my custom FP8 kernels.
- I can provide config JSONs or a smaller reproducer if maintainers think this is useful.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

candidates.title: CUDA device-side assert with nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 + MTP on nightly f91fb2f
candidates.body:
## Summary

`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-f91fb2fcf3f100d46baf4db2e5d86fa5596b276b` crashes with a CUDA device-side assert while serving the official NVIDIA `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` model with MTP/spec decoding enabled.

The same local model files were hash-checked against the official Hugging Face repo revision and safetensors LFS SHA256 values.

## Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, 32 GB VRAM
- NVIDIA driver reported by `nvidia-smi`: 610.47
- OS: WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04
- Kernel: `6.6.114.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2`
- Docker: `Docker version 29.5.2, build 79eb04c`
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-f91fb2fcf3f100d46baf4db2e5d86fa5596b276b`
- vLLM: `0.22.1rc1.dev55+gf91fb2fcf`
- Torch: `2.11.0+cu130`
- Transformers: `5.9.0`

## Model

HF model:

`nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4`

Repo revision from local Hugging Face metadata and HF API:

`6c7f09d4036e97393f82e9f9ecd1a5c35ca5ee92`

Local safetensors hashes matched official HF LFS hashes:

| File | SHA256 |
|---|---|
| `model-00001-of-00003.safetensors` | `07141c2db92e47bc08777132cd1a0323faf300eab3a7d7c111bc2bf075fda050` |
| `model-00002-of-00003.safetensors` | `6dea9c759a0f941cf9e1cc1501216b0e107966a66c90425050e212efbd053f02` |
| `model-00003-of-00003.safetensors` | `9758875fc55e49561165f4a44342b654c123c3e25c6811b34abb83553fb1a164` |
| `model.safetensors.index.json` | `d67403a4e9793c0ba8a136baf14b3b76ec7b32c822267978084895e07ebd8a3e` |

## Serving configuration

Profile line used locally:

```text
backend=vllm-docker image=vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-f91fb2fcf3f100d46baf4db2e5d86fa5596b276b port=8082 ctx=131072 kv=fp8 gpu=0.94 max_num_seqs=1 max_num_batched_tokens=8192 spec=mtp:3 vision=on chunked_prefill=on prefix_caching=on expert_parallel=on reasoning_parser=qwen3 tool_parser=qwen3_xml thinking=on preserve_thinking=on temp=0.6 top_p=0.95 alias=qwen35-nvidia-nvfp4-sci-thinking
```

Equivalent notable vLLM arguments:

```text
--model /model
--trust-remote-code
--max-model-len 131072
--quantization modelopt
--kv-cache-dtype fp8
--gpu-memory-utilization 0.94
--max-num-seqs 1
--max-num-batched-tokens 8192
--enable-chunked-prefill
--enable-prefix-caching
--enable-expert-parallel
--reasoning-parser qwen3
--enable-auto-tool-choice
--tool-call-parser qwen3_xml
--default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":true,"preserve_thinking":true}'
--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"moe_backend":"triton"}'
```

## Failure

During generation, the engine crashes with:

```text
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
```

Relevant stack excerpt:

```text
(EngineCore pid=264) ERROR [core.py:1188] EngineCore encountered a fatal error.
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 4041, in execute_model
    self.synchronize_input_prep(),
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 3709, in synchronize_input_prep
    self.prepare_inputs_event.synchronize()
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call, so the stacktrace below might be incorrect.
For debugging consider passing CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1
Compile with `TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA` to enable device-side assertions.
```

After that, `AsyncLLM output_handler` fails with `EngineDeadError`, and shutdown also hits the same CUDA assert during cleanup:

```text
vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue.
...
model_runner.shutdown()
...
torch.accelerator.synchronize()
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
```

## Expected behavior

The engine should either complete generation or return a non-fatal request-level error. A single request should not kill the EngineCore with a CUDA device-side assert.

## Notes

- This was observed after switching from `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.22.0` to the nightly image above.
- Because the assert is asynchronous, I cannot prove the originating kernel from this stack alone.
- The high-risk interaction appears to be Qwen35 NVFP4 + MTP/spec decoding + fp8 KV on Blackwell/RTX 5090.
- I have not yet reduced this to a minimal repro with `spec=off` vs `spec=mtp:3`.

- Model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash
- vLLM ROCm nightly-derived environment; latest repro used `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:base-nightly-b8336c3c7c298e0878f22a7bf70f4e295b2f4e01`
- TileLang installed and importable; observed TileLang version: 0.1.10
- Server config: TP4, VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1, kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3, tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4, moe-backend triton_unfused

### 🐛 Describe the bug

On gfx942, DeepSeek V4 / DeepSeek V4 Flash produces nonsensical output when the ROCm MHC path dispatches to TileLang. The same server configuration produces coherent output when TileLang is unavailable, forcing the non-TileLang MHC fallback.

This looks specific to the TileLang MHC path on gfx942, not to sparse attention, MoE, or the prompt. Prior local debugging found TileLang MHC numerics wrong on gfx942, while the torch/triton fallback is coherent.

## Minimal reproduction

Run on a gfx942 node with 4 GPUs available and TileLang installed in the vLLM environment. The prompt-level TileLang-vs-non-TileLang A/B below was validated on the DeepSeek V4 ROCm fix branch from vLLM PR #45681. PR #45681 is not believed to cause the TileLang MHC bug; it makes the DeepSeek V4 gfx942 path get past earlier FP8/FNUZ model-load issues, which exposes the separate TileLang MHC correctness problem.

Start the server with the default TileLang-available path:

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1

vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --moe-backend triton_unfused \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --disable-log-stats
```

Send a simple deterministic request:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
import urllib.request

payload = {
    "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash",
    "prompt": "Q: What is 17 + 25? Answer briefly.\nA:",
    "max_tokens": 64,
    "temperature": 0,
}

req = urllib.request.Request(
    "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions",
    data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
    headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    method="POST",
)

with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as resp:
    print(json.dumps(json.load(resp), indent=2))
PY
```

Expected: coherent answer beginning with `42`.

Observed with TileLang MHC selected on gfx942: gibberish / incoherent text.

As an A/B check, restart the same server after making TileLang unavailable:

```bash
python3 -m pip uninstall -y tilelang
```

With the same serve command and prompt, the output becomes coherent. In local validation, the non-TileLang MHC path produced a coherent `42...` response and full GSM8K 5-shot exact match around `0.95` on MI300X/gfx942.

## Additional validation signal

Local A/B evidence on gfx942:

| MHC path | TileLang available | Output / accuracy |
|---|---:|---|
| TileLang MHC | yes | gibberish / unusable |
| torch/triton fallback | no | coherent; GSM8K 5-shot exact match observed at `0.9568 ± 0.0056` in a TP4 MI300X validation |

Fresh prompt-level validation on MI300X/gfx942:

- Image base: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:base-nightly-b8336c3c7c298e0878f22a7bf70f4e295b2f4e01`
- Model/server config: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`, TP4, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4`, `--moe-backend triton_unfused`
- Prompt: `Q: What is 17 + 25? Answer briefly.\nA:`

| Source variant | TileLang status | Observed response |
|---|---|---|
| PR #45681 branch | installed, `tilelang==0.1.10` | Gibberish beginning with `\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ recogn也比 that specifically...`; did not answer `42`. |
| PR #45681 branch | uninstalled before server startup | Coherent response beginning with `42`; then continued with arithmetic examples. |
| PR #45681 branch + PR #43950 applied | installed, `tilelang==0.1.10` | Coherent response beginning with `42.`; then continued with arithmetic examples. |
| PR #45681 branch + PR #43950 applied | uninstalled before server startup | Coherent response: `42.</think>The sum of 17 and 25 is 42.` |

This suggests PR #43950 avoids the user-visible failure in the tested `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` configuration even when TileLang remains installed. It does so by changing ROCm MHC dispatch priority, not by fixing TileLang itself: when AITER MHC is available on ROCm/MI3xx and the hidden size is a multiple of 256, `MHCPreOp` and `MHCPostOp` now choose the AITER kernels before TileLang. The AMD DeepSeek V4 layer also routes this case through the unfused pre/post path when `HAS_AITER_MHC` is true, so the TileLang fused post+pre path is skipped. The narrower TileLang-specific issue still matters for configurations that can dispatch to TileLang MHC on gfx942.

Control without PR #45681:

- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-b8336c3c7c298e0878f22a7bf70f4e295b2f4e01`
- TileLang status: installed, `tilelang==0.1.10`
- Result: the same serve command did not reach the prompt request. Model load failed earlier while normalizing FP8 block scales for gfx942/FNUZ:

```text
NotImplementedError: "mul_cuda" not implemented for 'Float8_e8m0fnu'
```

Because upstream nightly without PR #45681 fails before generation, it is not a clean baseline for the TileLang MHC gibberish symptom. The TileLang MHC issue was isolated using PR #45681 as the validation vehicle, by showing that the same PR #45681 server becomes coherent when TileLang is made unavailable.

Related context:

- TileLang MHC was enabled for ROCm in vLLM PR #43679.
- vLLM PR #44692 fixed one TileLang MHC issue, but local gfx942 validation still indicates the TileLang MHC path is not numerically correct on gfx942.
- vLLM PR #43950 is related: in the local comparison above it routes the tested ROCm/AITER configuration away from the failing user-visible behavior when aiter is available. This issue is specifically about the TileLang MHC path being incorrect on gfx942 when selected.

## Before submitting a new issue

- [X] Searched existing vLLM issues for TileLang/MHC/gfx942/DeepSeek V4 reports.
- [X] Attached `python collect_env.py` output from the reproducing gfx942 node.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

candidates.title: [Performance]: Deepseek-V4 Support and Optimization on ROCm Backend
candidates.body:
## Motivation

This issue tracks the end-to-end enablement and optimization checklist for **DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm backend**.

DeepSeek-V4 includes multiple critical blocks (mHC/HCA/CSA/MoE/MTP), and ROCm readiness depends on both model-side kernels and system-side runtime behavior.

We’re launching a joint effort to optimize DeepSeek V4 on the ROCm backend—please feel free to take on any task, and we’d love to hear more optimization ideas.

## Purpose

- [ ] Track DeepSeek-V4 functionality and performance readiness on ROCm backend.
- [ ] Keep module-level optimization items visible and actionable.
- [ ] Align acceptance criteria for release and production readiness.

---

## Recipe 

- [ ] Recipe: `vLLM Recipe: DeepSeek-V4 on AMD (ROCm) Usage Guide - vLLM Recipes` https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/pull/433

## General Checklist

### 1) Functionality / Bugfix / Feature

- [x] [Functionality] Base PR has been merged for functionality/accuracy readiness on MI35x for DeepSeek-V4-Pro and DeepSeek-V4-Flash. <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40871>
- [ ] [Functionality] DeepSeek-V4-Flash Base FP8 enablement PR: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41136>
- [ ] [Functionality] MI30x support PR: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41451>
- [ ] [Bugfix] Enable cross-node TP=16 FP8 serving for DeepSeek-V4: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41312>
- [ ] [Feature][WIP] Enable KV offload for DeepSeek-V4: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41352>
- [ ] [Feature][WIP] Compressed tensors support for DSV4: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41276>
- [x] [Bugfix] Fix accuracy issue with high concurrency: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42810>

---

## Performance Checklist

### 1) High-Level Performance/Feature

- [x] Full graph support for Decode path. Piecewise graph capture support for Prefill path. <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42604>  <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41601>
- [ ] Support MTP 

### 2) Kernel Fusion

#### Element-wise Fusion
- [x] Avoid redundant dtype conversion: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41374>
- [x] Fuse norm and router for lower latency: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41263>
- [ ] Silu and Mul is implemented with [`torch native`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/activation.py#L173)
- [ ] inv_rope is implemented with [`torch native`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py#L872)

#### CSA

- [ ] Make the sparse MLA indexer optimization for Deepseek-V4, now the sparse attention indexder is [`pytorch native implementation`](<https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py#L592>).
- [ ] Replace torch native sparse MLA path with Triton kernel (<https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41136>). Another single kernel (<https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41812>)
- [ ] Enable CSA multi-stream execution in Decode (`default stream` + `indexer stream`) to overlap indexer and main attention paths, aligned with the DeepSeek-V4 blog design.

#### mHC
- [x] Now the MHC on ROCm is pytorch native implementation ([`mhc_pre`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/mhc.py#L237)， [`mhc_post`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/mhc.py#L451)), need to integrate [`AITER MHC kernel`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/main/csrc/include/mhc.h) https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41946

#### MoE
- [ ] AITER FlyDSL MoE integration when it's ready ([`MoE Kernel`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/2951/changes))

candidates.title: [Bug]: ROCm MI300X FP8 KV cache MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 accuracy issues
candidates.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Key environment details</summary>

```text
GPU              : 8x AMD Instinct MI300X (gfx942)
Image            : vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:minimax-m3
vLLM             : 0.22.1rc1.dev490+g4a560dd8d
Model            : MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8
Model dtype      : torch.bfloat16
Quantization     : mxfp8
Attention backend: TRITON_ATTN
Parallelism      : TP=8, expert parallelism enabled
KV cache         : fp8 (broken) / auto-BF16 (working)
Prefix caching   : disabled
```

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Summary

On ROCm/MI300X, `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` starts successfully with
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, and requests return HTTP 200, but generated output is
severely corrupted.

vLLM also reports that calibrated FP8 attention scales are unavailable and
uses `1.0`:

```text
Using uncalibrated q_scale 1.0 and/or prob_scale 1.0 with fp8 attention.
This may cause accuracy issues. Please make sure q/prob scaling factors are
available in the fp8 checkpoint.
```

That warning was initially suspected, but it is not the cause of this failure.
The failure is a dtype mismatch in the MiniMax-M3 sparse-attention path.

This is not a small accuracy regression. GSM8K strict accuracy drops from
`0.9666` with the default BF16 KV cache to `0.0099` with FP8 KV cache.
Outputs contain unrelated problem fragments, incorrect arithmetic, and
repetition that often continues to the generation limit.

Removing only `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` restores normal output and accuracy.

This appears related to #45533, but the failure mode is different: #45533
reports startup failure, while this configuration starts and serves normally
but silently returns incorrect output.

### Root cause

On ROCm gfx942, `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` is
`torch.float8_e4m3fnuz`. The MiniMax-M3 sparse backend instead hardcodes
`torch.float8_e4m3fn` when it reinterprets the byte-backed KV cache:

```python
self.kv_cache_fp8_dtype = (
    torch.float8_e5m2
    if "e5m2" in kv_cache_dtype
    else torch.float8_e4m3fn
)
```

The prefill and decode wrappers also classify only `float8_e4m3fn` and
`float8_e5m2` as FP8, omitting `float8_e4m3fnuz`.

FN and FNUZ do not have the same encoding. Interpreting gfx942 FNUZ KV-cache
bytes as FN changes the represented values before sparse attention consumes
them. A direct MI300X kernel comparison measured:

| KV interpretation | Relative L2 error | Cosine similarity | Output norm ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Correct FNUZ | 0.0387 | 0.9993 | 0.999x |
| Current FN hardcode | 3.227 | 0.8748 | 4.066x |

The fix is to use `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` for E4M3 KV caches and treat
`torch.float8_e4m3fnuz` as FP8 in both sparse-attention wrappers.

### Fix validation

We hot-patched those two Python modules into the same container image and ran
the complete 1,319-sample GSM8K evaluation again. No image rebuild or other
server/configuration change was made.

| KV-cache configuration | Strict match | Flexible extract |
|---|---:|---:|
| FP8 KV, unpatched | 0.0099 | 0.0296 |
| FP8 KV, patched | 0.9575 | 0.9568 |
| BF16 KV reference | 0.9666 | 0.9659 |

The patched run completed all 1,319 requests with HTTP 200 and no server
errors. This recovers the expected accuracy while retaining FP8 KV cache.

### Reproduction

Start the server:

```bash
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \
  --port 8888 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --block-size 128 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --language-model-only \
  --max-model-len 9472 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --enforce-eager \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

Send a deterministic request:

```bash
curl http://localhost:8888/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8",
    "temperature": 0,
    "max_tokens": 2048,
    "messages": [{
      "role": "user",
      "content": "Question: Janet'\''s ducks lay 16 eggs per day. She eats three for breakfast and uses four for muffins. She sells the remainder for $2 each. How much does she make per day? End your response with: #### [number]"
    }]
  }'
```

### Observed behavior

Expected answer: `#### 18`

Output with FP8 KV cache:

```text
Janet's ducks lay 16 eggs per day, so she will lay 16 x 7 = 112 eggs...
Therefore ... 112 - 21 = 91 eggs per day.
#### 91
Answer: 91
answer: 91
answer: 1 / 2 = 91
answer: 1 / 2 = 91
...
```

The response repeats until the generation limit.

Other examples from the same GSM8K run:

#### Example 2

Prompt:

```text
A robe takes 2 bolts of blue fiber and half that much white fiber.
How many bolts in total does it take?
```

Expected: `#### 3`

Observed:

```text
思维140 - 32 = 108 green bars.
After the loss, Corey had 108 + 32 = 140 green bars.
#### 140
Answer: 140 green apples.
Answer: 140 gold apple.
Answer: 140 gold apple.
...
```

#### Example 3

Prompt:

```text
James runs 3 sprints, 3 times a week, at 60 meters per sprint.
How many meters does he run per week?
```

Expected: `#### 540`

Observed:

```text
He runs 3 x 3 = 6 sprints per week.
He runs 6 x 60 = 360
#### 360
Question: 3/8 of his money to his father...
...
```

#### Example 4

Prompt:

```text
One glass costs $5, but every second glass costs 60% of the price.
How much do 16 glasses cost?
```

Expected: `#### 64`

Observed:

```text
<think>
...
3N + 6 = -147
N = -51
N + (N + 2) + (N + 4) = -147
N + (N + 2) + (N + 4) = -147
...
```

### Accuracy comparison

Full GSM8K, 5-shot, temperature 0:

| KV-cache configuration | Strict match | Flexible extract |
|---|---:|---:|
| `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` | 0.0099 | 0.0296 |
| Default (`kv_cache_dtype=auto`, BF16) | 0.9666 | 0.9659 |

Failed FP8-KV run:

https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/27482907707

Passing run after removing FP8 KV cache:

https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/27485772194

### Workaround

Remove:

```text
--kv-cache-dtype fp8
```

The engine then uses:

```text
dtype=torch.bfloat16
kv_cache_dtype=auto
```

No other server arguments were changed. The same image, model, attention
backend, parallelism, prompts, and evaluation configuration then pass GSM8K.

### Expected behavior

The MiniMax-M3 sparse-attention backend should interpret E4M3 KV-cache bytes
using the platform FP8 dtype. On gfx942, that is
`torch.float8_e4m3fnuz`; on platforms using standard E4M3, it remains
`torch.float8_e4m3fn`.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the documentation page, which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
