candidates.title: [RFC]: Tensor descriptor (TD) adoption strategy for vLLM Triton kernels
candidates.body:
### Motivation.

vLLM's Triton kernels load data and store results via raw pointer arithmetic (`tl.load(ptr + offset, mask=…)`). Triton's newer structured memory-access API — `tl.make_tensor_descriptor` (TD) — is the replacement API upstream Triton is steering toward (`tl.make_block_ptr` is officially deprecated) and the path to architecture-accelerated memory on modern hardware: TMA on NVIDIA Hopper, 2D block loads on Intel Xe. Adopting TD in vLLM kernels unlocks significant E2E speedups where backend lowering is mature (Intel Battlemage: +38–83%), creates headroom where lowering is still catching up (NVIDIA Blackwell today), and positions the code base ahead of the deprecation rather than behind it.

This RFC proposes a **strategy for adopting TD across vLLM's Triton kernels**: opt-in TD paths behind a single env var (`VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD`) with per-kernel constexpr gating, a platform-aware default, and graduation criteria that gate every future conversion and every default-on flip. The strategy has been applied to `triton_unified_attention.py` (the unified attention kernels used by the `TRITON_ATTN` backend) in PR [#40327](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40327) as the pilot that validates the approach; follow-up PRs extend TD to the remaining XPU-invocable Triton kernels under the same framework, each justified by per-kernel benchmarks meeting the graduation criteria below.

#### Triton surface area in vLLM

vLLM has **245 `@triton.jit` functions** in mainline today. The subset that is **invocable on Intel XPU** — either as default path or via documented opt-in env vars / backend selectors — is our primary scope:

| Category | Count | Invocation path (XPU) |
|---|---|---|
| **Unified attention (pilot)** | 3 | `--attention-backend=TRITON_ATTN` — PR [#40327](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40327) |
| **Other attention ops on the TRITON_ATTN path** | ~20 | `TRITON_ATTN` backend: `triton_decode_attention`, `triton_prefill_attention`, `chunked_prefill_paged_decode`, `triton_reshape_and_cache_flash`, `prefix_prefill`, `common.py` token merge, `turboquant_*`, `dcp_alltoall` |
| **MLA Triton kernels** | ~9 | `--attention-backend=TRITON_MLA` (auto-selected for MLA models), plus `xpu_mla_sparse` |
| **LoRA Triton path** | ~16 | `XPU_USE_TRITON_KERNEL=1` env var — routes `PunicaWrapperXPU` through Triton kernels instead of SYCL |
| *(Helpers / pure-compute in same files)* | ~15 | N/A — no memory I/O to wrap with TD |
| **XPU-invocable subtotal** | **~50** | This is the RFC's XPU scope |
| Not currently XPU-invocable (CUDA/ROCm-only today) | ~160 | fused_moe, quantization, sample/spec_decode, mamba, FLA, rotary, deepseek_v4_ops — XPU delegates to SYCL (`vllm-xpu-kernels`) or has no Triton path. Covered by this strategy *if* the ecosystem later adds XPU paths. |
| *(Helpers / pure-compute, other)* | ~20 | Excluded from scope |
| **Total** | **245** | |

This RFC's strategy applies to all 245 kernels in principle, but the empirical evidence and near-term work focus on the ~50 XPU-invocable kernels where Intel has both the data and the motivation to drive conversion. NVIDIA / ROCm conversions of the remaining ~160 kernels are free to follow under the same framework and the same graduation criteria.

#### Why this matters now

1. **XPU enablement gap.** Current raw-pointer Triton attention kernels are functional on Intel XPU (Battlemage) but perform below hardware potential. Measured impact of TD on Battlemage: **+38% to +83% throughput** on Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct across prefill-heavy and decode-heavy workloads.

2. **NVIDIA Hopper TMA path underutilized.** On Hopper (H100/H200), TD lowers to Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA) instructions, unlocking hardware memory throughput otherwise inaccessible to raw-pointer kernels. We do not include Hopper benchmarks in this RFC; community runs are welcome.

3. **NVIDIA Blackwell: opt-in bridges the gap.** On B200, the TD path currently underperforms raw pointers (–33% to –60% E2E). We attribute this to implementation-level factors — per-tile descriptor reconstruction overhead, autotune configs not yet tuned for TMA — rather than a structural property of the API. `tl.make_tensor_descriptor` carries strictly more information than raw pointers (explicit shape, strides, and block layout), so in principle the backend can always lower it to at least parity. The opt-in design lets Blackwell users take the fast path today and adopt TD later as these optimizations land, without a second kernel migration.

   The asymmetry between the Battlemage speedup and the B200 regression is consistent with the fraction of forward-pass FLOPs each model spends in the attention block. Computed at a representative decoding shape (`seq_q=1, seq_kv=4096`) from public HF configs, the attention block (QKV + QK + AV + O) accounts for ~25% of forward FLOPs on Qwen3-4B, ~22% on Llama-3.1-8B, and ~14% on Qwen2-7B. On Battlemage, Xe 2D block loads make the TD path substantially faster in the attention kernel itself, and the E2E gain tracks this share (+83% / +55% / TD-neutral respectively). On B200, the current Triton→TMA lowering has not closed the gap to the highly tuned raw-pointer path, so the same attention-share multiplier works against the TD kernel rather than for it.

4. **Alignment with Triton's direction.** `tl.make_block_ptr` is officially deprecated in Triton: as of 2026-03-06, it emits a runtime deprecation warning explicitly directing users to `tl.make_tensor_descriptor` (or the `TensorDescriptor` class) as its replacement ([triton-lang/triton#9667](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/9667)). TD is the API Triton upstream is steering toward for lowering to accelerated memory paths — TMA on Hopper, 2D block loads on Xe. Adopting TD in attention kernels aligns with this direction and gives every backend a single API to optimize against, rather than requiring per-platform rewrites as block pointers phase out.

5. **Zero regression by design.** TD is off by default on all NVIDIA platforms. When disabled, the kernel compiles to the exact same code path — same autotuning, same performance, bit-exact output. Enabling TD is a single env-var flip (`VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=1`) that users can benchmark on their own hardware before committing. This change adds capability; it removes nothing. The engineering cost of converting attention to TD is paid once — every backend benefits as its lowering improves, without a second kernel migration.

6. **Adjacency to [RFC #40458](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40458).** A parallel RFC (#40458) proposes converting simple element-wise kernels (SwiGLU, MRoPE, etc.) to **block pointers**, and asks maintainers: *"`tl.make_block_ptr` vs `tl.make_tensor_descriptor`?"* Given the deprecation of `tl.make_block_ptr` (see point 4) and the fact that on tiled-memory and TMA-capable architectures (Intel XPU, NVIDIA Hopper) TD is the API steering toward the accelerated memory paths while block pointers are not, this RFC complements #40458 by empirically answering that question for attention kernels: **block_ptr and TD are both useful for different kernel classes; for heavy kernels on tiled-memory and TMA-capable HW, TD is the path forward**.

### Proposed Change.

#### Pilot kernel (PR [#40327](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40327))

The pilot that validates the strategy is `vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py`. PR [#40327](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40327) refactored the file so that the previously separate 2D and 3D attention kernels are now a single unified kernel with two opt-in TD gates; the refactor also added four TD-path `@triton.jit` helpers:

| `@triton.jit` function | Role | TD path status |
|---|---|---|
| `kernel_unified_attention` | Main kernel — prefill / decode / segmented decode in one entry | **Opt-in TD available** (`USE_TD` for K/V cache tile loads, `USE_TD_QO` for Q load + output store). |
| `reduce_segments` | Post-processing kernel (online softmax reduction of per-segment outputs) | Not yet wrapped; access is already contiguous, trivial candidate for follow-up. |
| `_cast_kv_tile` | Helper — cast/dequant K/V tile data | N/A (operates on in-register tile data post-load). |
| `_load_q_td`, `_load_kv_tile_td`, `_store_output_td` | TD-path loaders/storer helpers | **Part of the TD path**; active only when `USE_TD` / `USE_TD_QO` are set. Dead-code-eliminated at compile time otherwise. |

Plus Python helpers (`_is_gemma3_attention`, `_get_tile_size`, entry point `unified_attention`) that are not `@triton.jit` and are not impacted by this RFC.

#### Mechanism

Two independent opt-in constexpr flags at the kernel level:

- **`USE_TD`** (bool, default `False`): TD path for K/V cache tile loads inside the per-tile loop.
- **`USE_TD_QO`** (bool, default `False`): TD path for Q load at kernel entry and output store at kernel exit.

A Python-side env var controls the TD path with **tri-state semantics**:
- unset (default): **auto** — TD on for Intel XPU (where Battlemage evidence shows consistent net-positive impact), off elsewhere;
- `1`: force TD on regardless of platform (used by NVIDIA users who want to evaluate TD on their own HW — Hopper users are the most likely candidates);
- `0`: force TD off regardless of platform (useful for A/B testing and for platforms where TD may be selected by default in the future but the user wants to stay on raw pointers).

The tri-state makes platform-aware defaults the norm without removing user control.

PR [#40327](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40327) shipped this as `VLLM_TRITON_ATTN_USE_TD` — specific to the attention pilot. As the strategy extends to other Triton kernels under the same opt-in pattern, we propose **renaming the env var to `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD`** in a follow-up PR so that a single flag gates the TD path across all kernels (consistent with the single-flag, no-subsystem-subflags design below). The tri-state semantics stay unchanged.

No subsystem subflags. A single flag is enough for the strategy's scope and keeps the interface simple. If finer granularity is ever needed, it can be introduced as a follow-up without breaking this interface.

#### TD path for K/V cache — how paged KV is handled

vLLM's paged KV cache introduces a 2-level indirection: `seq_offset // BLOCK_SIZE → block_table[…] → physical_block_idx → cache_offset`. `tl.make_tensor_descriptor` requires its base pointer (and strides) to be known at descriptor construction time, which conflicts with per-tile dynamic lookups.

The proposed approach is a **hybrid**:

1. Perform block-table lookup with raw pointer (unchanged).
2. Extract scalar `physical_block_scalar = tl.min(physical_block_idx, axis=0)`; this is valid because **all tiles within one block share the same physical block index** when `BLOCK_SIZE % TILE_SIZE == 0`.
3. Construct TD per tile iteration with base `= cache_ptr + physical_block_scalar * stride_cache_0 + kv_head_idx * stride_cache_2`, then load via `desc.load([offset_in_block, 0])`.

#### Required preconditions

The TD path requires:
- `BLOCK_SIZE % TILE_SIZE == 0` (enforced via `tl.static_assert` in the kernel);
- Triton ≥ 3.4.0 (first release shipping the non-experimental `tl.make_tensor_descriptor`; the experimental predecessor in 3.3.x is not sufficient). For XPU, `triton-xpu` ≥ 3.6.0 includes this API.
- Tile caller must clamp `TILE_SIZE` to `BLOCK_SIZE` when `USE_TD=True`.

When these do not hold, the non-TD path (raw pointer + mask) is selected — **no functional regression**.

#### Code layout

TD path is structured as three `@triton.jit` helpers called from `kernel_unified_attention` when the corresponding constexpr flag is set:
- `_load_q_td` — Q load at kernel entry (used when `USE_TD_QO=True`),
- `_load_kv_tile_td` — K/V cache tile load inside the per-tile loop (used when `USE_TD=True`),
- `_store_output_td` — output store at kernel exit (used when `USE_TD_QO=True`).

The raw-pointer path remains inline in `kernel_unified_attention` under the `else` branches of the same constexpr ifs.

Both paths co-exist in the source, but only one is compiled per kernel specialization. `USE_TD` is a `tl.constexpr` parameter, so Triton specializes the kernel per unique value. When `USE_TD=False`, the TD branch is never visited during AST-to-TTIR translation (see [`python/triton/compiler/code_generator.py`](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/main/python/triton/compiler/code_generator.py), `visit_If`: after `_unwrap_if_constexpr`, only the active branch is emitted) — the inactive code path is absent from the generated Triton IR and therefore from all downstream artifacts (LLVM IR, PTX, SPIR-V). The compiled binary contains no runtime branch and no instructions for the disabled path. This is a property of Triton's specialization mechanism, applied uniformly across all backends. Long-term, as TD becomes the default across platforms, the raw-pointer path can be removed, simplifying the kernel back to a single code path.

#### Planned kernel conversions beyond the pilot

The strategy proposed here applies uniformly to further kernels; each conversion lands as its own PR, using the same `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD` env var, the same constexpr-gating pattern, and the graduation criteria below. Near-term targets (all XPU-invocable under the paths in the table above):

1. **Rest of the `TRITON_ATTN` path** in `v1/attention/ops/` — `triton_decode_attention` (4), `triton_prefill_attention` (1), `chunked_prefill_paged_decode` (2), `triton_reshape_and_cache_flash` (3), `prefix_prefill` (2), `common.py` token-merge (~3), `turboquant_*` (5), `dcp_alltoall` (2). ~22 memory-I/O kernels total.
2. **MLA Triton kernels** (`triton_mla.py`, `xpu_mla_sparse.py`) — ~9 kernels, invocable on XPU via `--attention-backend=TRITON_MLA` or the XPU-specific MLA sparse backend.
3. **LoRA Triton kernels** in `lora/ops/triton_ops/` — ~16 kernels, invocable on XPU via `XPU_USE_TRITON_KERNEL=1`.

Non-XPU-invocable kernels (MoE, sampling, spec_decode, mamba, FLA, standard quantization, rotary, DeepSeek V4 ops — ~160 total) are covered by this strategy in principle but are currently routed away from Triton on XPU (delegated to `vllm-xpu-kernels` SYCL ops or simply not supported). Their conversion is open to CUDA / ROCm maintainers under the same framework if and when it makes sense for their platforms.

*Explicit non-goal:* blanket, unconditional conversion of all Triton kernels. The evidence (B200 regression) does not support in-place replacement. Every PR that lands a TD path must be backed by per-kernel, per-backend benchmarks meeting the graduation criteria, and every default-on flip (per platform) requires the same evidence.

#### Validation approach

1. **Numerical equivalence.** Per-kernel tests (`tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py`) comparing TD and non-TD paths across shapes, dtypes (fp16, bf16), and GQA ratios. Implemented in PR [#40327](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40327).
2. **End-to-end throughput.** `vllm bench throughput` on a representative model set spanning standard attention (Qwen3-4B, Llama-3.1-8B) and non-power-of-2 GQA (Qwen2-7B) × three workloads (ShareGPT, random-prefill, random-decode). Standard `vllm bench throughput` CLI, no custom harness.

#### Evidence: cross-platform impact

TD is not a single-platform feature — its value depends on how each backend lowers it today and where it is headed. We organize results by impact category.

##### 1. Hardware where TD helps today

**Intel Battlemage**, `TRITON_ATTN` backend, `VLLM_TRITON_ATTN_USE_TD=1`.

Throughput median (req/s, 3 runs) vs `TRITON_ATTN` baseline (TD=0):

| Model | Architecture | GQA | random-decode | random-prefill | sharegpt |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 | standard attn | 4:1 | 3.51 → **6.41** (+83%) | 3.50 → **6.41** (+83%) | 5.02 → **8.52** (+70% R1; +38–39% R2/R3 medians) |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | standard attn | 4:1 | 2.83 → **4.38** (+55%) | 2.83 → **4.37** (+55%) | 5.42 → **7.48** (+38%) |

Measured by the Intel XPU team across Battlemage SKUs (B60 and B70). Numbers are expressed as relative deltas; the trend across SKUs is consistent.

Default (flash-attn) backend varies ±1.6% across same runs — TD effect is isolated to the Triton backend.

##### 2. Hardware where TD is safe and neutral

**Qwen2-7B (GQA 7:1) on Intel Battlemage** — TD=0 and TD=1 produce identical throughput (2.28 req/s on random-decode, 4.29 → 5.32 on sharegpt within noise). Confirms TD introduces no regression on non-power-of-2 GQA configurations. The `TRITON_ATTN` vs. default gap on this model is shared by both paths — an autotuning limitation of `TRITON_ATTN` for the 7:1 shape, not a TD issue.

##### 3. Hardware with headroom for future gains

**B200 (NVIDIA Blackwell)** — TD currently underperforms raw pointers (–33% to –60% across Qwen3-4B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2-7B). This reflects implementation-level factors — per-tile descriptor reconstruction, autotune configs not yet tuned for TMA — rather than a structural property of the API. TD is off by default on NVIDIA; Blackwell users pay no cost. As these optimizations land in the Triton backend or kernel-side tuning, Blackwell users can opt in without a kernel migration.

**NVIDIA Hopper (H100/H200).** We expect TD to lower to TMA on Hopper, which is the accelerated memory path there. We do not include Hopper benchmarks in this RFC — community runs are welcome and would help map the strategy to Hopper, but they are not required for the decision proposed here: the opt-in design means Hopper users pay no cost until they choose to enable the TD path and validate on their own setup.

#### Graduation criteria for default-on adoption

TD remains opt-in per platform until all three criteria are met on that platform's representative hardware:

1. **Numerical equivalence.** Per-kernel tests pass on TD vs raw-pointer paths across shapes, dtypes, and GQA ratios.
2. **Performance parity or better.** E2E throughput at parity or above the raw-pointer path on ≥3 models spanning different attention configurations (e.g., standard attention, GQA, non-power-of-2 GQA).
3. **Compilation cost.** No autotune-time regression exceeding 2× the raw-pointer baseline.

When a platform meets these criteria for the pilot kernel, a follow-up PR flips its default in `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD`. Intel Battlemage meets all three today. The same framework applies to every subsequent kernel conversion and every subsequent default-on flip — this is the single bar under which TD spreads across vLLM Triton kernels. Intel holds itself to the same bar, and NVIDIA graduation is expected as Triton-backend optimizations land — a *when*, not an *if*.

### Feedback Period.

Two weeks.

### CC List.

@ProExpertProg, @LucasWilkinson, @tdoublep, @bringlein, @jikunshang and @xuechendi

### Any Other Things.

#### Open questions for maintainers

1. **Acceptance of per-backend opt-in strategy.** Is a constexpr-gated dual-path (TD + raw) acceptable as the long-term design, or should vLLM prefer a single-path-with-runtime-switch approach?
2. **Env var design.** We propose a single `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD` switch with tri-state semantics (unset = auto; `1` = force on; `0` = force off), platform-aware auto-default (on for Intel XPU, off elsewhere), and no subsystem subflags. The pilot landed in PR [#40327](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40327) as the more specific `VLLM_TRITON_ATTN_USE_TD`; we would rename it to the general form in a follow-up PR once the strategy is accepted. Does this design and rename plan work for maintainers?
3. **Benchmark gate for future kernel conversions.** What should be the minimum evidence bar for each additional TD conversion? (proposed: numerical equivalence + per-kernel microbench + E2E throughput on ≥1 NVIDIA + ≥1 non-NVIDIA backend.)
4. **Triton version floor.** Are we comfortable depending on Triton ≥ 3.4.0 (first stable `tl.make_tensor_descriptor`) / `triton-xpu` ≥ 3.6.0 for the TD code path? Users on older Triton continue to use the raw-pointer default and see no change.
5. **Relation to [#40458](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40458) scope.** Should #40458 (block_ptr for simple kernels) and this RFC proceed in parallel, or should one be gated on the other's merge?

candidates.title: [Performance] MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 on 8x B200, first numbers after the #48929 correctness fix: 1M real-prose envelope, EAGLE3 2.1-2.3x decode
candidates.body:
## Summary

The recipes-page "validated B200 benchmark" for `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4` (vllm-project/recipes#605, merged
2026-07-09) predates the NVFP4 inference-correctness fix #48929 (merged 2026-08-05), and no stable release
contains that fix (v0.26.0 cut 2026-07-27). As far as we can tell, every published B200 number for this
checkpoint was measured on a build carrying the pre-fix swiglu/indexer behavior. We re-ran the recipe on a
post-fix nightly on 8x B200 with correctness gates in front of every measurement. Findings:

- **Correctness now holds at temperature 0** on a post-fix nightly: a seven-prompt content-checked suite
  passes 7/7 in benchmark mode (thinking disabled), and needle recovery is 144/144 across the 9 envelope
  cells and 15/15 across the context ladder (cache-busted real prose, 128K to 1M).
- **1M real-prose context works at production latency**: TTFT p50 43.2s for 1,011,492 input tokens
  (c=1, 3 reps), scaling smoothly from 2.63s at 128K. Aggregate prefill throughput reaches ~54K input
  tok/s at 128K c=16.
- **The 1M concurrency line is admission queueing.** The engine reports 2,558,976 KV tokens = 2.44x
  max concurrency at 1M, but the observed behavior is one 1M-class sequence in flight: `running=1` in 359 of
  378 sampled 2-second ticks across c=1..3, with one tick at `running=2` during the c=3 second rep (the
  prefill-to-decode handoff). Excess requests queue cleanly with linear makespan scaling and zero errors.
  Deployments should plan 1M traffic as serialized.
- **EAGLE3 gives 2.1-2.3x decode speedup at c=1** (decode-window medians: 2.06x at 8K, 2.30x at 128K, 2.23x at
  1M) at +5% TTFT (+4.6% at 128K, +5.5% at 1M; +0.04s at 8K where TTFT is ~0.2s), acceptance 2.01 tokens
  per 3-token draft. These are c=1 figures: the base decode is
  latency-bound, so a mean acceptance length of 3.01 maps almost linearly into TPOT; at concurrency the
  same acceptance length yields less. One counterintuitive interaction:
  `--language-model-only` (required by the EAGLE3 recipe) drops the vision tower, so the EAGLE3
  configuration has MORE KV capacity than the base recipe (2,727,296 vs 2,558,976 tokens).
- **`--enable-expert-parallel` is a no-op on a single node** for this model: identical KV capacity and
  identical latency (128K c=8 warm makespans 19.0s both ways; EP-on n=2 after excluding rep 1, a whole-rep
  post-start warmup at 88.6s, vs EP-off n=3). Some deployment guides include the
  flag; on one 8x B200 node it buys nothing.
- **MSA claim check, bounded by the measurable zone:** MiniMax claims 9x prefill / 15x decode vs the M2 family at 1M.
  The direct comparison ceiling is 196,608 tokens (M2.7's real `max_position_embeddings`; requests at the
  marketed "200K" return HTTP 400). Within that zone M3 shows ~parity prefill with a crossover near 150K
  (1.14x faster at 192K) and 1.22x faster decode. The 9x/15x figure is neither verified nor disproven by
  our data; it concerns a context regime where no M2-family model we can run accepts requests.

## Why a re-run was needed (the time axis)

| Date | Event |
| --- | --- |
| 2026-06-12 | M3 day-0 support lands; `vllm/vllm-openai:minimax-m3` vendor tag built (predates NVFP4 support entirely) |
| 2026-06-29 | NVFP4 ModelOpt plumbing merges (#46756) |
| 2026-07-09 | vllm-project/recipes#605 "validated B200 benchmark" for M3-NVFP4 merges |
| 2026-07-25 | #49149 (Triton token-major top-k buffer fix) merges |
| 2026-07-27 | v0.26.0 cut (latest stable at time of writing) |
| 2026-08-05 | **#48929 "Fix MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 inference correctness" merges** (swiglu alpha/beta/clamp plumbing to FlashInfer CUTLASS + Marlin; SM100 MSA index top-k layout) |

Consequence: stable v0.25.0/v0.26.0 and the vendor tag cannot serve NVFP4-correct M3, and the recipes-page
validation numbers predate the fix. We are not aware of other published B200 numbers measured on a
post-#48929 build; if an earlier post-fix set exists we will link it.

One operational note for anyone reproducing on nightlies from the 2026-08-05 to 2026-08-07 window: they
fail at startup with `TYPE_UNSTABLE_JOIN` in the SM100 FMHA path due to quack-kernels 0.6.3's import-time
AST rewrite under cutlass-dsl 4.6. #51418 (merged 2026-08-07) pins it upstream. The image used here
predates #51418, so the derived image pins quack-kernels below 0.6.3.

## Environment

| Component | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Hardware | 8x NVIDIA B200 SXM (183,359 MiB per GPU per nvidia-smi), single node |
| Image | `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-c810e5ee9976ad86b81d1277b53e76d0ee639414` (digest `sha256:928dde7d6c19478c9c6ab975fed12e6466f6d9b7cb3695d218e287c0c88ad608`) + quack-kernels pin (see note above) |
| vLLM | 0.26.1rc1.dev457+gc810e5ee9 (contains #48929, #49149) |
| Model | `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4`, HF snapshot id `901464083161` (captured at pull time; 88 shards, 250.1 GB) |
| Serve config | TP8, `--block-size 128`, `--tool-call-parser minimax_m3 --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 --enable-auto-tool-choice`, `VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION=high`. No scheduler overrides passed (partial-prefill and concurrency caps at defaults); `max_num_batched_tokens=8192` printed at startup |
| Startup KV line | `GPU KV cache size: 2,558,976 tokens, Maximum concurrency for 1,048,576 tokens per request: 2.44x` |

Workload: cache-busted real prose (rotating public-domain corpus, unique cache-bust id per request, needle
at mid-depth), `thinking_mode: disabled`, temperature 0, per-token client timestamps, 900s client timeout,
3 reps per cell unless labeled. All statistics are computed per rep and combined as a median over the 3
reps (p50 = median); ratios and deltas are computed from cell medians; the envelope table's TTFT
min/p50/max columns pool requests within a cell. Decode measurements use decode-window arithmetic
((last-token time - first-token time) / (tokens - 1)) with 512 forced completion tokens
(`min_tokens=max_tokens=512`, `finish_reason=length` on every request); streaming inter-arrival TPOT is not
used anywhere because both engines batch SSE events (the EAGLE3 leg delivers 512 tokens in 117-193 events).

## Context ladder, c=1 (TTFT p50 of 3 reps; needle recovered 15/15, 5 rungs x 3 reps)

| Input tokens | TTFT p50 |
| --- | --- |
| ~128K | 2.63s |
| ~256K | 6.09s |
| ~512K | 15.49s |
| ~768K | 27.91s |
| ~1.01M | 43.24s |

## Concurrency envelope (max_tokens=64, 3 reps per cell, all 144 requests ok across the 9 cells, needles 144/144)

| Context | c | Makespan p50 | TTFT min/p50/max | Aggregate input tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 128K | 8 | 19.0s | 2.7 / 10.9 / 19.0s | ~54.0K |
| 128K | 16 | 37.6s | 2.7 / 20.1 / 37.6s | ~54.3K |
| 256K | 4 | 22.3s | 6.2 / 14.3 / 22.2s | ~46.0K |
| 256K | 8 | 43.9s | 6.2 / 25.0 / 43.9s | ~46.6K |
| 512K | 2 | 29.6s | 15.5 / 22.6 / 29.7s | ~34.8K |
| 512K | 4 | 57.8s | 15.5 / 36.7 / 57.8s | ~35.6K |
| 1M | 1 | 43.2s | 43.2 / 43.2 / 43.4s | ~23.4K |
| 1M | 2 | 83.3s | 43.3 / 63.5 / 83.7s | ~24.3K |
| 1M | 3 | 123.6s | 43.4 / 83.5 / 123.7s | ~24.5K |

The 1M c=2/c=3 rows are the admission-behavior probe: `num_requests_running` is 1 in 359 of 378 sampled
2-second ticks across the c=1..3 reps, with exactly one tick at 2 (during the c=3 second rep, the moment
one request leaves prefill and the next is admitted); the waiting gauge steps 0/1/2 as instantaneous
readings, and makespan scales near-linearly (1.93x, 2.86x, slightly under perfect seriality, consistent
with that brief handoff overlap). Total prefill throughput is roughly flat (23.4K at c=1 to 24.5K at c=3
tok/s). Admitting one full 1M prefill at a time is consistent with the default partial-prefill caps under
chunked prefill; the result is that the 2.44x KV line does not translate into usable concurrency: requests
wait their turn, with no tail collapse and no error.

## EAGLE3 speculative decoding (c=1, 512/512 tokens, decode-window medians of 3 reps unless labeled)

Draft: `Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3`, 3 speculative tokens, `--language-model-only`, parsers dropped.

| Context | Base TPOT | EAGLE3 TPOT | Decode gain | TTFT delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8K | 4.02 ms | 1.95 ms (n=2) | 2.06x (n=2) | +21% (+0.04s; n=2, first-request warmup rep excluded) |
| 128K | 4.19 ms | 1.82 ms | 2.30x | +4.6% |
| 1M | 5.45 ms | 2.44 ms | 2.23x | +5.5% |

Acceptance over the run: 3,077 accepted / 1,530 draft passes = 2.01 accepted tokens per draft (ratio of
totals); per-position rates 0.842 / 0.678 / 0.490 are marginal, and they sum to the same 2.01. Mean
acceptance length by the vLLM convention is 3.01. The gain holds at 1M; the lower 8K gain (2.06x) reflects
relatively higher draft-step overhead at short context. KV asymmetry disclosed: the EAGLE3 configuration
reports 2,727,296 KV tokens (2.60x) vs the base recipe's 2,558,976 (2.44x) because `--language-model-only`
starts the engine in text-only mode, freeing the vision tower and its memory reservation; all cells here
are c=1 so the extra capacity does not affect the measurements.

## MSA scaling claim, checked in the runnable zone

MiniMax's launch materials claim 9x prefill / 15x decode vs M2 at 1M context. We hold same-node,
same-protocol M2.7-NVFP4 data (`nvidia/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4`, TP8, same image family). Two scope facts first:
the engine-reported M2.7 ceiling is 196,608 tokens, not the marketed 200K+ (a 200,000-token request returns
HTTP 400), and M2 itself is not runnable on this hardware. So the direct comparison zone ends at 192K:

| Context | M3 TTFT / TPOT | M2.7 TTFT / TPOT | M3 prefill | M3 decode |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8K | 0.17s / 4.02 ms | 0.10s / 4.18 ms | 0.6x (slower) | ~parity |
| 64K | 1.32s / 4.13 ms | 1.01s / 5.05 ms | 1.30x slower | 1.22x faster |
| 128K | 2.65s / 4.19 ms | 2.60s / 5.13 ms | ~parity | 1.22x faster |
| 192K | 4.29s / 4.29 ms | 4.90s / 5.28 ms | 1.14x faster | 1.23x faster |

Within the runnable zone, M3's sparse attention buys roughly nothing at small context, reaches prefill
parity near 150K, and pulls ahead by low double digits at the M2.7 ceiling, with a steady decode advantage
that is essentially flat (1.22x at 64K, 1.23x at 192K). The 9x/15x claim concerns the 1M regime where no
M2-family comparator accepts requests; our M3-only curve beyond the ceiling (43.2s TTFT and 5.45 ms TPOT
at 1M) is consistent with sparse attention keeping 1M viable, but we cannot confirm or refute the specific
multipliers.

## Asks

1. **Recipes page** (vllm-project/recipes; we can PR this directly): the M3-NVFP4 B200 recipe's validation
   note predates #48929. Should the page re-validate on a post-fix build and state a minimum build date?
   We are happy to contribute the post-fix numbers above, plus the quack-kernels pin note while it is
   still live.
2. **1M admission behavior** (vllm/vllm): is one-at-a-time admission for full-context sequences under
   chunked prefill the intended behavior when the KV line reports 2.44x? Our serve command passes no
   scheduler overrides, so the observed serialization matches the default partial-prefill admission caps;
   `max_num_batched_tokens=8192` is the printed default. If this is intended, a docs note would help
   capacity planners read the startup line correctly; if not, we have full metrics samples to share.
3. **EAGLE3 as the recommended pairing** (vllm-project/recipes): given 2.1-2.3x decode-window gain at +5%
   TTFT and the KV asymmetry favoring the EAGLE3 config, should the recipe present it as the default
   rather than an option? Launch command and engine log excerpt are attached (b); acceptance counters are
   in the EAGLE3 section above.

Attached: (a) base recipe startup log excerpt through the KV capacity line, (b) EAGLE3 startup log excerpt
(launch command + KV capacity line), (c) the envelope client script used for every measurement. Full
per-request JSONL (per-token timestamps, metrics samples) is retained and available on request.

<details>
<summary>Attachment (a): base recipe startup log excerpt</summary>

```text
# Attachment (a): MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 base recipe startup log excerpt
# Engine: vllm 0.26.1rc1.dev457+gc810e5ee9 (pinned nightly, contains #48929 + #49149; predates #51418; quack-kernels<0.6.3 pin applied)
# 8x NVIDIA B200, TP8, --block-size 128. Key boot lines through the KV capacity print:

(APIServer pid=1) INFO 08-07 22:55:56 [api_utils.py:273] non-default args: {'model_tag': 'nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4', 'enable_auto_tool_choice': True, 'tool_call_parser': 'minimax_m3', 'model': 'nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4', 'trust_remote_code': True, 'served_model_name': ['MiniMax-M3'], 'reasoning_parser': 'minimax_m3', 'tensor_parallel_size': 8, 'block_size': 128}
(APIServer pid=1) INFO 08-07 22:56:22 [scheduler.py:242] Chunked prefill is enabled with max_num_batched_tokens=8192.
(Worker_TP0 pid=1021) INFO 08-07 22:58:35 [gpu_worker.py:564] Available KV cache memory: 107.99 GiB
(EngineCore pid=792) INFO 08-07 22:58:35 [kv_cache_utils.py:1882] GPU KV cache size: 2,558,976 tokens, Maximum concurrency for 1,048,576 tokens per request: 2.44x

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Concurrency envelope client for MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 on 8x B200 (cache-busted real-prose cells, c>1).

Per cell (size, c): fire c concurrent streaming requests (threads), 3 reps.
Per request: unique cache_bust_id + rotated corpus, needle at ~50% depth,
max_tokens=64 (default; 512/512 for the spec-decode comparison via flags), thinking disabled,
per-token time.monotonic() capture; client timeout 900s (disclosed).
Also samples server /metrics during each rep (2s cadence) for
num_requests_running/waiting evidence on admission-boundary cells.
Emits one JSONL record per request + cell summaries + SUMMARY record.
Cells:
  TTFT_s, TTLT_s, wall_s; decode-window tps = (completion-1)/(TTLT-TTFT)
  cell makespan = max(request wall); min/p50 TTFT aggregated in summary.
"""
import argparse, json, pathlib, statistics, threading, time, urllib.request, uuid

CORPUS = None
NEEDLE = "the password is `lampshade-47`"
NEEDLE_SENT = f"By order of the secretary {NEEDLE} and must be remembered."
METRIC_LINES = ("vllm:num_requests_running", "vllm:num_requests_waiting")


def build_prompt(target_tokens, rep, size_idx, req_idx, cpt, base_url=None, model=None):
    bust = f"[cache_bust_id: {uuid.uuid4()}] The following is an excerpt collection from the Federalist Papers (real prose). Read it carefully.\n"
    q = f"\nQuestion: Quote exactly the password mentioned in the passage. Reply with only the password."
    target_chars = int(target_tokens * cpt)
    copies = -(-target_chars // len(CORPUS))
    parts = []
    for k in range(copies):
        rotate = ((rep * 7919 + size_idx * 104729 + req_idx * 12991 + k * 524287) % len(CORPUS))
        parts.append(f"\n[continued, part {k+1}; passage continues from a different section, still real Federalist prose]\n" + CORPUS[rotate:] + CORPUS[:rotate])
    rot = "".join(parts)
    def assemble(chars):
        body_chars = chars - len(bust) - len(q)
        half = (body_chars - len(NEEDLE_SENT)) // 2
        passage = rot[:half] + "\n" + NEEDLE_SENT + "\n" + rot[half:half + (body_chars - len(NEEDLE_SENT) - 2)]
        return bust + "<passage>\n" + passage + "\n</passage>" + q
    prompt = assemble(target_chars)
    if base_url:
        chars = target_chars
        n = tokenize(base_url, prompt, model)
        for _ in range(3):
            if abs(n - target_tokens) / target_tokens <= 0.02:
                break
            chars = int(chars * target_tokens / n)
            prompt = assemble(chars)
            n = tokenize(base_url, prompt, model)
        needle_frac = prompt.find(NEEDLE_SENT) / len(prompt)
        return prompt, n, needle_frac
    return prompt, None, None


def tokenize(base_url, text, model):
    req = urllib.request.Request(base_url.replace("/v1", "") + "/tokenize",
                                 data=json.dumps({"model": model, "prompt": text}).encode(),
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    d = json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=300).read())
    return len(d.get("tokens", d.get("count", [])))


def stream_chat(base_url, model, prompt, max_tokens, min_tokens, timeout):
    body = {"model": model, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
            "max_tokens": max_tokens, "min_tokens": min_tokens, "temperature": 0,
            "chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking_mode": "disabled"}, "stream": True}
    req = urllib.request.Request(base_url + "/chat/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    rec = {}
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    rec["t_submit_rel"] = t0 - CELL_T0
    chunks, content, usage, fin = [], "", None, None
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as r:
            for line in r:
                t = time.monotonic()
                if not line.startswith(b"data: "): continue
                payload = line[6:].strip()
                if payload == b"[DONE]": break
                d = json.loads(payload)
                if d.get("usage"): usage = d["usage"]
                ch = (d.get("choices") or [{}])[0]
                if ch.get("finish_reason"): fin = ch["finish_reason"]
                delta = (ch.get("delta") or {}).get("content")
                if delta:
                    chunks.append((t - t0, len(delta)))
                    content += delta
    except Exception as e:
        rec["error"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
    rec["TTFT_s"] = chunks[0][0] if chunks else None
    rec["TTLT_s"] = chunks[-1][0] if chunks else None
    rec["wall_s"] = time.monotonic() - t0
    ctok = (usage or {}).get("completion_tokens") or len(chunks)
    rec["completion_tokens"] = ctok
    rec["finish_reason"] = fin
    rec["out_tps_decode_window"] = (ctok - 1) / (rec["TTLT_s"] - rec["TTFT_s"]) if (ctok and rec["TTFT_s"] and rec["TTLT_s"] and rec["TTLT_s"] > rec["TTFT_s"]) else None
    rec["needle_recovered"] = "lampshade-47" in content
    rec["chunks"] = chunks
    return rec


def sample_metrics(base_url, stop_event, sink, interval=2.0):
    url = base_url.replace("/v1", "") + "/metrics"
    while not stop_event.is_set():
        t = time.monotonic() - CELL_T0
        try:
            txt = urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=10).read().decode()
            snap = {}
            for key in METRIC_LINES:
                for ln in txt.splitlines():
                    if ln.startswith(key + "{"):
                        snap[key + ln[len(key):].split("}")[0] + "}"] = float(ln.rsplit(" ", 1)[1])
                    elif ln.startswith(key + " "):
                        snap[key] = float(ln.rsplit(" ", 1)[1])
            sink.append((t, snap))
        except Exception as e:
            sink.append((t, {"error": str(e)}))
        stop_event.wait(interval)


def run_rep(base_url, model, c, prompts_info, max_tokens, min_tokens, timeout):
    global CELL_T0
    CELL_T0 = time.monotonic()
    records, metrics = [], []
    stop = threading.Event()
    sampler = threading.Thread(target=sample_metrics, args=(base_url, stop, metrics), daemon=True)
    sampler.start()
    def worker(i, pi):
        r = stream_chat(base_url, model, pi[0], max_tokens, min_tokens, timeout)
        r.update({"req_idx": i, "prompt_tokens": pi[1], "needle_depth_frac": pi[2]})
        records.append(r)
    threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(i, pi)) for i, pi in enumerate(prompts_info)]
    for th in threads: th.start()
    for th in threads: th.join()
    stop.set(); sampler.join()
    return records, metrics


def main():
    global CORPUS, CELL_T0
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--base-url", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--cells", default="128000:8,128000:16,256000:4,256000:8,512000:2,512000:4,1000000:1,1000000:2,1000000:3")
    ap.add_argument("--reps", type=int, default=3)
    ap.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=64)
    ap.add_argument("--min-tokens", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--client-timeout", type=int, default=900)
    ap.add_argument("--corpus", default="federalist-full.txt")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--label", default="envelope-recipe1")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    CORPUS = pathlib.Path(args.corpus).read_text()
    cells = [(int(p.split(":")[0]), int(p.split(":")[1])) for p in args.cells.split(",")]
    out = pathlib.Path(args.out); out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    CELL_T0 = time.monotonic()
    ref = tokenize(args.base_url, CORPUS[:100000], args.model)
    cpt = 100000.0 / ref
    with out.open("w") as f:
        summary = {}
        for si, (size, c) in enumerate(cells):
            key = f"{size}k_c{c}"
            cell_recs = []
            for rep in range(args.reps):
                pis = [build_prompt(size, rep, si, i, cpt, args.base_url, args.model) for i in range(c)]
                records, metrics = run_rep(args.base_url, args.model, c, pis, args.max_tokens, args.min_tokens, args.client_timeout)
                for r in records:
                    r.update({"cell": key, "rep_label": f"n={rep+1}", "size_target": size, "concurrency": c,
                              "thinking_mode": "disabled", "max_tokens": args.max_tokens, "min_tokens": args.min_tokens,
                              "client_timeout_s": args.client_timeout, "leg": args.label,
                              "corpus": "federalist real prose, rotated per rep+request, unique cache_bust_id"})
                    f.write(json.dumps(r) + "\n")
                f.write(json.dumps({"METRICS_SNAP": key, "rep": rep + 1, "samples": metrics}) + "\n")
                f.flush()
                makespan = max((r["wall_s"] or 0) for r in records)
                needles = sum(1 for r in records if r["needle_recovered"])
                cell_recs.extend(records)
                ttfts = sorted(r["TTFT_s"] for r in records if r["TTFT_s"])
                def _f(x):
                    return f"{x:.2f}" if x is not None else "None"
                print(f"cell {key} rep {rep+1}/{args.reps}: c={c} makespan={makespan:.1f}s minTTFT={_f(ttfts[0] if ttfts else None)} p50TTFT={_f(statistics.median(ttfts) if ttfts else None)} needles={needles}/{c}", flush=True)
            ttfts = [r["TTFT_s"] for r in cell_recs if r["TTFT_s"]]
            makespans = [max([rec["wall_s"] for rec in cell_recs if rec["rep_label"] == r["rep_label"]]) for r in cell_recs[:1]]
            alltt = sorted(ttfts)
            summary[key] = {"size": size, "c": c, "n_recs": len(ttfts),
                            "min_TTFT": alltt[0] if alltt else None,
                            "p50_TTFT": statistics.median(alltt) if alltt else None,
                            "p95_TTFT": alltt[int(0.95*(len(alltt)-1))] if alltt else None,
                            "max_TTFT": alltt[-1] if alltt else None}
            f.write(json.dumps({"CELL_SUMMARY": summary[key]}) + "\n"); f.flush()
        f.write(json.dumps({"SUMMARY": summary}) + "\n")
    print("ENVELOPE_COMPLETE")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

candidates.title: [Bug]: kernel_warmup() has no inter-rank synchronization between stages that issue real TP/EP collectives, causing startup hangs on multi-node deployments
candidates.body:
## Summary

`kernel_warmup()` (`vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py`) runs a sequence of ~10 warmup stages, several of which internally call `runner._dummy_run(...)` and thereby issue real cross-rank TP/EP collectives (all-reduce, all-gather, etc.) against the model. There is no inter-rank synchronization between these stage calls. If one rank finishes a stage and moves on to the next (which issues a *different* collective sequence) before its peer has finished the earlier stage, the ranks can permanently desync — once two ranks disagree on the sequence/count of collective calls they've issued, they can never rendezvous again, so every subsequent step (including real inference later) blocks forever instead of erroring.

This is distinct from — but can compound with — live-JIT-during-inference hangs (e.g. #45198, #43009): it's a startup-time ordering bug, not a compilation bug, and can happen even when every kernel is already warmed.

## Why I believe this is real, not just theoretical

`flashinfer_autotune()`, defined in the same file just below `kernel_warmup()`, already guards against exactly this: it explicitly calls `get_world_group().barrier()` after its own `runner._dummy_run(...)` calls (kernel_warmup.py:266 and :311) specifically because tuning is distributed and needs rank sync. That shows the failure mode is already known and handled *for that one function* — but the barrier isn't applied anywhere else in `kernel_warmup()`'s outer sequence. None of `warm_v1_block_table_kernels`, `deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup`, `sparse_mla_triton_warmup_if_needed`, `flashinfer_sparse_mla_decode_autotune_warmup`, `deepseek_v4_sparse_mla_attention_warmup`, `deep_gemm_warmup`, `minimax_m3_msa_warmup`, or the FlashInfer-attention `_dummy_run` near the end of `kernel_warmup()` (kernel_warmup.py:197-203) have any synchronization around them or between them, despite several issuing real collectives via `_dummy_run`.

## Reproduction (indirect, but concrete)

On a 2-node TP=2 DGX Spark (GB10) cluster serving DeepSeek-V4-Flash, we added a custom warmup stage (a long-context decode sweep, inserted into the `kernel_warmup()` sequence) to close an unrelated live-JIT gap. Our new stage issues real TP collectives via `_dummy_run`, so we wrapped it in `get_world_group().barrier()` before and after, expecting that to be sufficient.

It wasn't: the engine still hung at startup with the classic desync signature (`shm_broadcast: No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds` repeating every 60s, then `EngineCore` fatal `TimeoutError: RPC call to sample_tokens timed out`) — but this time at a **different, pre-existing stage boundary** elsewhere in the stock `kernel_warmup()` sequence that we hadn't touched. In other words: barriering only our own addition wasn't enough, because the *next* unbarriered boundary in the stock pipeline was just as capable of desyncing the ranks. This strongly suggests the gap is systemic to the whole sequence, not isolated to any one stage.

We didn't get a clean single-stage minimal repro of the *stock* pipeline in isolation (our reproduction is entangled with our own added stage), so I'm filing this as a code-inspection-supported report rather than a guaranteed one-line repro. Happy to try to isolate a cleaner stock-only repro if that would help triage.

## Why it's more likely to bite on some setups than others

Anything that increases per-rank timing variance around a stage boundary makes this more likely to manifest: e.g. cross-node topologies where NCCL falls back to a host-staged/CPU-mediated transport (as on hardware without GPUDirect RDMA) are more sensitive to one rank's host thread being briefly slower than a GPU-driven transport would be. But the underlying bug — no synchronization between stages that issue real collectives — is hardware-independent, and could plausibly affect any multi-node TP/EP deployment given enough timing skew (disk cache state, first-time codepath differences between ranks, etc.), not just DGX Spark.

## Proposed fix

Apply the same pattern `flashinfer_autotune()` already uses to the rest of `kernel_warmup()`'s stage sequence — either a `get_world_group().barrier()` between every stage that can issue real collectives, or (cheaper, less precise) one barrier at the very end of `kernel_warmup()` before returning. This is startup-time-only overhead, so the cost of over-barriering is small relative to the cost of a silent, permanent production hang.

## Environment

- vLLM v0.26.0, 2× NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark), TP=2 across nodes, `--enable-expert-parallel`, Ray executor backend, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`.
- Related, same hardware class: #46253 (a separate CUDA-graph-replay desync, same `shm_broadcast` signature, different mechanism — that one's about graph capture/replay, this one's about warmup-stage ordering).

The same model/config/hardware works on **vLLM 0.26.0 + torch 2.12** wheels (which bundle oneCCL 2021.17.2). isolated this below vLLM: it is an **oneCCL 2022.x regression**, reproduced with a 15-line pure `torch.distributed` (`xccl`) script — full analysis, minimal reproducer, and per-size matrix in https://github.com/uxlfoundation/oneCCL/issues/215 - oneCCL **2021.17.2** (torch 2.12 wheels): all allreduce sizes pass at full speed. - oneCCL **2022.0.0 / 2022.1.1** (torch 2.13 wheels): messages **≤16 MiB pass at parity**, messages **≥20 MiB hang the GPUs** (cliff at `CCL_SYCL_ALLREDUCE_MEDIUM_THRESHOLD`). vLLM's default warmup dummies `max_num_batched_tokens=8192` tokens → 8192×3584×2 B ≈ **56 MiB** allreduce → hang, before serving a single request. - Downgrading is blocked by an ABI wall: `oneccl==2021.17.2` needs `libsycl.so.8`, torch 2.13 links `libsycl.so.9`. - `CCL_ALLREDUCE=ring` avoids the hang but is ~4–7× slower on the collective — ~30% end-to-end decode regression (~21–22 vs ~31–32 tok/s, TP=4). The ≤16 MiB message-size workaround (`--max-num-batched-tokens 2048`, i.e. ≤14 MiB for hidden 3584) should keep warmup on the healthy path but is an awful bandaid solution. ### Environment | Item | Value | |---|---| | GPUs | 8× Intel Arc Pro B60 24 GB (`8086:e211`), PCIe-only, P2P via `pci=disable_acs_redir=`, `amd_iommu=off` | | Board / CPU | ASRock X870 Pro-A WiFi (AM5), Ryzen 9 9900X | | OS / kernel | Ubuntu 26.04, `7.1.3-070103-generic`, xe driver | | Level Zero | `libze-intel-gpu1 26.27.39122.11-0`, `libze1 1.32.0` | | Broken stack | vLLM main, torch 2.13, `intel-sycl-rt 2026.0.0/2026.1.1`, `oneccl 2022.0.0/2022.1.1`, vllm-xpu-kernels 0.12.0 | | Working stack | vLLM 0.26.0, torch 2.12, `intel-sycl-rt 2025.3.2`, `oneccl 2021.17.2`, vllm-xpu-kernels 0.11.1 | | Model | Gemma-4 31B multimodal (`gemma4_mm`), fp8 and bf16 | ### Repro ```bash vllm serve --tensor-parallel-size 4 # hangs at warmup/profile_run # also with: --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 (multimodal: still hangs) # works, ~30% slower: CCL_ALLREDUCE=ring vllm serve ... ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

candidates.title: [Performance]: Qwen3-Omni MoE decode 3-6x slower on RTX 5090 (sm_120) — no fused-MoE tuned configs for GeForce Blackwell
candidates.body:
### Proposal to improve performance

MoE decode on GeForce Blackwell (RTX 5090, sm_120) runs with default fused-MoE configs and is 3-6x slower than it should be. Requesting tuned configs for RTX 5090 (bf16 and fp8_w8a8 block at minimum) — we are happy to contribute ours.

### Report of performance regression

**Setup**: 8x RTX 5090 32GB, driver 570.124, vLLM 0.11.2 (cu12x wheels), Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B (fine-tuned, thinker-only, bf16), TP=4, online serving (`vllm serve`), video caption workload (~50-token text prompt + 10s 720x1280 video, max_tokens=128, concurrency 16).

At startup vLLM warns:

```
Using default MoE config. Performance might be sub-optimal! Config file not found at ...
```

Measured against sglang 0.5.15 on the same hardware, same model, same TP layout, same requests:

| Metric (c16, 32 reqs) | vLLM 0.11.2 | sglang 0.5.15 |
|---|---|---|
| Request throughput | 0.41 req/s | 0.74 req/s |
| Mean ITL (decode) | **178.8 ms** | 27-52 ms |
| Median TTFT | 11.6 s | ~10 s |

Prefill/TTFT is roughly comparable; the gap is almost entirely MoE decode ITL, consistent with the missing tuned config (Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B: 128 experts, moe_intermediate_size=768).

Related: #24968 added NVFP4 MoE for sm_120; #36095 (closed) requested int4_w4a16 configs for RTX 5090. As far as we can tell the only Blackwell tuned config in-tree today is RTX PRO 6000 fp8_w8a8 — consumer Blackwell (5090/5080) has none for any dtype.

**Suggestions, in increasing order of effort:**

1. Accept community-contributed `...device_name=NVIDIA_GeForce_RTX_5090.json` tuned configs. We can run `benchmark_moe.py` and contribute bf16 and fp8_w8a8 (128x128 block) configs for the E=128/N=768 shape family if maintainers are open to it.
2. When no tuned config matches, consider a lightweight first-run auto-tune with on-disk caching instead of silently using defaults — the current warning is easy to miss and the penalty (3-6x ITL) is much larger than users expect.
3. The sm_120 fused-MoE kernel itself may be worth a profiling pass beyond tile configs; 178 ms mean ITL for a 3B-active MoE seems too high to be tile parameters alone.

**Additional context on why we tested 0.11.2 rather than latest**: driver 570 is the CUDA 12.x ceiling and GeForce has no forward-compatibility package channel, so cu130-only wheels (0.12+) are not installable on these hosts. Consumer Blackwell users are widely on 5xx drivers; keeping a cu12x wheel variant alive for a while (or a documented main + cu129-torch source build path) would make this hardware testable on recent releases.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

Output of python -m vllm.collect_env (run inside the affected H20 container) ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 11.4.0 Libc version : glibc-2.35 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.11.0+cu130 CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.13 Python platform : Linux-4.18.0-372.32.1.90.po1.x86_64-x86_64-with-glibc2.35 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 13.0.88 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA H20-3e (Hopper, sm_90) Nvidia driver version : 580.105.08 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.6.12 [pip3] numpy==2.2.6 [pip3] torch==2.11.0+cu130 [pip3] torchvision==0.26.0+cu130 [pip3] transformers==5.12.0 [pip3] triton==3.6.0 vLLM Version : 0.23.0 ``` Also reproduced on vLLM **0.24.0** and **0.25.0** — `vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_expand_op.py` and `kernel_utils.py` are byte-identical across 0.23/0.24/0.25, so upgrading does not fix it.
--- # === 🐛 Describe the bug === ## Summary On **NVIDIA Hopper (sm_90, e.g. H20/H100)**, serving a Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct LoRA adapter with vLLM produces **completely garbled output** (e.g. repeated `!!!!!!`, or incoherent mixed-language/code-like tokens). The **base model without LoRA is perfectly fine**. I traced this to the LoRA **`lora_expand`** Triton kernel producing **NaN**. `lora_shrink` is fine. The trigger is the default expand kernel config **`block_n = 128`** (single-slice path); forcing **`block_n = 32`** makes the kernel numerically correct and the garbling disappears. It is **architecture-specific**: the exact same adapter runs correctly on **Blackwell (RTX 5070, sm_120)** and via **HF Transformers + PEFT** on the same GPU-family — only the vLLM Triton expand kernel on sm_90 is wrong. ## Transformers vs vLLM (per the issue template) I ran the **same adapter** through plain **HF Transformers + PEFT** (`PeftModel.from_pretrained`) — output is **correct**. Only vLLM garbles. So this is a vLLM (Triton kernel) issue, not a modeling/transformers issue. ## What I ruled out (each tested, not guessed) - vLLM version: 0.23.0 / 0.24.0 / 0.25.0 all reproduce (kernel code identical). - `--enforce-eager` on/off: both reproduce. - Attention backend: FlashAttn v2 / v3 / `TORCH_SDPA` all reproduce. - Sampler backend: flashinfer sampler on/off, both reproduce. - Quantization: bf16 / fp8 / bitsandbytes-4bit all reproduce. - Virtualization: reproduced on **bare-metal H20** (no HAMi/vGPU). - Stale `~/.triton/cache`: wiping it does **not** help; NaN reproduces on a fresh compile. ## Minimal, model-free reproduction This calls only the LoRA Triton ops with synthetic tensors and compares against the torch reference (`vllm/lora/ops/torch_ops`): ```python import torch from vllm.lora.ops.triton_ops import lora_expand, LoRAKernelMeta from vllm.lora.ops.torch_ops import bgmv_expand dev = "cuda" T, H, R, scaling = 1029, 4096, 64, 2.0 # num_tokens, hidden, rank, alpha/r for dtype in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16): x = torch.randn(1, T, R, device=dev, dtype=dtype) # shrink output [slices, tokens, rank] B = (torch.randn(1, H, R, device=dev) * 0.02).to(dtype) # lora_b [num_loras, hidden, rank] out = torch.zeros(T, H, device=dev, dtype=dtype) tlm = torch.zeros(T, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev) # all tokens -> lora 0 meta = LoRAKernelMeta.make(max_loras=1, max_num_tokens=T, device=dev) meta.prepare_tensors(tlm) lora_expand(x, [B], out, *meta.meta_args(T, False), offset_start=0, add_inputs=True) ref = torch.zeros(T, H, device=dev, dtype=dtype) bgmv_expand(x[0], B, ref, torch.zeros(T, dtype=torch.long, device=dev), add_inputs=True) print(dtype, "| lora_expand(triton) NaNs:", torch.isnan(out).sum().item(), "| bgmv_expand(torch) NaNs:", torch.isnan(ref).sum().item()) ``` Observed on H20 (sm_90): ```text torch.bfloat16 | lora_expand(triton) NaNs: 4480 | bgmv_expand(torch) NaNs: 0 torch.float16 | lora_expand(triton) NaNs: 36352 | bgmv_expand(torch) NaNs: 0 ``` Only a subset of output elements are NaN (looks like a boundary N-tile), then it propagates through the forward pass → garbled decode. ## The trigger: `block_n = 128` In `vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/utils.py`, the default single-slice expand config is: ```python "block_n": 64 if num_slices > 1 else 128, ``` Changing `128` → `32` yields **0 NaN** and matches the torch reference (max abs diff ~1e-3, normal bf16 rounding). So the fault is specific to the **`block_n=128` tile on sm_90** — pointing at a Triton codegen / memory-access bug at that tile size (possible out-of-bounds read on the boundary N-tile, or an MMA/shared-memory layout issue for a 128-wide tile on Hopper). Compare with #47303 (Triton MoE kernels producing NaN due to OOB reads) — similar flavor. ## Impact / fix verified With either workaround, garbling disappears and downstream task accuracy is restored (0.63 base → ~0.90 LoRA, matching the Transformers+PEFT reference): 1. Set single-slice expand `block_n = 32` in `utils.py` (keeps native Triton, negligible perf hit, CUDA-graph safe). **Recommended.** 2. Fall back to a torch `lora_expand` on sm_90 (correct but slower; must be written CUDA-graph-safe or capture fails with `operation not permitted when stream is capturing`). ## Ask - Is `block_n=128` for the expand kernel expected to be valid on sm_90? The NaN strongly suggests a tiling/masking/codegen bug at that config on Hopper. - Could the default expand config avoid `block_n=128` on sm_90, or the boundary-tile masking be fixed? Happy to provide full serve logs and the instrumentation details.

  call times out because shared memory broadcast blocks are unavailable — workers are unresponsive.
                                                                                                                
  Environment                                                                                                   
  
  - vLLM version: v0.1.dev15830+g8d599d76a                                                                      
  - Python version: 3.12                                          
  - CUDA version: 13.0 (driver), NCCL 2.28.9                                                                    
  - OS: Linux                                                                                                   
  - GPU: 8x NVIDIA GPU (Tensor Parallel=8)                                                                      
  - Model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro/                                                                         
  - Speculative decoding: MTP (method='mtp', num_speculative_tokens=1)                                          
  - Quantization: deepseek_v4_fp8                                                                               
  - KV cache dtype: fp8                                                                                         
  - Tokenizer mode: deepseek_v4                                                                                 
  - max_seq_len: 800,000

  - enable_expert_parallel: True                                                                                
  - CUDAGraph mode: FULL_DECODE_ONLY                                                                            
                                                                                                                
  Reproduction                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                
  The issue occurs intermittently during normal inference serving. The engine runs fine for a period (hours),

      engine_core.run_busy_loop()                                 
    File "vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 1144, in run_busy_loop

    File "vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 397, in get_response                                    
      raise TimeoutError(f"RPC call to {method} timed out.") from e                                             
  TimeoutError: RPC call to sample_tokens timed out.                                                            
                                                                                                                
  Scheduler Stats at Crash Time                                                                                 
                                                                                                                
  num_running_reqs=1, num_waiting_reqs=0                                                                        
  kv_cache_usage=0.44%                                                                                          
  prefix_cache_stats: queries=11645, hits=11264 (hit rate ~96.7%)                                               
                                                                                                                
  Additional Context                                                                                            
                                                                                                                
  - The server was serving traffic normally before the hang. GPU KV cache usage was consistently low (0-3.5%),

candidates.title: [Feature]: Add Rotorquant support
candidates.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

**RotorQuant** is a Clifford algebra-based reimagining of TurboQuant (ICLR 2026) for KV cache compression. It replaces the dense d×d random orthogonal rotation matrix used in TurboQuant with lightweight Clifford rotors from Cl(3,0), achieving **10–19× faster** quantization on NVIDIA GPUs, **9–31× faster** on Apple Silicon, and using **44× fewer parameters** — all while matching TurboQuant's attention fidelity on real models.

- **Paper/Report:** https://www.scrya.com/rotorquant/
- **Code:** https://github.com/scrya-com/rotorquant
- **Related issue:** #38171 (TurboQuant support request)

### Why this matters for vLLM

KV cache memory is the primary bottleneck for long-context serving. At 8K tokens on Qwen2.5-3B (36 layers), the KV cache is ~289 MB in FP16. RotorQuant compresses this to ~58 MB at 3-bit (5× compression) with 99.0% attention cosine similarity — comparable to TurboQuant (99.5%) but with dramatically lower computational overhead for the rotation step.

The core advantage for a serving engine like vLLM is the **quantize/dequantize speed**: TurboQuant's rotation requires a 128×128 dense matmul (16,384 FMAs per vector), while RotorQuant's rotor sandwich product uses only ~100 FMAs per vector. This translates directly to lower latency on the KV cache write path.

### How RotorQuant works

1. **Chunk** the d-dimensional KV vector into groups of 3 dimensions (43 groups for d=128).
2. **Embed** each 3D chunk as a Cl(3,0) multivector (8 components).
3. **Apply rotor sandwich product** `RxR̃` per group to decorrelate coordinates. Each rotor has only 4 non-zero components (scalar + 3 bivectors), making the geometric product extremely sparse.
4. **Quantize** each coordinate with grade-aware Lloyd-Max scalar quantization (separate codebooks for scalar vs. bivector grades).
5. **Apply QJL residual correction** (1-bit per dimension) for unbiased inner product estimation, same as TurboQuant Stage 2.

### Benchmarks (from official website)

**CUDA fused kernel speed (RTX PRO 4000, d=128, 3-bit):**

| n_vectors | TurboQuant | RotorQuant CUDA | Speedup |
|-----------|-----------|-----------------|---------|
| 1,024     | 69 μs     | 6 μs            | 11×     |
| 4,096     | 132 μs    | 12 μs           | 11×     |
| 8,192     | 285 μs    | 20 μs           | 14×     |
| 16,384    | 740 μs    | 39 μs           | 19×     |

**Real model validation (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct KV cache):**

| Context | Bits  | Method     | Cosine Sim | Top-1 | Top-5 |
|---------|-------|------------|------------|-------|-------|
| 2K      | 3-bit | TurboQuant | 0.9906     | 81.2% | 93.8% |
| 2K      | 3-bit | RotorQuant | 0.9903     | 81.2% | 93.8% |
| 4K      | 4-bit | TurboQuant | 0.9880     | 75.0% | 93.8% |
| 4K      | 4-bit | RotorQuant | 0.9874     | 81.2% | 93.8% |

RotorQuant matches or exceeds TurboQuant on top-k retrieval accuracy at 4K context, despite slightly lower cosine similarity on synthetic benchmarks. The Clifford rotor decorrelation appears to better preserve directional structure in real attention heads.

**Parameter efficiency:**

| Method     | Params (d=128) | Params (d=4096) |
|------------|----------------|-----------------|
| TurboQuant | 16,399         | ~16.7M          |
| RotorQuant | 372            | ~11K            |

### Alternatives

- **TurboQuant** (#38171): The baseline this improves upon. Higher raw MSE fidelity on synthetic data, but slower rotation step and 44× more parameters. RotorQuant could be added as a drop-in alternative sharing the same QJL and Lloyd-Max infrastructure.

### Additional context

- Pope, J.D. (2026). "RotorQuant: Clifford Algebra Vector Quantization for LLM KV Cache Compression." https://www.scrya.com/rotorquant/
- Zandieh et al. (2026). "TurboQuant: Online Vector Quantization with Near-optimal Distortion Rate." ICLR 2026. arXiv:2504.19874

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

When running DeepSeek-V4-Pro model with vLLM v0.26.0 on multi-node H100 setup with speculative decoding (DSpark) enabled, the engine crashes during inference with a CUDA assertion error in flashmla sparse MLA prefill kernel. The error occurs during TMA (Tensor Memory Accelerator) descriptor initialization, indicating an invalid GPU memory pointer being passed to the kernel.

This issue does NOT occur on v0.25.x with the exact same configuration. The regression was introduced in v0.26.0.

candidates.title: [Performance]: DeepSeek-V3.2 Performance Optimization Tracking

labels.name: unstale
labels.description: Recieved activity after being labelled stale

candidates.body:
## Overview

This issue tracks performance optimization efforts for **DeepSeek-V3.2** (`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp`) inference in vLLM.

## Optimization Areas

### 1. General
- [ ] Indexer overlap (multistream cuda): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35226

### 2. Prefill Perf

- [ ] Support TP without padding — update kernel to support head counts of 16 and remove [padding logic](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/b9793e6a8c30bc42f35d2a1eac919284aea27f76/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py#L928-L938)
- [ ] Support PCP
- [x] Optimize top-k
- [x] Optimize concat: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/34917
- [x] Gather and upconvert: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35290


#### FP8 KV-Cache Specific

- [X] Use sparse prefill kernel, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/27532
- [ ] Use prefill kernels for TP (once kernels support it) — [remove mixed batch mode fallback](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/b9793e6a8c30bc42f35d2a1eac919284aea27f76/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py#L46-L56)

### 3. Short-Context Prefill Perf

**Issue**: We currently use the absorbed approach (data-movement friendly MQA) for prefill instead of the un-absorbed approach (compute-friendly MHA), which is suboptimal for short-context prefill. The absorbed pathway requires ~3.36x more FLOPs than the un-absorbed approach (see [PR #551: feat: support MLA decode](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/FlashMLA/pull/551)).

- [ ] Use un-absorbed dense MHA pathway for requests with `seqlen <= topk`
- [ ] Use un-absorbed masked MHA pathway for requests with `seqlen <= threshold` (where `threshold > topk`) — will require a new masked MHA kernel: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/34744

### 4. Decode Perf

- [ ] Investigate DCP (see if this could actually help)
- [x] Optimize top-k: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/33680 long-context: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/34265
- [ ] Optimize Indexer MTP support (Hopper & Blackwell): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35878

### 5. Tensor Parallel Perf
- [x] FlashInfer Sparse MLA (B200): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/33451

#### BF16 KV-Cache Specific

- [ ] Support TP without padding — update kernel to support head counts of 16 and [remove padding logic](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/b9793e6a8c30bc42f35d2a1eac919284aea27f76/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py#L928-L938)

## Related Issues

- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/31368
